genesis.title: Genesis Sermon Series
genesis.headline: Where Everything That Is Wrong Began, and the Promise That It Would Be Made Right
genesis.bigIdea: Genesis is not a science textbook or a children's story. It is the book that explains why the world is glorious and broken at once, and where the rescue was first promised.
genesis.christConnection: The offspring who crushes the serpent (3:15), the lamb God provides in place of the son (22:8), the curse-bearer who becomes blessing for all nations (12:3), all of it points to Christ.

sermons.title: Made, Not Random
sermons.idea: You are not an accident. You are made, in His image, on purpose.
sermons.verdict: You bear the image you did not earn.

sermons.title: The Day It Broke
sermons.idea: Sin is not breaking a rule. It is the refusal to be a creature.
sermons.verdict: Every wrong began with one grasp.

sermons.title: Judgment and the Ark
sermons.idea: God's judgment and God's mercy meet in one door.
sermons.verdict: There is room in the ark.

sermons.title: The Call of Abram
sermons.idea: God's plan to bless the world runs through one undeserving man.
sermons.verdict: Blessed to be a blessing.

sermons.title: The Mountain and the Lamb
sermons.idea: God provides the sacrifice He requires.
sermons.verdict: God Himself will provide the lamb.

sermons.title: Meant for Good
sermons.idea: What men intend for evil, God weaves for salvation.
sermons.verdict: You meant evil; God meant good.

john.title: John Sermon Series
john.headline: The Signs Were Never the Point. The One They Pointed To Was.
john.bigIdea: John selects seven signs and seven 'I AM' sayings to make one case: Jesus is God in the flesh, and believing Him is life.
john.christConnection: This is the most explicitly Christ-centered book in the canon; the connection is not drawn, it is the text.

sermons.title: The Word Became Flesh
sermons.idea: The infinite God took on a body you could touch.
sermons.verdict: The Word moved into the neighborhood.

sermons.title: Born Again
sermons.idea: You do not need improvement. You need a new birth.
sermons.verdict: You must be born from above.

sermons.title: The Woman at the Well
sermons.idea: Jesus offers living water to the person everyone else avoided.
sermons.verdict: He went where He didn't have to go.

sermons.title: I Am the Resurrection
sermons.idea: Jesus weeps at the grave and then empties it.
sermons.verdict: He wept at the tomb He would open.

sermons.title: The Towel and the Basin
sermons.idea: The Lord of all kneels to wash feet.
sermons.verdict: The throne was a basin.

sermons.title: It Is Finished
sermons.idea: The cross is not a defeat to be reversed but a victory to be announced.
sermons.verdict: Finished, and then He rose.

philippians.title: Philippians Sermon Series
philippians.headline: A Man in Chains Wrote the Happiest Letter in the Bible. Ask Why.
philippians.bigIdea: Paul writes from prison about a joy that circumstances cannot reach because its source is not circumstantial.
philippians.christConnection: The hymn of 2:5–11, Christ's descent and exaltation, is the engine of the whole letter's joy and humility.

sermons.title: To Live Is Christ
sermons.idea: When Christ is your life, even death becomes gain.
sermons.verdict: To live is Christ, to die is gain.

sermons.title: The Mind That Moves Down
sermons.idea: The path to exaltation runs through descent.
sermons.verdict: He humbled Himself.

sermons.title: Counting It Loss
sermons.idea: Everything you'd boast in is rubbish next to knowing Him.
sermons.verdict: Loss, for the surpassing worth.

sermons.title: The Peace That Guards
sermons.idea: Anxiety answered by prayer becomes peace standing guard.
sermons.verdict: Peace will guard your heart.

1-chronicles.title: The God Who Keeps His Word: Preaching Through 1 Chronicles
1-chronicles.headline: A returned and ruined people read their own family record and find a covenant that did not break.
1-chronicles.bigIdea: 1 Chronicles retells Israel's story for a discouraged post-exilic community to prove that God's covenant with David, and the worship He commanded, still stand. The Chronicler does not write nostalgia. He writes assurance that the throne and the temple belong to a faithfulness larger than the nation's failure.
1-chronicles.christConnection: The genealogies narrow toward a king, the covenant promises a son of David whose throne is established forever, and the temple David cannot build but only prepare for points past Solomon to the One in whom God finally dwells with His people. 1 Chronicles is a book pointing at a name it has not yet learned to say.

sermons.title: The List That Is a Sermon
sermons.idea: The nine chapters of names trace humanity from Adam through the chosen line of Judah, Levi, and the returned exiles, declaring that God has kept track of every generation and lost none of His promises across the wreckage of the exile.
sermons.verdict: God forgot none of these names.

sermons.title: The King Who Was Not Asked
sermons.idea: Saul dies on Gilboa because he was unfaithful, did not keep the word of the Lord, and consulted a medium instead of God, so the kingdom is turned over to David, and the throne is set on obedience rather than stature.
sermons.verdict: He sought everything but God.

sermons.title: The Whole Nation Comes to Hebron
sermons.idea: All Israel gathers to anoint David, and the warriors who rally to him at Hebron and Ziklag show that God's appointed king draws a scattered people into one army of glad allegiance under the shepherd He has chosen.
sermons.verdict: They came of one heart.

sermons.title: Bringing the Ark Up Rightly
sermons.idea: David's first attempt to move the ark on a cart ends in Uzzah's death, and only when the Levites carry it as the law commanded does the ark come to Jerusalem with joy, teaching that God must be worshiped on His terms and not our convenience.
sermons.verdict: Sought rightly, not just sincerely.

sermons.title: The House David Wanted to Build
sermons.idea: When David desires to build God a house, God refuses and instead promises to build David a house, an offspring whose throne and kingdom will be established forever, grounding Israel's hope not in what David gives God but in what God gives David.
sermons.verdict: You will not build. I will.

sermons.title: The Wars the King Wins
sermons.idea: David's victories over surrounding nations are recorded as the Lord giving him triumph wherever he went, establishing the kingdom in justice and righteousness so that the promised house rests on a secured and God-given peace.
sermons.verdict: The Lord gave him victory everywhere.

sermons.title: The Census and the Threshing Floor
sermons.idea: David's prideful census brings a plague, but his repentance and refusal to offer what costs him nothing lead him to buy Ornan's threshing floor, the very ground that will become the temple site, where judgment is answered by sacrifice.
sermons.verdict: I will not offer cheap worship.

sermons.title: Preparing a House He Will Not See
sermons.idea: Barred from building because he shed much blood, David spends his last strength gathering materials, organizing priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and officers, and charging Solomon to build, modeling a faith that labors for a glory it will not personally enjoy.
sermons.verdict: He built for a coming generation.

sermons.title: The Charge and the Offering
sermons.idea: David publicly commissions Solomon, gives him the pattern for the temple, leads the people in lavish giving, and prays that all they offer came first from God's own hand, ending the book in worship that confesses the kingdom belongs to the Lord.
sermons.verdict: From your hand we have given.

1-corinthians.title: The Cross in a Divided Church: 1 Corinthians
1-corinthians.headline: A working pastor preaches the letter Paul wrote to a church that had everything but maturity.
1-corinthians.bigIdea: A church gifted with knowledge, eloquence, and spiritual power was tearing itself apart, and Paul answered every fracture the same way: by returning the Corinthians to the cross they were ashamed of, the body they were dividing, and the resurrection that makes their labor matter.
1-corinthians.christConnection: Christ crucified is the wisdom and power of God that empties human boasting, and his bodily resurrection is the firstfruits that guarantees ours. Every quarrel in Corinth was a refusal of one or the other, and Paul refuses to let them keep either at arm's length.

sermons.title: The Foolishness of God
sermons.idea: The Corinthians were splitting into parties around their favorite teachers, and Paul exposes the root: they were measuring the gospel by human eloquence and wisdom when God had chosen a crucified Messiah to shame the strong and empty every boast.
sermons.verdict: The cross ends our boasting.

sermons.title: Infants Fighting Over Servants
sermons.idea: The same people who prided themselves on wisdom were spiritually immature, jealous and quarreling, and Paul tells them the teachers they idolized are only field hands and the church is God's temple, holy ground no faction may claim.
sermons.verdict: You are God's temple, not factions.

sermons.title: Apostles on Display, Last of All
sermons.idea: While the Corinthians played at being already rich and reigning kings, Paul holds up the apostles as the world's refuse, beaten and homeless, to confront a church that had grown arrogant on borrowed gifts and forgotten that the kingdom is power, not talk.
sermons.verdict: Boast in nothing you received as gift.

sermons.title: Leaven, Lawsuits, and the Body You Were Bought to Honor
sermons.idea: A church proud of its tolerance was harboring open sexual sin, dragging brothers before pagan courts, and treating the body as disposable, and Paul calls them to purge the leaven, judge themselves, and glorify God in bodies they no longer own.
sermons.verdict: You were bought; honor God bodily.

sermons.title: Married, Single, and Called Where You Are
sermons.idea: Answering their questions about sex, marriage, divorce, and singleness, Paul refuses both the ascetic who despises marriage and the libertine who despises restraint, teaching that every believer is called to undivided devotion to the Lord in the situation grace found them.
sermons.verdict: Live for the Lord, undivided.

sermons.title: Knowledge Puffs Up, Love Builds Up
sermons.idea: The Corinthians who knew idols were nothing used that knowledge to wound weaker consciences, and Paul answers with his own example, surrendering even an apostle's rights, because love that builds the brother is worth more than a freedom that destroys him.
sermons.verdict: Surrender your rights for love.

sermons.title: Warnings from the Wilderness, Freedom for the Other
sermons.idea: Israel had the cloud, the sea, and the rock and still fell in the desert, and Paul warns the overconfident Corinthians that participation in Christ's table cannot coexist with the table of demons, then bends all liberty toward the glory of God and the good of the neighbor.
sermons.verdict: Whatever you do, seek another's good.

sermons.title: Worship That Honors and a Table That Divides
sermons.idea: In their gatherings the Corinthians dishonored both the order of worship and one another at the Lord's Supper, the rich eating while the poor went hungry, and Paul recalls them to the body and blood they were despising and the body of believers they were shaming.
sermons.verdict: Discern the body at the table.

sermons.title: Many Gifts, One Body
sermons.idea: A church competing over showier gifts is told that the same Spirit distributes every gift for the common good, and that the body cannot say to any member you are unneeded, because God arranged the weaker and less honorable parts as indispensable.
sermons.verdict: The Spirit gifts for one body.

sermons.title: The More Excellent Way
sermons.idea: Set against their hunger for impressive gifts, Paul insists that tongues, prophecy, knowledge, and even sacrifice are nothing without love, the one thing that never ends when the partial passes away and we see face to face.
sermons.verdict: Without love you are nothing.

sermons.title: Building Up the Gathered Church
sermons.idea: Because love seeks the other's good, Paul orders their worship toward intelligibility, ranking prophecy that builds the church above tongues no one understands, so that the gathered body is edified, outsiders are convicted, and God is honored in order, not confusion.
sermons.verdict: In worship, build the church up.

sermons.title: If Christ Has Not Been Raised
sermons.idea: Some in Corinth denied the resurrection of the dead, and Paul stakes the entire gospel on it: Christ is risen as the firstfruits, the body will be raised imperishable, death is swallowed in victory, and therefore their labor in the Lord is never wasted.
sermons.verdict: Your labor is not in vain.

sermons.title: The Collection, the Coming, and the Love
sermons.idea: The resurrection that secures their future also commands their present, so Paul turns at once to a regular, planned gift for the saints in Jerusalem, to faithful labor and watchful love, ending a hard letter with a longing for the Lord to come.
sermons.verdict: Let all you do be love.

1-john.title: Tests of Life: An Exposition of 1 John
1-john.headline: Five sermons through the letter that asks whether what you believe is real
1-john.bigIdea: John writes to people unsettled by teachers who left, and he gives them three tests by which to know they belong to God and possess eternal life: walking in the light, loving one another, and confessing that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh. The letter does not soothe doubt by lowering the standard. It grounds assurance in the fellowship of the Father and the Son, and in the blood of Jesus that cleanses.
1-john.christConnection: When the test exposes us, Jesus Christ the righteous stands as our advocate with the Father, and he is himself the propitiation for our sins, so that confession leads not to despair but to cleansing. The same Christ who is the ground of our forgiveness is the love we are commanded to imitate, for he laid down his life, and we know love by that.

sermons.title: The Word of Life and the Light We Walk In
sermons.idea: Eternal life appeared in a man the apostles touched and heard, and fellowship with the God who is light is real only for those who stop pretending they have no sin and instead confess it, trusting the blood of Jesus and his advocacy to cleanse them.
sermons.verdict: Walk in the light. Confess.

sermons.title: The Old Commandment Made New, and a Love That Cannot Hold the World
sermons.idea: We know we have come to know God if we keep his commandments and love our brother, for the one who hates is still in darkness, and the love of the Father cannot live in the same heart that loves the world, which is passing away with its desires.
sermons.verdict: Love the Father, not the world.

sermons.title: Children of God, and Love That Costs Something
sermons.idea: The Father has called us his children now, and though what we will be is not yet seen, we know that when Christ appears we shall be like him, and that hope purifies, so that the children of God are known by righteousness and by a love that, like Christ laying down his life, gives in deed and not merely in word.
sermons.verdict: Love in deed and truth.

sermons.title: Test the Spirits, Because God Is Love
sermons.idea: Every spirit must be tested by whether it confesses Jesus Christ come in the flesh, and the spirit that does belongs to God who is love, a love proven when he sent his Son as the propitiation for our sins, so that we love because he first loved us and cannot claim to love God while hating a brother we have seen.
sermons.verdict: We love because he first loved.

sermons.title: The Faith That Overcomes, and the Knowledge of Eternal Life
sermons.idea: Everyone born of God believes Jesus is the Christ and overcomes the world by that faith, and God has given this testimony plainly: he gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son, so that those who have the Son may know, not merely hope, that they have eternal life.
sermons.verdict: Know that you have life.

1-kings.title: The Divided Heart: Preaching Through 1 Kings
1-kings.headline: A throne, a temple, and a kingdom that breaks along the fault line of the heart
1-kings.bigIdea: 1 Kings traces a kingdom from its golden height under Solomon to its fracture and decline, exposing how divided hearts ruin kings and how God keeps speaking through prophets when kings will not listen.
1-kings.christConnection: Every king in 1 Kings is measured against a standard none of them keeps, and the wisdom, temple, and word they each fail to embody point forward to the true King whose heart was never divided, who is greater than Solomon and the temple, and who is the Word the prophets only carried.

sermons.title: The Throne Secured in Blood
sermons.idea: David's kingdom passes to Solomon not through clean succession but through palace intrigue and settled scores, and the throne is established only after old debts are paid in death.
sermons.verdict: A kingdom secured. Not yet pure.

sermons.title: Ask What You Will
sermons.idea: Given a blank check from God, Solomon asks not for long life or riches but for a listening heart to discern good and evil, and God grants the wisdom along with what he did not request.
sermons.verdict: He asked rightly. Watch what follows.

sermons.title: Wisdom on Display
sermons.idea: Solomon's wisdom, wealth, and peace reach every corner of the kingdom and beyond its borders, and the nations come to listen, fulfilling the promise that Israel would bless the world.
sermons.verdict: Wisdom that draws the nations in.

sermons.title: A House for the Name
sermons.idea: Solomon builds the temple over seven years as a dwelling for God's name, and the long account of stone, cedar, and gold insists that God's presence among his people is worth this much care.
sermons.verdict: The presence is worth every stone.

sermons.title: The Glory Fills the House
sermons.idea: At the dedication the cloud fills the temple and Solomon prays that God would hear from heaven when his people sin, repent, and turn toward this place, knowing already they will need to.
sermons.verdict: A house built. Exile already named.

sermons.title: The Queen Comes to Listen
sermons.idea: God renews the covenant with conditions while Solomon's fame, gold, and the queen of Sheba's praise reach their peak, and the gathering of horses, silver, and treasure quietly breaks the law given to kings.
sermons.verdict: The height. And the seed of ruin.

sermons.title: The Heart Turned Away
sermons.idea: Solomon's many wives turn his heart after other gods, and the wisest king becomes an idolater, so God tears the kingdom from his son and keeps only a remnant for David's sake.
sermons.verdict: The wise king lost his heart.

sermons.title: The Kingdom Torn in Two
sermons.idea: Rehoboam's harshness and Jeroboam's golden calves split the kingdom and set the northern throne on idolatry from its first day, so that the sin of Jeroboam becomes the measure of every king who follows.
sermons.verdict: One foolish word. A nation split.

sermons.title: King After King, Sin After Sin
sermons.idea: A rapid succession of kings in Judah and Israel walk in the sins of those before them, with murder, conspiracy, and idolatry compounding until Ahab arrives doing more evil than all who came before.
sermons.verdict: The pattern hardens into a curse.

sermons.title: Fed by Ravens, Sustained at Zarephath
sermons.idea: As Ahab's reign begins, Elijah declares a drought and is kept alive by ravens and a widow's last meal, and the God of Israel proves himself Lord even over the rain that Baal claimed to give.
sermons.verdict: The God who feeds in famine.

sermons.title: The God Who Answers by Fire
sermons.idea: On Mount Carmel Elijah forces Israel to choose, and when Baal is silent the fire of the Lord falls on the soaked altar, proving before all the people that the Lord is God and Baal is nothing.
sermons.verdict: Stop limping between two opinions.

sermons.title: The Still Small Voice
sermons.idea: After the mountaintop Elijah collapses into fear and despair, and God meets him not in wind, earthquake, or fire but in a low whisper, feeds him, corrects his self-pity, and sends him back to work.
sermons.verdict: Not in the fire. In the whisper.

sermons.title: Victory Despised
sermons.idea: God twice hands Ahab victory over Syria to prove that he is the Lord, but Ahab spares the king God had devoted to destruction, and a prophet pronounces his life forfeit for the mercy he had no right to give.
sermons.verdict: He spared what God condemned.

sermons.title: Naboth's Vineyard
sermons.idea: Ahab covets a man's inheritance, Jezebel murders Naboth to seize it, and Elijah meets the king in the stolen vineyard with a verdict of doom, until Ahab's mortified repentance delays the judgment.
sermons.verdict: Coveting ends in a man's blood.

sermons.title: The Lying Spirit and the Last Ride
sermons.idea: Four hundred prophets flatter Ahab toward war while Micaiah alone tells the truth he does not want to hear, and the king who dressed in disguise to cheat the word of God dies by a random arrow exactly as foretold.
sermons.verdict: No disguise outruns the word.

1-peter.title: Elect Exiles: An Expository Series Through 1 Peter
1-peter.headline: A letter to scattered Christians on how to suffer well, stay holy, and hold a living hope when the world treats you as a stranger.
1-peter.bigIdea: Peter writes to believers displaced and slandered for their faith, and he does not promise them an easier life. He grounds them in a living hope secured by the resurrection, calls them to holiness in a hostile culture, and teaches them to follow the pattern of a Savior who suffered before he was glorified. The whole letter answers one question: how do you live well as a stranger in a world that is not your home?
1-peter.christConnection: Christ is the suffering and glorified Savior whose path the exile must walk: he was rejected by men yet chosen by God, he bore sin in his body on the tree, and he was raised and crowned so that those who follow him through suffering will share his glory. He is at once the example the exile imitates and the Lamb whose precious blood ransoms the exile home.

sermons.title: A Living Hope and a Faith Refined by Fire
sermons.idea: God has caused us to be born again into an imperishable inheritance through the resurrection of Christ, so that the fires of trial do not destroy our faith but prove it genuine, more precious than gold.
sermons.verdict: Your hope outlasts the fire.

sermons.title: Be Holy, Ransomed by the Precious Blood
sermons.idea: Because we were ransomed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ, we are now called to be holy as our Father is holy, loving one another earnestly from a heart purified by the living and abiding word.
sermons.verdict: Bought at that price. Be holy.

sermons.title: The Living Stone, a Chosen People, and the Pattern of the Cross
sermons.idea: Christ is the living stone rejected by men but chosen by God, and those built upon him become a chosen people who honor authority and endure unjust suffering by following the steps of the One who, when reviled, did not revile in return.
sermons.verdict: Follow the Stone they rejected.

sermons.title: The Hidden Person of the Heart and a Reason for the Hope
sermons.idea: In marriage and in a hostile world alike, the believer answers slander not with retaliation but with a quiet beauty of character and a ready, gentle defense of the hope within, because Christ suffered the righteous for the unrighteous to bring us to God.
sermons.verdict: Suffer well. Answer with hope.

sermons.title: Arm Yourselves with Christ's Mindset and Steward His Grace
sermons.idea: Because Christ suffered in the flesh, we arm ourselves with the same resolve to be done with sin, stewarding God's varied grace toward one another and not being surprised by the fiery trial, but rejoicing that we share the sufferings of Christ.
sermons.verdict: Arm yourself for the fire.

sermons.title: Shepherd the Flock, Humble Yourselves, Cast Your Anxieties
sermons.idea: Elders are to shepherd God's flock willingly and not for gain, all are to clothe themselves with humility under God's mighty hand, casting every anxiety on the One who cares for them and will himself restore, confirm, and strengthen them.
sermons.verdict: Stoop low. He lifts you.

1-samuel.title: The Kingdom No One Asked For Rightly: Preaching Through 1 Samuel
1-samuel.headline: From a Barren Woman's Prayer to a King's Body on a Wall
1-samuel.bigIdea: 1 Samuel traces how God dismantles a failed priesthood, refuses to be managed by a demanded monarchy, and quietly raises up the kind of king He has wanted all along, a king after His own heart, not the people's eyes.
1-samuel.christConnection: Hannah's song announces a God who reverses the proud and lifts the powerless, and that reversal runs through the whole book toward David, the anointed shepherd-king from Bethlehem who is hunted, spared by no power but God's, and waits years for a throne already promised, the pattern the true Anointed One, Jesus, fulfills and exceeds.

sermons.title: The Prayer of an Empty Woman
sermons.idea: God hears the cry of a barren, mocked woman and answers it with a son she then gives away, beginning the whole story of Israel's deliverance in a place of unbearable weakness.
sermons.verdict: God begins where you are emptied.

sermons.title: Sons of Eli, Son of Hannah
sermons.idea: While Eli's sons treat the holy things of God with contempt and Eli will not restrain them, the boy Samuel grows in favor, and God announces judgment on a house that honored itself above Him.
sermons.verdict: God is not mocked by His priests.

sermons.title: A Word Becomes Rare, Then a Boy Hears
sermons.idea: In a time when the word of the Lord was rare, God bypasses the failing priesthood and speaks to a child, and Samuel learns that the first task of a prophet is to tell the hard word without softening it.
sermons.verdict: Speak the word you were given.

sermons.title: The Glory Has Departed
sermons.idea: Israel treats the ark as a lucky charm to win a battle without repentance, and God lets it be captured, killing Eli's sons and Eli, exposing a religion that wants God's power without God Himself.
sermons.verdict: You cannot carry God like a charm.

sermons.title: God Needs No Defense
sermons.idea: Captured by the Philistines, the ark topples Dagon and afflicts every city that holds it, proving that the God of Israel defends His own honor among the nations without a single Israelite lifting a hand.
sermons.verdict: God defends Himself among His enemies.

sermons.title: If You Return, Return Fully
sermons.idea: Samuel calls Israel to put away foreign gods and return to the Lord with all their heart, and when they do, God Himself thunders against the Philistines, so Samuel raises a stone of remembrance called Ebenezer.
sermons.verdict: Repentance is the only real defense.

sermons.title: Give Us a King Like the Nations
sermons.idea: Israel rejects the Lord as king and demands a human king to be like the nations, and God grants the request as both gift and judgment, warning that the king they crave will take and take from them.
sermons.verdict: Be careful what you demand from God.

sermons.title: The Tall Man Hiding in the Baggage
sermons.idea: God privately anoints Saul, a striking and humble young man, and gives him a new heart and confirming signs, yet even at his coronation Saul hides among the supplies, an early crack in the king the people wanted.
sermons.verdict: Stature is not the same as a heart.

sermons.title: A Real Victory and a Sober Farewell
sermons.idea: Saul's Spirit-driven rescue of Jabesh-gilead is real, but Samuel's farewell makes plain that king and people alike now stand under the same demand: fear the Lord and serve Him, or be swept away with your king.
sermons.verdict: Fear the Lord, king and people both.

sermons.title: The King Who Could Not Wait
sermons.idea: Pressed by a Philistine army and a delayed Samuel, Saul seizes the priestly role he was never given, and in that anxious disobedience he forfeits an enduring dynasty while his son Jonathan trusts God against the odds.
sermons.verdict: Obedience cannot be replaced by religion.

sermons.title: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice
sermons.idea: Commanded to devote Amalek to destruction, Saul spares the best and blames the people, and God rejects him as king, teaching that partial obedience dressed as worship is still rebellion before God.
sermons.verdict: Partial obedience is still rebellion.

sermons.title: The Lord Looks at the Heart
sermons.idea: Sent to anoint a king among Jesse's sons, Samuel learns that God passes over the impressive eldest and chooses the overlooked shepherd boy David, because the Lord does not see as man sees but looks on the heart.
sermons.verdict: God sees what your mirror cannot.

sermons.title: The Battle Belongs to the Lord
sermons.idea: While a trained army cowers before Goliath, a shepherd boy who knows his God runs at the giant in the name of the Lord of hosts, declaring that the battle is the Lord's and the whole earth will know there is a God in Israel.
sermons.verdict: The fight belongs to your God.

sermons.title: When a Song Turns a Heart to Murder
sermons.idea: A women's song crediting David with more than Saul ignites a jealousy that hardens into murderous intent, while Jonathan binds himself to David in covenant love, dividing the house of Saul against itself.
sermons.verdict: Jealousy will rot a kingly heart.

sermons.title: A Friend Between Two Spears
sermons.idea: As Saul's hatred breaks into open attempts on David's life, Jonathan risks his own future and his father's wrath to protect God's anointed, choosing covenant loyalty over the throne he might have had.
sermons.verdict: Covenant love costs the loyal one.

sermons.title: The Blood on the Road to the Throne
sermons.idea: On the run, David's deception sets in motion the slaughter of the priests at Nob by Saul's hand, and the gathering of the desperate to David's side shows the heavy cost paid by others as the anointed flees.
sermons.verdict: Innocent blood marks Saul's descent.

sermons.title: Hunted, and Still Inquiring of God
sermons.idea: Though pursued relentlessly, David repeatedly inquires of the Lord before he acts and rescues a city that will betray him, learning to trust God's guidance and protection even when the net seems to be closing.
sermons.verdict: Inquire of God before you move.

sermons.title: The Robe He Would Not Tear Further
sermons.idea: With Saul defenseless in a cave, David refuses to lift his hand against the Lord's anointed, cutting only a corner of his robe and then grieving even that, refusing to seize by violence the throne God promised to give.
sermons.verdict: Refuse the shortcut God forbids.

sermons.title: The Sword a Wise Woman Stopped
sermons.idea: Insulted by a fool named Nabal, David rides out to slaughter his household, and only Abigail's wisdom and courage keep David from avenging himself, reminding him to leave vengeance to the Lord.
sermons.verdict: Let God avenge what wounds you.

sermons.title: Spared a Second Time
sermons.idea: Again given Saul sleeping and vulnerable, David takes only the spear and water jug and again refuses to strike the Lord's anointed, proving his restraint was conviction and not a single lucky moment.
sermons.verdict: True restraint repeats when no one watches.

sermons.title: The Doubt That Drove Him to the Enemy
sermons.idea: Worn down, David tells himself he will perish by Saul's hand and flees to the Philistines, living a double and deceptive life, showing how even a man after God's heart can act from fear instead of faith.
sermons.verdict: Fear can outargue what God promised.

sermons.title: A King Who Asked the Dead
sermons.idea: Abandoned by a God who no longer answers him, the terrified Saul seeks out a medium to summon Samuel, only to hear his own doom confirmed, the bitter end of a man who would not obey while he still could.
sermons.verdict: Silence from God is its own verdict.

sermons.title: Brought Low, Then Strengthened in the Lord
sermons.idea: Rejected by the Philistine lords and returning to a Ziklag burned and emptied of his family, David strengthens himself in the Lord his God, inquires of Him, and recovers all, while Saul moves toward ruin.
sermons.verdict: Strengthen yourself in your God.

sermons.title: The King the People Wanted, Dead on a Wall
sermons.idea: Saul and his sons fall on Mount Gilboa and his body is fastened to the wall of Beth-shan, the grim end of the king Israel demanded, while the men of Jabesh-gilead remember mercy and bury him with honor.
sermons.verdict: The throne God gives, only God keeps.

1-thessalonians.title: The Church That Waits: Expository Studies in 1 Thessalonians
1-thessalonians.headline: A young church, a watching world, and the God who comes back
1-thessalonians.bigIdea: Paul writes to a congregation only months old, hunted by persecution and unsettled by death, and he does not give them management tips. He grounds them in what God has done, models a ministry that costs the minister everything, and points them again and again to the day the Lord returns. The whole letter teaches a church how to stand by teaching it how to wait.
1-thessalonians.christConnection: Every chapter of 1 Thessalonians bends toward one horizon: the return of the risen Christ, who delivers His people from the wrath to come and gathers the living and the dead to Himself. The church's hope is not a better life now but a Lord who is coming, and that coming is what makes faith, labor, and grief bearable.

sermons.title: Faith, Love, and Hope in a Watching Church
sermons.idea: Paul gives thanks for a church he can read from the outside, because the gospel that came to them in power produced visible faith, laboring love, and a hope that endured suffering, and that hope was nothing other than waiting for God's Son from heaven who rescues from the wrath to come.
sermons.verdict: Their waiting was their witness.

sermons.title: The Minister Who Has Nothing to Hide
sermons.idea: Paul defends his ministry not by listing credentials but by recalling how he came: gentle as a nursing mother, working night and day so as not to burden them, exhorting them like a father, never trading in flattery or greed, because a ministry approved by God answers to God and not to the crowd.
sermons.verdict: He gave them the gospel and himself.

sermons.title: Timothy's Report and a Faith That Stands
sermons.idea: Separated from the church and unable to return, Paul sends Timothy and waits in dread until the report comes back that they are standing firm, and the good news of their faith is so much life to him that he prays night and day to see them again and to perfect what is lacking.
sermons.verdict: Their standing was his life.

sermons.title: The Holiness God Has Called You To
sermons.idea: The will of God for this church is their sanctification, worked out concretely in sexual purity that controls the body in honor rather than passion, in brotherly love that increases, and in a quiet, working, self-supporting life that commands the respect of outsiders and depends on no one.
sermons.verdict: God called you to be holy.

sermons.title: The Dead in Christ and the Coming of the Lord
sermons.idea: Paul will not let them grieve as those without hope, because the Lord Himself will descend, the dead in Christ will rise first, the living will be caught up together with them, and since that day comes like a thief on a sleeping world, the children of light keep awake and sober, armed with faith, love, and the hope of salvation.
sermons.verdict: Grieve, but not without hope.

sermons.title: Final Words for a People Who Wait
sermons.idea: Paul closes with rapid commands for the life of a waiting church: honor those who labor among you, warn the idle and help the weak, rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in everything, do not quench the Spirit, test everything and hold the good, and trust the faithful God who calls to keep you blameless until Christ comes.
sermons.verdict: The faithful God will keep you.

1-timothy.title: Sound Doctrine, Ordered Households: An Exposition of 1 Timothy
1-timothy.headline: Six sermons through Paul's charge to a young pastor about what guards a church and what wrecks it
1-timothy.bigIdea: Paul writes to ground a church under pressure: that the gospel he was entrusted with be guarded against false teaching, that worship and leadership be ordered, and that those who teach it be the kind of people their teaching describes. The mercy that found a blasphemer is the mercy that holds a church together.
1-timothy.christConnection: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom Paul names himself the foremost, and there is one God and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all. Every charge in this letter rests on that single mediating mercy, not on the strength of the church or its leaders.

sermons.title: The Charge and the Foremost Sinner
sermons.idea: Paul commands Timothy to silence teachers who turn the law into speculation, because the law's purpose is to expose the lawless and drive them to the gospel that saved Paul, the foremost of sinners, as living proof of Christ's perfect patience.
sermons.verdict: Mercy found the worst of us.

sermons.title: Prayer First, and the One Mediator
sermons.idea: Because God desires all people to be saved and there is one mediator who gave himself as a ransom, the gathered church orders its worship around prayer for all people and conduct that adorns the gospel rather than distracts from it.
sermons.verdict: One mediator. Pray for all.

sermons.title: Character Before Office
sermons.idea: Overseers and deacons are qualified chiefly by tested character, household faithfulness, and a clear conscience, because the church is the household of God and the pillar of the truth, and its leaders must embody the mystery of godliness they guard.
sermons.verdict: The office requires the man.

sermons.title: Train Yourself for Godliness
sermons.idea: Against teachers who forbid what God created good, the good minister is nourished on sound doctrine and trains himself for godliness, watching his life and teaching closely so that both he and his hearers are kept.
sermons.verdict: Train yourself. Watch your life.

sermons.title: Honor in the Household of God
sermons.idea: The church orders its relationships by honor and justice: caring for genuine widows while pressing families to provide, paying and protecting faithful elders, and refusing both rash judgment and partiality among its members.
sermons.verdict: Honor the church as family.

sermons.title: Godliness With Contentment, and the Good Fight
sermons.idea: Against teachers who imagine godliness is a means of gain, Paul commands contentment, warns that the love of money pierces the soul, charges the rich to be generous, and calls Timothy to flee, pursue, and fight the good fight of faith while guarding the deposit entrusted to him.
sermons.verdict: Flee greed. Fight for faith.

2-chronicles.title: The House and the Heart: Preaching Through 2 Chronicles
2-chronicles.headline: From the temple Solomon built to the rubble Babylon left, a kingdom is weighed by whether it will seek the Lord with all its heart.
2-chronicles.bigIdea: The Chronicler retells the story of Judah's kings for the people who came home from exile, measuring every reign by one question: did they seek the Lord, and did they keep His house. Glory rises with worship and obedience; ruin comes through pride, idolatry, and a deafness to the prophets. The book ends not with a tomb but with a door left open, the decree of Cyrus, a God who is not finished.
2-chronicles.christConnection: Every king the Chronicler praises eventually fails, and every reform he records eventually erodes, which is why the final word is not a king at all but a decree to rebuild a house. The true Son of David built a temple not made with hands, kept faith where Solomon faltered, bore the exile Judah earned, and is Himself the dwelling of God with humanity. The open door at the end of 2 Chronicles opens onto Him.

sermons.title: The King Who Asked for the Right Thing
sermons.idea: Solomon, established by God and surrounded by wealth, stands before the altar and asks not for riches or long life or the death of his enemies but for wisdom to govern God's people, and God gives him both the wisdom and the things he did not request.
sermons.verdict: Ask first for wisdom to lead.

sermons.title: No House Can Hold Him
sermons.idea: As Solomon gathers the labor and treasure and craftsmen to build the temple, he confesses that the God who fills heaven and earth cannot be contained by any building, so the house is not a cage for God but a place to bring Him offering.
sermons.verdict: Build for a God uncontained.

sermons.title: Gold Over Everything
sermons.idea: On the threshing floor where the plague had been stopped, Solomon overlays the house in gold and casts its pillars and furnishings, and the labor of seven years declares that the worship of God is worth the best a nation can give.
sermons.verdict: Give God the costly best.

sermons.title: When the Glory Filled the House
sermons.idea: When the ark is brought in and the singers and trumpeters make one sound to praise the Lord for His goodness and His steadfast love forever, the cloud of glory fills the temple so the priests cannot stand to minister, and God takes residence in what was built for Him.
sermons.verdict: Praise as one. Glory comes.

sermons.title: A House for the Prayers of Sinners
sermons.idea: At the dedication Solomon kneels before the whole assembly and prays not that the temple will keep Israel from sin but that when they sin and turn back, even from a foreign captivity, God will hear from heaven and forgive, anchoring the nation's hope in mercy rather than perfection.
sermons.verdict: Hear from heaven and forgive.

sermons.title: If My People
sermons.idea: Fire falls and glory fills the house again, and then God answers Solomon's prayer with terms the exiles needed to hear: when judgment comes, if His people humble themselves, pray, seek His face, and turn from their ways, He will hear, forgive, and heal their land, but the same house can be cast off if they forsake Him.
sermons.verdict: Humble, pray, seek, and turn.

sermons.title: The Glory That Cannot Save
sermons.idea: Solomon's reign reaches its height in cities, ships, gold, and a queen who travels far to see his wisdom and goes home overwhelmed, yet the Chronicler tells it knowing this golden peak will not hold, because no human glory, however dazzling, secures a heart toward God.
sermons.verdict: Splendor is not the same as faithfulness.

sermons.title: The Kingdom Torn in a Day
sermons.idea: Rehoboam scorns the counsel of the old men and the cry of the people, the kingdom tears in two, and though he humbles himself when Shishak invades and so is spared total ruin, his reign records a king whose heart was not set to seek the Lord.
sermons.verdict: Set your heart to seek Him.

sermons.title: The God Who Helps the Outnumbered
sermons.idea: Abijah and then Asa learn that battles belong to the Lord who helps those who rely on Him, yet Asa, who began by leaning wholly on God against a vast army, ends by trusting a foreign alliance and his own physicians, proving that faith early is no guarantee of faith late.
sermons.verdict: Rely on God to the end.

sermons.title: Stand Still and See
sermons.idea: Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah by sending the law through the land and seeks the Lord, and when three armies come against him he fasts, prays, and is told the battle is not his but God's, so Judah sends the singers ahead and watches the enemy destroy itself, though even this good king's alliances with the house of Ahab leave a stain.
sermons.verdict: The battle is the Lord's.

sermons.title: Joash Rescued From the Slaughter
sermons.idea: Jehoram and Ahaziah and the murderous Athaliah nearly extinguish the line of David, but one infant is hidden in the house of God for six years until the priest Jehoiada crowns him and topples the usurper, and the covenant promise survives by the width of a single rescued child.
sermons.verdict: God preserves the promised line.

sermons.title: Good While the Counselor Lived
sermons.idea: Joash repairs the temple while Jehoiada guides him but turns to idols and murders the priest's son once Jehoiada dies, and Uzziah grows strong until he grows proud and seizes the priest's altar and is struck with leprosy, two kings undone the moment they stopped depending on God.
sermons.verdict: Strength turned to pride destroys.

sermons.title: The King Who Sinned in the Time of His Distress
sermons.idea: Jotham becomes mighty because he orders his ways before the Lord, but Ahaz, pressed by enemies, responds by sacrificing to the gods of the nations that defeated him and shutting the doors of the temple, growing more faithless precisely when affliction should have driven him back to God.
sermons.verdict: Distress is no excuse for unbelief.

sermons.title: Open the Doors Again
sermons.idea: Hezekiah, in the first month of his first year, reopens and cleanses the temple his father shut, restores the Passover and invites even the remnant of the fallen north, and the joy in Jerusalem is greater than any since Solomon, because true reform begins by reopening the house and calling people back to worship.
sermons.verdict: Reopen the house. Call them home.

sermons.title: When the Wall Could Not Save Him
sermons.idea: Hezekiah prepares the city and trusts the Lord against Assyria's mockery, and God answers, but his later pride after recovery and wealth shows that even a great deliverance does not cure the heart, which must keep humbling itself before God.
sermons.verdict: Deliverance does not cure pride.

sermons.title: No One Is Past Return
sermons.idea: Manasseh fills Jerusalem with idolatry and innocent blood, the worst king Judah knew, yet when he is dragged in chains to Babylon and humbles himself greatly before God, the Lord hears him and brings him home, so that even the most ruined life is not beyond the reach of repentance.
sermons.verdict: No sinner is beyond return.

sermons.title: The Word That Tore a King's Heart
sermons.idea: Josiah seeks God as a boy and purges the land, and when the lost book of the law is found and read, he tears his clothes, renews the covenant, and keeps a Passover unmatched since Samuel, showing that real reformation is born when the Word is recovered and a leader trembles at it.
sermons.verdict: Tremble when the Word is found.

sermons.title: The Fall and the Door Left Open
sermons.idea: The last kings mock the messengers of God until there is no remedy and Babylon burns the house and carries Judah away, yet the Chronicler ends not in ashes but in a Persian decree to rebuild the house of the Lord, proving that judgment is real, the land keeps its sabbaths, and God is not finished with His people.
sermons.verdict: He is not finished yet.

2-corinthians.title: Strength Made Perfect: Through 2 Corinthians
2-corinthians.headline: Paul writes from inside the affliction, not above it, and shows a church that ministry is cruciform or it is fraudulent.
2-corinthians.bigIdea: The gospel does not exempt the minister from suffering; it locates God's power precisely in the place suffering opens up. Across thirteen chapters Paul defends a ministry the Corinthians were tempted to despise, unimpressive, afflicted, financially scrupulous, slow to boast, and grounds its legitimacy not in strength but in the God who comforts the crushed, reconciles enemies, and perfects his power in weakness.
2-corinthians.christConnection: The crucified Christ is the pattern and the source: God reconciled the world to himself by making the sinless one to be sin for us, so that the power carried in our broken bodies is unmistakably his and not ours. The same Lord who said grace is sufficient and strength is perfected in weakness is the one who was crucified in weakness and lives by the power of God.

sermons.title: The God of All Comfort
sermons.idea: God meets his afflicted servants not by removing the affliction but by comforting them inside it, so that the comfort they receive becomes the comfort they hand to others, Paul was burdened beyond his strength, despaired of life itself, and learned to rely not on himself but on the God who raises the dead.
sermons.verdict: Comfort is given to be given away.

sermons.title: The Aroma of Christ
sermons.idea: Paul's competence for ministry is not his own but comes from God, who leads his servants in triumphal procession and spreads through them the fragrance of Christ, life to some, death to others, so that the Corinthians themselves, written on Paul's heart by the Spirit, are his only letter of recommendation.
sermons.verdict: Our sufficiency comes from God alone.

sermons.title: Unveiled Faces
sermons.idea: The ministry of the new covenant surpasses the glory of the old in permanence and boldness, for where the law engraved on stone brought condemnation that faded from Moses' face, the Spirit gives a glory that increases, and all who turn to the Lord have the veil removed and are being changed into his image from one degree of glory to another.
sermons.verdict: The Spirit unveils what law concealed.

sermons.title: Treasure in Jars of Clay
sermons.idea: God deliberately stores the surpassing power of the gospel in fragile, breakable people so that the power is plainly seen to be his and not ours, afflicted but not crushed, struck down but not destroyed, the minister carries the dying of Jesus in his body so that the life of Jesus is made visible, and does not lose heart because the unseen and eternal outweighs the momentary.
sermons.verdict: The clay is meant to crack.

sermons.title: Be Reconciled to God
sermons.idea: Because the love of Christ controls him and one died for all, Paul no longer regards anyone by worldly standards but pleads as Christ's ambassador the message entrusted to him: God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ, making the sinless one to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
sermons.verdict: God made him sin for us.

sermons.title: The Marks of True Ministry
sermons.idea: Paul commends his ministry not by credentials but by endurance, afflictions, beatings, sleepless nights, dishonor and honor alike, and on the basis of that costly honesty calls the Corinthians to open their hearts wide and to refuse partnership that compromises their devotion, since they are the temple of the living God who dwells among them.
sermons.verdict: True ministry is proven by endurance.

sermons.title: Godly Grief
sermons.idea: There is a grief that produces repentance leading to salvation without regret, and a worldly grief that only produces death, Paul rejoices not that he caused the Corinthians pain by his severe letter but that their pain turned them back, producing earnestness, indignation, and longing, proving them innocent in the matter.
sermons.verdict: Godly grief works repentance without regret.

sermons.title: The Grace of Giving
sermons.idea: Generosity is itself a grace of God, the Macedonians, in extreme poverty and severe affliction, gave beyond their means and begged for the privilege, because they first gave themselves to the Lord; and the supreme pattern is Christ, who though rich became poor so that by his poverty the Corinthians might become rich.
sermons.verdict: He became poor to make us rich.

sermons.title: The Cheerful Giver
sermons.idea: The one who sows generously reaps generously, and God loves a cheerful giver because he is able to supply every need so that the giver abounds in good work, generosity is not depletion but provision, producing thanksgiving to God and proving the gospel the giver confesses, all answered by God's indescribable gift.
sermons.verdict: God loves a cheerful giver.

sermons.title: Weapons Not of the Flesh
sermons.idea: Paul wages his ministry with divine weapons that demolish arguments and every pretension raised against the knowledge of God, refusing to commend himself by comparison or to boast beyond the field God assigned, for it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
sermons.verdict: Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.

sermons.title: Boasting in Weakness
sermons.idea: Forced by false apostles to defend himself, Paul boasts not in visions or eloquence but in the catalogue of his sufferings, imprisonments, beatings, shipwrecks, dangers, the daily pressure of anxiety for the churches, turning the world's measure of credibility upside down by glorying in the very things that show his weakness.
sermons.verdict: He boasts in his weakness.

sermons.title: My Grace Is Sufficient
sermons.idea: Granted extraordinary revelations, Paul was given a thorn in the flesh to keep him from conceit, and though he pleaded three times for its removal, the Lord answered that his grace is sufficient and his power is perfected in weakness, so Paul learned to boast gladly of his weaknesses, that the power of Christ might rest upon him.
sermons.verdict: Power is perfected in weakness.

sermons.title: Examine Yourselves
sermons.idea: Coming a third time, Paul warns that he will not spare the unrepentant and urges the Corinthians to test themselves to see whether they are in the faith, for Christ, crucified in weakness, lives by the power of God, and Paul would rather appear weak than have to use his authority for tearing down rather than building up.
sermons.verdict: Test yourselves; Christ lives by God's power.

2-john.title: Truth and the Door: Preaching 2 John
2-john.headline: A short letter that refuses to separate love from truth, and refuses to open the door to those who deny that Christ has come in the flesh.
2-john.bigIdea: Love walks in truth, and truth has a threshold; the elder writes to a church to keep them in the commandment they have had from the beginning and to keep deceivers off the porch.
2-john.christConnection: The whole letter turns on one test: whether a person abides in the teaching of Christ, that Jesus has come in the flesh. To remain in that teaching is to have both the Father and the Son; to run ahead of it is to have neither, which is why fellowship is finally measured by Christ, not by sincerity.

sermons.title: Walking in Truth and Love
sermons.idea: The elder loves this church in the truth, rejoices to find her children walking in it, and presses an old commandment, not a new one: that we love one another, and that this love is defined as walking according to His commandments.
sermons.verdict: Love is the old commandment, kept.

sermons.title: Watching the Door
sermons.idea: Many deceivers have gone out who deny that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh; whoever runs ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ has neither the Father nor the Son, so the church must guard its full reward and not receive such a one into the house or even greet him.
sermons.verdict: Some doors must stay shut.

2-kings.title: The Fire and the Fall: Preaching Through 2 Kings
2-kings.headline: A kingdom dies slowly, and the word of God keeps coming until the gate of Jerusalem is broken.
2-kings.bigIdea: 2 Kings is the long account of how the word of the LORD outlasts the kings who ignore it. Prophets succeed prophets, kings rot from the inside, two nations go into exile, and the temple burns. Through it all the book insists on one thing: God said it would happen, and it happened. Covenant judgment is not random tragedy but the keeping of an old promise, and even in the rubble a small mercy is held open for a people who deserved none.
2-kings.christConnection: The book ends with a king of Judah lifted from prison and given a seat at a foreign table, an undeserved kindness that keeps David's line breathing in exile. That ember of grace points past every failed son of David to the Son who would not fail. Elijah taken up alive, Elisha raising the dead and feeding the hungry, a leper cleansed, water made sweet, an axe head raised from the deep, a temple wept over and rebuilt in flesh, the LORD defending His city for His own name's sake, a Passover kept again under Josiah, a king's heart torn at the reading of the book, and a guarded line of David that judgment could not extinguish all reach forward to Christ, the prophet greater than Elisha and the King who keeps covenant where every other king broke it.

sermons.title: The God Who Will Not Be Consulted As One Among Many
sermons.idea: Ahaziah sends to a foreign god because his bones are broken, and Elijah meets him with the LORD's question: is there no God in Israel? Then Elijah is taken up, the mantle falls to Elisha, and the same Spirit that parted the Jordan for the master parts it for the servant.
sermons.verdict: Ask Israel's God, or none.

sermons.title: The Word in the Wilderness and the House of Mercy
sermons.idea: Three kings march into a waterless desert and live only because Elisha speaks the LORD's provision, while in Israel's ordinary homes the prophet fills the widow's empty jars, restores the Shunammite's dead son, heals the poisoned pot, and feeds a hundred from a few loaves. The God of armies is the God of the kitchen.
sermons.verdict: He provides where you ran dry.

sermons.title: Wash and Be Clean: The Pride That Almost Missed the Cure
sermons.idea: Naaman the great commander wants healing on his own terms and nearly walks away from grace because it comes too plainly, in a muddy river he despises. He bends, he washes, he is made clean, and Gehazi grabs for what was given freely and carries the leprosy out the door.
sermons.verdict: Grace offends before it heals.

sermons.title: The Eyes That See the Hills Full of Fire
sermons.idea: Surrounded by an army, Elisha's servant despairs until his eyes are opened to the chariots of fire that were there all along, and the same LORD breaks a starving siege overnight so that four lepers stumble into an abandoned camp of plenty. The unseen armies of God outnumber the visible armies of fear.
sermons.verdict: More are with you than against.

sermons.title: The Sword of Judgment and Its Own Half Heart
sermons.idea: The word spoken against Ahab's house comes due as Jehu is anointed and rides hard, cutting down Joram, Jezebel, and the whole rotten line, doing exactly what the LORD decreed. Yet Jehu, zealous against Baal, will not leave the golden calves, and the executioner of one sin keeps another.
sermons.verdict: Zeal is not yet obedience.

sermons.title: A Hidden Child and the Arrows Struck Too Few
sermons.idea: Athaliah murders the royal seed but one infant is hidden in the temple, and David's lamp is not put out; Joash is crowned, the covenant renewed, the house of the LORD repaired. Then the deaths of faithful priest and prophet leave Israel half-hearted, and a dying king strikes the ground only three times when he should have struck until it was finished.
sermons.verdict: Half measures forfeit full deliverance.

sermons.title: Why Samaria Fell: The Long Indictment of the North
sermons.idea: King after king walks in the sin of Jeroboam, prophets warn, the LORD is patient across generations, and at last Assyria carries the northern kingdom into exile. The narrator stops the story to explain plainly that this was no accident of politics but the harvest of covenant breaking the people were warned of from the start.
sermons.verdict: God warned them. They would not hear.

sermons.title: The LORD Defends His City for His Own Name
sermons.idea: Hezekiah trusts the LORD, tears Sennacherib's blasphemous letter open before God, and the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp so that the city is spared by no sword of Judah's. Yet the same king, granted fifteen added years, parades his treasure before Babylon and is told where his sons will one day go.
sermons.verdict: He saves the city, names the future.

sermons.title: When the Book Was Found: Reform That Could Not Reverse the Verdict
sermons.idea: Manasseh fills Jerusalem with blood and idols and sets the sentence beyond recall, then Josiah hears the long-lost book read, tears his robes, and tears down the high places in the most thorough reform Judah ever saw. The reform is real and it is good, and it cannot undo what an earlier generation made certain.
sermons.verdict: Repentance matters even when it costs.

sermons.title: The Gate Is Broken, the Lamp Still Burns
sermons.idea: Babylon comes, the wall is breached, the temple is burned, the last king's eyes are put out, and Judah goes into exile exactly as the prophets said. Then the book ends not in total dark but on a strange mercy: Jehoiachin is lifted from prison, given a seat at the king's table, and David's line keeps breathing in a far country.
sermons.verdict: Judgment fell. The promise held.

2-peter.title: Make Your Calling Sure: An Exposition of 2 Peter
2-peter.headline: A dying apostle, a coming Lord, and the patience that has not yet closed the door
2-peter.bigIdea: Because God has already given everything required for life and godliness, and because the Lord who promised to return is certain to come, believers must guard the truth against those who deny it and grow in grace while the patience of God still holds the door of repentance open.
2-peter.christConnection: The whole letter strains toward the day of the Lord Jesus Christ, whose return is delayed not by weakness but by mercy. He counts the long wait as patience, not slowness, because he is not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance.

sermons.title: Everything You Need, and the Word You Can Trust
sermons.idea: God's divine power has already granted everything needed for life and godliness through the knowledge of Christ, so the believer is to confirm his calling by adding to faith a growing character, resting on the prophetic word that did not come from human will but from men carried along by the Holy Spirit and confirmed by eyewitnesses of his majesty.
sermons.verdict: He gave it all. Add yourself.

sermons.title: False Teachers and the Judgment That Waits
sermons.idea: Just as false prophets rose among the people of old, false teachers will secretly bring in destructive heresies, exploiting the church with greed and sensuality; but the same God who did not spare angels, the ancient world, or Sodom knows how to rescue the godly and hold the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgment.
sermons.verdict: Their judgment is not asleep.

sermons.title: The Day Will Come, So Grow
sermons.idea: Scoffers mock the delay of Christ's coming, but the Lord is not slow as some count slowness; he is patient, not wishing that any should perish but that all should reach repentance, and because the day of the Lord will come and the heavens will pass away, believers are to live holy lives and grow in the grace and knowledge of their Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
sermons.verdict: Mercy delays it. Grow meanwhile.

2-samuel.title: The Weight of a Crown: Preaching Through 2 Samuel
2-samuel.headline: David rises, David falls, and the throne outlives the man who sat on it
2-samuel.bigIdea: God establishes an everlasting kingdom through a flawed king, so that every throne after David must answer to a covenant David could not keep.
2-samuel.christConnection: The covenant of 2 Samuel 7 promises David a son whose throne God will establish forever, a promise no son of David ever fulfilled until Jesus, born of David's line, raised to reign without end. The grief, the sin, and the broken house of David all press toward the King who would not fail where David failed.

sermons.title: How the Mighty Have Fallen
sermons.idea: David grieves the death of Saul and Jonathan and executes the Amalekite who claimed to finish the king, refusing to climb to the throne over the body of God's anointed.
sermons.verdict: He would not seize the crown.

sermons.title: A House Divided
sermons.idea: David is made king over Judah while Abner crowns Ish-bosheth over Israel, and the long, bloody war between the houses exposes how slowly even a God-given kingdom is won.
sermons.verdict: The throne came by patience, not force.

sermons.title: King Over All Israel
sermons.idea: After the murder of Ish-bosheth, the tribes anoint David king over all Israel, and he takes Jerusalem, growing greater because the Lord of hosts was with him.
sermons.verdict: The Lord made the king great.

sermons.title: The Ark and the Threshing Floor
sermons.idea: David brings the ark to Jerusalem, but Uzzah dies for steadying it and Michal despises David's dancing, teaching that the holy God is approached on His terms and worshiped without reserve.
sermons.verdict: Holiness is not handled casually.

sermons.title: A House You Did Not Build
sermons.idea: When David offers to build God a house, God refuses and instead promises to build David a house, an everlasting throne secured by grace and not by David's achievement.
sermons.verdict: God builds the house, not us.

sermons.title: Kindness in a Conquering Reign
sermons.idea: At the height of his victories David seeks out Mephibosheth, the crippled heir of Saul, and shows covenant kindness to a man who could expect only death.
sermons.verdict: Grace seeks the one left behind.

sermons.title: The Spring When Kings Go to War
sermons.idea: David stays home, takes Bathsheba, and arranges Uriah's death, and the chapter that names every sin plainly ends by naming the One who saw it.
sermons.verdict: The thing David did displeased the Lord.

sermons.title: You Are the Man
sermons.idea: Nathan's parable strips David of his defenses, and the king who escaped no one's notice before God confesses, is forgiven, and still bears the consequence in his house.
sermons.verdict: Forgiven, and still the sword remains.

sermons.title: The Sword in the House
sermons.idea: Amnon's crime against Tamar, Absalom's revenge, and David's failure to act show the promised judgment unfolding inside the family the king could not govern.
sermons.verdict: The sin came home to David.

sermons.title: The King Goes Out Weeping
sermons.idea: Absalom steals the kingdom and David flees Jerusalem barefoot and weeping, submitting to God's hand even as Ahithophel's counsel is turned to folly.
sermons.verdict: The king bowed beneath God's hand.

sermons.title: O Absalom, My Son
sermons.idea: Absalom dies against David's orders and the king's grief nearly costs him the kingdom, until Joab forces him to govern the love that would have undone the realm.
sermons.verdict: Even right grief must serve the people.

sermons.title: Old Debts and New Revolts
sermons.idea: Sheba's rebellion and the famine for Saul's broken oath show that a kingdom carries unsettled accounts, and atonement, not amnesia, is what sets the land right.
sermons.verdict: Old guilt must be answered, not ignored.

sermons.title: The Song of a Delivered King
sermons.idea: David sings of the Lord as his rock and deliverer and speaks his last words of the righteous ruler to come, confessing that his house's hope rests on an everlasting covenant.
sermons.verdict: His hope was a coming King.

sermons.title: The Census and the Altar
sermons.idea: David numbers the people in pride, repents under judgment, and refuses to offer God a sacrifice that costs him nothing, buying the threshing floor where atonement is made.
sermons.verdict: He would not worship for free.

2-thessalonians.title: Hold the Line: Suffering, Deception, and Work in 2 Thessalonians
2-thessalonians.headline: A church under pressure, learning to wait without panic and to stand without quitting
2-thessalonians.bigIdea: Between the cross and the coming of Christ, the church suffers, gets lied to, and grows weary, and the answer to all three is the same God who will set everything right when Jesus is revealed.
2-thessalonians.christConnection: Paul anchors a frightened, persecuted church to one fixed point: the day the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven in flaming fire, when he repays affliction and is glorified in his saints. Their steadfastness now is not heroism but a settled confidence that the One who suffered for them will return to judge for them.

sermons.title: When God Settles the Account
sermons.idea: The Thessalonians' growing faith and love under persecution is itself evidence of the righteous judgment of God, who will repay their afflicters with affliction and grant them relief when the Lord Jesus is revealed in flaming fire, glorified in his saints.
sermons.verdict: He repays. We endure.

sermons.title: Do Not Be Shaken
sermons.idea: The day of the Lord has not already come, because the rebellion and the man of lawlessness must first be revealed and then destroyed by Christ at his appearing; so the church must not be deceived by spirit, word, or forged letter, but stand firm and hold to the teaching it received.
sermons.verdict: Hold what you were taught.

sermons.title: Stand Firm, and Get to Work
sermons.idea: While the faithful Lord guards them from evil, the believers are commanded to keep away from idlers and imitate Paul's own labor, for the one unwilling to work should not eat, and they must not grow weary in doing good.
sermons.verdict: Do not grow weary.

2-timothy.title: Last Words: Preaching Through 2 Timothy
2-timothy.headline: A dying apostle hands the gospel to the next man, and tells him to hold the line
2-timothy.bigIdea: Paul writes from a Roman prison knowing he will not get out, and instead of asking for comfort he asks Timothy to guard the gospel, suffer for it, pass it on intact, and preach it to the end. The pastor's calling is not to keep himself but to keep the deposit.
2-timothy.christConnection: The whole letter rests on a Christ who has already abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel, so that a man in chains can speak of dying without fear. The crown of righteousness Paul waits for is laid up by the righteous Judge for all who have loved His appearing, won not by Paul's record but by the One who remains faithful when we are faithless.

sermons.title: Fan Into Flame
sermons.idea: The gift of God in Timothy was real but fading under fear, so Paul tells him to rekindle it, because God did not give a spirit of fear but of power, love, and self-control, and the same gospel worth being chained for is worth guarding by the Spirit who dwells in us.
sermons.verdict: Guard the deposit. Stop being ashamed.

sermons.title: Soldier, Athlete, Farmer
sermons.idea: Grace strengthens a man for hardship he does not avoid: the soldier does not entangle himself, the athlete competes by the rules, the hardworking farmer gets the first share, and what Timothy received from Paul he must entrust to faithful men who will teach others, because the word of God is not chained even when its preachers are.
sermons.verdict: Endure. Entrust it to faithful men.

sermons.title: When the Last Days Are Hard
sermons.idea: Paul names the difficult times to come, lovers of self and of pleasure with a form of godliness denying its power, and against that collapse he sets two anchors for Timothy: the people who taught him the faith, and the sacred writings that are breathed out by God and able to make the man of God complete for every good work.
sermons.verdict: Scripture is God-breathed. Continue in it.

sermons.title: Preach the Word, Finish the Race
sermons.idea: With the appearing and the kingdom in view, Paul charges Timothy to preach the word in season and out of season, because a time is coming when people will not endure sound teaching, and then the apostle looks at his own end without flinching: he has fought the good fight, finished the race, kept the faith, and a crown of righteousness waits from the righteous Judge.
sermons.verdict: I have kept the faith. Preach.

3-john.title: Hospitality and the Truth: Preaching 3 John
3-john.headline: A short letter about who you let in, and who has to be first.
3-john.bigIdea: The truth is not only believed; it is hosted. 3 John measures a church not by its doctrine on paper but by whom it receives, whom it sends, and who it lets sit at the head of the table. Gaius supports the workers who carry the Name; Diotrephes guards his own seat and shuts the door; Demetrius is simply trusted. John writes to a congregation to say that love and truth are the same act, and that act looks like an open house.
3-john.christConnection: The traveling teachers went out for the sake of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles, and those who supported them became fellow workers for the truth. Christ is the Name they carried and the truth they served, so that an act as ordinary as feeding a stranger and funding his next leg becomes participation in the mission of the Son who was himself received by some and refused by others.

sermons.title: The Open House
sermons.idea: To support those who go out for the Name is to become a fellow worker for the truth, so that love practiced as hospitality is itself the doing of the truth.
sermons.verdict: Fellow workers, or merely audience.

sermons.title: Who Has to Be First
sermons.idea: Diotrephes loves the first place and shuts the door; Demetrius has the testimony of everyone and of the truth itself; the church is told to imitate good and not evil, because what you imitate reveals whose you are.
sermons.verdict: Imitate the good. Refuse the seat.

acts.title: The Acts of the Risen Christ
acts.headline: How the church was carried from one room in Jerusalem to the heart of the empire
acts.bigIdea: Luke writes not the acts of brave men but the continuing acts of the ascended Jesus, who pours out his Spirit and drives a witness that no council, no prison, and no shipwreck can stop, from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
acts.christConnection: The risen and ascended Christ is the real actor in Acts, building his church by the Holy Spirit he poured out at Pentecost. Every conversion, every council, every chain is the work of the Lord who promised that the gates of hell would not prevail.

sermons.title: What Jesus Began to Do
sermons.idea: The risen Christ ascends as enthroned Lord and tells his witnesses to wait, because the mission belongs to the Spirit he will send, not to the strength or schedule of the men who carry it.
sermons.verdict: Wait. The mission is his.

sermons.title: This Jesus God Raised Up
sermons.idea: At Pentecost the ascended Christ pours out the promised Spirit, and Peter preaches that the crucified Jesus is now Lord and Christ, so that the only fit response to the resurrection is repentance and faith.
sermons.verdict: The Lord you killed now reigns.

sermons.title: In the Name He Walks
sermons.idea: The healing of the lame man is a sign that the name of the risen Jesus carries the power he once carried in the flesh, and the boldness of unschooled men before the council comes from having been with him.
sermons.verdict: We cannot stop speaking him.

sermons.title: You Have Not Lied to Men
sermons.idea: The church that shares everything is also the church where Ananias and Sapphira die for a managed lie, because the Spirit who fills the body will not be performed for, and the apostles refuse to trade the word of God for the work of tables.
sermons.verdict: God is not your audience.

sermons.title: I See the Heavens Opened
sermons.idea: Stephen reads Israel's whole history as a record of resisting the Spirit and rejecting the Righteous One, and his death under the stones, praying for his killers, shows the church its first martyr looking on the standing Son of Man.
sermons.verdict: The witness dies still seeing.

sermons.title: Scattered, and Still Preaching
sermons.idea: The persecution that scatters the church does not silence it but spreads it into Samaria and to the Ethiopian on the desert road, so that the gospel crosses the first walls and the eunuch goes home rejoicing.
sermons.verdict: Scattering is how it spreads.

sermons.title: Why Do You Persecute Me
sermons.idea: Saul the persecutor is stopped on the Damascus road by the Lord he was hunting, and his conversion proves that the risen Christ takes his fiercest enemy and makes him the chosen instrument to carry the name he hated.
sermons.verdict: Grace seizes its worst enemy.

sermons.title: What God Has Cleansed
sermons.idea: Through Cornelius and Peter's vision God tears down the wall between Jew and Gentile, pouring out the same Spirit on the uncircumcised, so the church must confess that he shows no partiality and grants repentance unto life to the nations.
sermons.verdict: God has no second class.

sermons.title: By Grace, the Same Way
sermons.idea: The Jerusalem Council settles whether Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved and rules that all are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus alone, guarding the gospel from the law that would add a condition to faith.
sermons.verdict: Grace alone, or no gospel.

sermons.title: The Lord Opened Her Heart
sermons.idea: Called across to Macedonia, Paul sees the gospel take root in Philippi through a wealthy woman, a slave girl, and a jailer, showing that the Lord himself opens hearts and that even a midnight prison becomes a place of worship.
sermons.verdict: He opens what we cannot.

sermons.title: The God You Worship Unknowing
sermons.idea: In Athens Paul confronts the philosophers not by borrowing their gods but by announcing the Creator who commands all men everywhere to repent because he has fixed a day of judgment by the man he raised from the dead.
sermons.verdict: Now he commands repentance everywhere.

sermons.title: The Word Prevailed Mightily
sermons.idea: In Ephesus the word of the Lord grows against magic books and a silversmith's riot, exposing that the gospel does not merely add to a culture's gods but dethrones them, and the city's idol trade rises up because its trade is threatened.
sermons.verdict: His word burns false gods.

sermons.title: I Stand on Trial for Hope
sermons.idea: Arrested in Jerusalem and held through trial after trial, Paul turns every defense into testimony, telling and retelling the risen Christ before mobs, governors, and a king, because the chain is not an interruption of the mission but the pulpit of it.
sermons.verdict: The chain becomes the pulpit.

sermons.title: And So We Came to Rome
sermons.idea: Through storm, shipwreck, and a viper God keeps his word to bring Paul to Rome, where the apostle preaches the kingdom of God and the Lord Jesus with all boldness and unhindered, so that the book ends not at a wall but with an open door.
sermons.verdict: Nothing stops the open word.

amos.title: Amos: The God Who Will Not Look Away
amos.headline: An expository series through the prophet who measured a comfortable nation against the plumb line and found the wall leaning.
amos.bigIdea: The God who knows a people most intimately holds them most accountable, and no amount of religion, prosperity, or sacrifice will buy back a nation that has traded justice for its own ease.
amos.christConnection: When Amos ends, the wreckage of the house of David lies open to the sky, and God promises to raise the fallen booth and repair its breaches. That ruined and restored shelter is finished in Jesus, the Son of David, whose risen body becomes the place where the nations are gathered in, exactly as James reads it at Jerusalem.

sermons.title: The Roar That Comes Home
