sermons.idea: God indicts the surrounding nations for atrocities they knew were wrong, then turns the same judgment on Judah and Israel for sins the chosen people thought their election excused, so the lion's roar that began at the borders ends in the sanctuary.
sermons.verdict: The roar circles back to you.

sermons.title: Known, Therefore Accountable
sermons.idea: Israel mistook God's choosing for God's leniency, but to be known by God is to be answerable to God, and the same covenant intimacy that made them a people becomes the ground on which He visits their iniquities and the worship at Bethel becomes the sin He punishes.
sermons.verdict: Election is not a shield.

sermons.title: Let Justice Roll
sermons.idea: God rejects the feasts, songs, and offerings of a people who crush the poor at the gate, refusing the worship of hands stained by injustice and demanding instead that justice run down like waters and righteousness like a never-failing stream.
sermons.verdict: He hates your stolen worship.

sermons.title: At Ease in Zion
sermons.idea: Woe falls on those who lie on beds of ivory, feast on the choicest meat, and sing idle songs while they are not grieved over the ruin of God's people, for a comfort that feels nothing for the broken is itself the sin God will overturn.
sermons.verdict: Comfort that feels nothing condemns.

sermons.title: The Plumb Line and the Priest
sermons.idea: God shows Amos visions that measure Israel against His own straight standard and finds the wall past saving, and when the prophet says it plainly the priest Amaziah tells him to take his words elsewhere, so the rejection of the messenger seals the famine of hearing the word.
sermons.verdict: Silence the prophet, starve the land.

sermons.title: The Fallen Booth Raised
sermons.idea: After judgment leaves no sinner of Israel to escape, God refuses to make a full end, promising to raise up the fallen booth of David, repair its breaches, and plant His people again so securely that they will never be uprooted.
sermons.verdict: Out of ruin, He rebuilds.

colossians.title: All Things Hold Together: An Exposition of Colossians
colossians.headline: A church Paul never met, threatened by a fuller gospel that was no gospel at all, and one letter that answers every counterfeit with a single name.
colossians.bigIdea: Christ is supreme over all creation and all-sufficient for salvation, so the church that has received Him needs nothing added to Him and lives the whole of life from union with Him.
colossians.christConnection: Colossians places Christ above every power, principle, and religious supplement the world can offer: the image of the invisible God in whom all the fullness dwells, in whom all things hold together, in whom the believer is already complete. To add anything to Him is to lose Him; to have Him is to have everything.

sermons.title: The Gospel That Bears Fruit
sermons.idea: Paul gives thanks because the same gospel that came to Colossae is bearing fruit and growing in the whole world and in them, and he prays not for ease but for knowledge of God's will worked out in a life worthy of the Lord.
sermons.verdict: The gospel grows where it lands.

sermons.title: The Image of the Invisible God
sermons.idea: Christ is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation, the one in whom all things were created and in whom all things hold together, and through His blood on the cross He reconciles all things to God, including the people once alienated and hostile in mind.
sermons.verdict: In Him all things hold together.

sermons.title: Christ in You, the Hope of Glory
sermons.idea: Paul labors and suffers to make known the mystery hidden for ages and now revealed, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory, and his struggle is that the church would be knit together in love and assured of every treasure of wisdom and knowledge hidden in Christ alone.
sermons.verdict: The mystery has a name.

sermons.title: Rooted, Built Up, and Complete
sermons.idea: Because believers have received Christ Jesus the Lord and are filled in Him who is the head over every power, they must be rooted and built up in Him and not taken captive by hollow philosophy, legal observance, or self-made religion, which have an appearance of wisdom but no power against the flesh.
sermons.verdict: You are complete in Him.

sermons.title: Seek the Things Above
sermons.idea: Since believers have been raised with Christ and their life is now hidden with Christ in God, they are to set their minds above, put to death what belongs to the old self, and put on the new self where Christ is all and in all, letting His peace rule and His word dwell richly among them.
sermons.verdict: Set your mind above.

sermons.title: The Lordship of Christ in House and Prayer
sermons.idea: The supremacy of Christ reaches into the ordinary relationships of household and labor, where every duty is rendered as to the Lord and not to people, and it sustains a life of watchful, thankful prayer and clear witness toward outsiders, sealed by the names of real coworkers who carried the gospel together.
sermons.verdict: Whatever you do, do it for Him.

daniel.title: Daniel: Faithful Under an Empire That Owns the World
daniel.headline: A captive people, a sovereign God, and a kingdom no power can end
daniel.bigIdea: Daniel insists that the God of Israel rules the rise and fall of every empire, that he keeps his people faithful in the furnace of pagan power, and that the future belongs not to Babylon or any kingdom of men but to one like a son of man whose dominion will never pass away.
daniel.christConnection: The one like a son of man who comes on the clouds in Daniel 7, receiving an everlasting dominion that will never be destroyed, is the figure Jesus claims as his own before the high priest, the King in whom the indestructible kingdom of God arrives. The stone cut without hands that shatters the statue and fills the earth is that same kingdom, established by Christ and certain to outlast every empire.

sermons.title: The King's Food and the Faithful Refusal
sermons.idea: Carried into Babylon and pressed into the king's service, Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the royal food, and God gives him favor, wisdom, and a witness that survives the empire's attempt to remake him.
sermons.verdict: Exile did not own them.

sermons.title: The Statue, the Stone, and the Kingdom That Will Not End
sermons.idea: God alone reveals the king's dream of a statue of declining metals, naming the succession of empires and the stone cut without hands that shatters them all and becomes a mountain filling the earth.
sermons.verdict: His kingdom outlasts every empire.

sermons.title: The Furnace and the Fourth Man
sermons.idea: Standing before the golden image, the three refuse to bow even if God does not deliver them, and the God they trust meets them in the fire and brings them out untouched.
sermons.verdict: Even if not, we will not bow.

sermons.title: The King Humbled Until He Knew Heaven Rules
sermons.idea: Warned in a dream and unbroken by his glory, Nebuchadnezzar is driven from his throne to live like a beast until he lifts his eyes and confesses that the Most High rules the kingdom of men.
sermons.verdict: Heaven rules. The proud are brought low.

sermons.title: The Writing on the Wall
sermons.idea: Belshazzar profanes the holy vessels at his feast, and a hand writes his sentence on the plaster: weighed in the balance, found wanting, his kingdom given to another that very night.
sermons.verdict: You have been weighed and found wanting.

sermons.title: The Lions' Den and the Window Left Open
sermons.idea: Trapped by a law against prayer, Daniel kneels at his open window as he always has, and the God he serves continually shuts the mouths of the lions.
sermons.verdict: He kept praying with the window open.

sermons.title: The Four Beasts and the Son of Man
sermons.idea: In a night vision the beastly empires rise from the chaotic sea, but the Ancient of Days takes his seat in judgment and gives everlasting dominion to one like a son of man.
sermons.verdict: Dominion that will never pass away.

sermons.title: The Ram, the Goat, and the Prayer of a Broken People
sermons.idea: The visions of the ram and goat name the empires to come and the desolation of the sanctuary, and Daniel answers by confessing his people's sin and pleading on the ground of God's mercy alone.
sermons.verdict: We have sinned. He is righteous.

sermons.title: Those Who Are Wise Shall Shine
sermons.idea: The final vision unveils the conflict behind history, a time of trouble unlike any before, and the promise of resurrection in which the wise who turn many to righteousness shall shine like the stars forever.
sermons.verdict: Go your way. You shall rise.

deuteronomy.title: The Second Telling: Preaching Through Deuteronomy
deuteronomy.headline: A whole generation stands at the edge of the land, and Moses tells them everything again before they cross without him.
deuteronomy.bigIdea: Deuteronomy is covenant renewal on the plains of Moab. A people who failed in the wilderness are summoned to love the LORD with everything they are, to remember what He has done, and to obey before they possess the land they did not earn.
deuteronomy.christConnection: Moses promises a Prophet like himself whom God will raise up, and dies looking at a land he may not enter. The law he delivers exposes a people who cannot keep it and a heart that must be circumcised by God Himself. Christ is the Prophet greater than Moses, the obedient Son who kept the covenant Israel broke, who bore its curse on the tree so its blessing could reach a people who deserved its judgment.

sermons.title: The Sermon Before the Crossing
sermons.idea: Moses retells the wilderness years so a new generation will read their own history rightly: God was faithful, the fathers were faithless, and the One who acts in history alone is to be worshiped without image or rival.
sermons.verdict: Remember who actually kept faith.

sermons.title: Keep Your Soul Diligently
sermons.idea: Because Israel saw no form at Horeb, only heard a voice, they must guard against making God into anything they can carve, and teach their children that the LORD is God in heaven and on earth and there is no other.
sermons.verdict: You heard a voice. Make nothing.

sermons.title: The Ten Words Again
sermons.idea: The covenant at Horeb was not made only with the fathers but with the living congregation standing here today, and the same God who redeemed them from Egypt commands their whole life in response.
sermons.verdict: This covenant is with you, now.

sermons.title: Hear, O Israel
sermons.idea: The LORD is one, and the only fitting response to the one God is love with all heart, soul, and strength, a love so total it is repeated to children, bound to the hands, and spoken at every threshold of the day.
sermons.verdict: Love Him with everything you are.

sermons.title: Set Apart and Few
sermons.idea: God did not choose Israel because they were great but because He loved them and kept His oath, and that undeserved love demands they refuse the idols of the nations and the marriages that would lead them away.
sermons.verdict: He loved you. Do not forget it.

sermons.title: Do Not Forget in the Plenty
sermons.idea: The wilderness humbled Israel to teach them that man lives by every word from God, and the real danger is not the desert but the good land, where full barns tempt the heart to say my own hand made this wealth.
sermons.verdict: Abundance is the harder test.

sermons.title: Not Because of Your Righteousness
sermons.idea: Israel will enter the land not by their own goodness but in spite of their stubbornness, the golden calf still fresh in memory, and the God who pardoned them now asks only that they fear, love, and circumcise their hearts.
sermons.verdict: You are not the righteous ones here.

sermons.title: Blessing and Curse Set Before You
sermons.idea: The generation that saw God's mighty works with their own eyes is bound to obey, and the land itself, watered by heaven rather than by their labor, will answer their obedience or disobedience with blessing or curse.
sermons.verdict: You saw it. Now choose.

sermons.title: One Place, One Worship
sermons.idea: God will choose the place where His name dwells, and Israel must not worship Him however the nations worship their gods nor follow any prophet, however persuasive, who calls them after other gods.
sermons.verdict: Worship God on His terms only.

sermons.title: A Holy People and a Holy Year
sermons.idea: Holiness reaches into the table, the tithe, the seventh year of release, and the freed slave, so that Israel's distinct life remembers the poor, releases the debtor, and keeps the feasts that rehearse their redemption.
sermons.verdict: Holiness shows up at the table.

sermons.title: The King Who Reads, the Prophet Who Comes
sermons.idea: Israel's offices are bound under the word: the king must write out the law and not lift himself above his brothers, and God will raise up a Prophet like Moses whom the people must heed.
sermons.verdict: A Prophet like Moses is coming.

sermons.title: Blood, War, and the Unsolved Death
sermons.idea: Justice in the land guards the innocent through cities of refuge and honest witnesses, restrains even warfare, and refuses to leave an unsolved murder unanswered, because innocent blood defiles the land God gave.
sermons.verdict: Innocent blood is never ignored.

sermons.title: The Law in the Ordinary Day
sermons.idea: The covenant governs the lost ox, the wage of the poor, the weight in the bag, and the dignity of the vulnerable, because love of God is proven in how a neighbor is treated when no one is watching.
sermons.verdict: Covenant lives in small justice.

sermons.title: The Wandering Aramean
sermons.idea: When Israel brings the firstfruits, they confess their whole story aloud, that their father was a wandering Aramean and the LORD brought them out with a mighty hand, so worship becomes remembered grace returned in gratitude.
sermons.verdict: Confess the story when you give.

sermons.title: The Blessing and the Curse
sermons.idea: Standing between Gerizim and Ebal, Israel hears that obedience brings blessing on body, field, and city, but the curses for forsaking the covenant are longer and heavier, exile and dread, a warning that the people will not finally keep.
sermons.verdict: The curse outweighs what we can carry.

sermons.title: Circumcise the Heart
sermons.idea: The covenant is sworn with this generation and those not yet born, and though Moses foresees their failure and exile, he promises a return when God Himself will circumcise their hearts to love Him, for the word is near, in the mouth and heart.
sermons.verdict: God must change the heart Himself.

sermons.title: Be Strong, for Moses Will Not Cross
sermons.idea: Moses hands leadership to Joshua and writes the law down, and God tells him plainly that the people will turn aside, so the song is given as a witness against them when they do.
sermons.verdict: He knew we would turn aside.

sermons.title: The Song of Moses
sermons.idea: Moses sings of a faithful Rock and a faithless people, of the God who found Jacob in a desert and fed him only to be forsaken, and yet vindicates His name and atones for the land and the people in the end.
sermons.verdict: The Rock is faithful. We are not.

sermons.title: The Blessing of Moses
sermons.idea: Before he dies, Moses blesses the tribes one by one, the man of God speaking grace over a flawed people, declaring there is none like the God of Jeshurun who rides the heavens to their help.
sermons.verdict: He blessed them on his way out.

sermons.title: The Death of Moses
sermons.idea: Moses climbs Nebo, sees the whole land he may not enter, and dies at the LORD's word, buried by God in a grave no one knows, and no prophet has arisen like him whom the LORD knew face to face.
sermons.verdict: He saw the land and died outside.

ecclesiastes.title: Under the Sun: Preaching Through Ecclesiastes
ecclesiastes.headline: What life weighs when you finally stop pretending it weighs nothing.
ecclesiastes.bigIdea: Ecclesiastes refuses every easy answer the world hands a person about meaning, and drives the reader to the only ground that holds: a God who must be feared, obeyed, and trusted with the days we cannot control.
ecclesiastes.christConnection: The Preacher exhausts every road under the sun and finds each one a dead end, and that exhaustion is the soil where the gospel grows. The one who fears God and keeps his commandments is the verdict Ecclesiastes leaves unfulfilled, and it is fulfilled in Christ, who kept the commandments we broke, became vanity for us on a cross outside the city, and rose to give the toil of our hands a meaning the sun could never reach.

sermons.title: Vanity of Vanities
sermons.idea: The Preacher surveys all that happens under the sun and declares it a vapor, because a closed world without God offers no gain that the grave does not erase.
sermons.verdict: Everything under the sun passes.

sermons.title: The Test of Pleasure and Wisdom
sermons.idea: The Preacher gives himself every pleasure, every work, and every wisdom a man can build, and discovers that the wise and the fool share one grave, so that enjoyment of the ordinary comes only as a gift from the hand of God.
sermons.verdict: You cannot keep what you build.

sermons.title: A Time for Everything
sermons.idea: God has set every season in its place and put eternity in the human heart, yet hidden the whole of his work, so that the right posture is reverent acceptance of times we did not appoint and cannot read.
sermons.verdict: You are not the timekeeper.

sermons.title: The Loneliness of Toil
sermons.idea: Under the sun the Preacher sees oppression without a comforter, labor driven by envy, and the solitary man who heaps up riches for no one, and he commends companionship as the small mercy that steadies a life otherwise spent alone.
sermons.verdict: No man should toil alone.

sermons.title: Guard Your Steps to the House of God
sermons.idea: Because God is in heaven and we are on earth, worship demands few words and kept vows, and the love of money never satisfies, so that the one who fears God receives his work and his bread as a portion to be enjoyed, not hoarded.
sermons.verdict: Fear God. Keep your vows.

sermons.title: The Wealth a Man Cannot Enjoy
sermons.idea: God may give a man riches and honor and yet withhold the power to enjoy them, exposing the futility of appetite that is never filled and reminding us that no one knows what is good or what comes after.
sermons.verdict: Having is not the same as enjoying.

sermons.title: The Limits of Wisdom
sermons.idea: Wisdom is better than folly and a house of mourning teaches what a house of feasting cannot, yet even wisdom cannot make crooked things straight or find out the deep scheme of God, so the wise person fears God and refuses both extremes.
sermons.verdict: Wisdom knows what it cannot know.

sermons.title: Remember Your Creator
sermons.idea: Because the future is uncertain and the days of darkness are many, the Preacher calls the young to sow generously, rejoice with sober joy, and remember their Creator before the body fails and the dust returns to the ground.
sermons.verdict: Remember him before the dark.

sermons.title: The End of the Matter
sermons.idea: When every road under the sun has been walked to its end, the whole duty of man stands plain: fear God and keep his commandments, for God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing.
sermons.verdict: Fear God. Keep his commandments.

ephesians.title: Seated, Sent, and Standing: An Expository Series Through Ephesians
ephesians.headline: Six chapters that move from the heights of heaven to the ground of a marriage, a household, and a battle line.
ephesians.bigIdea: God chose, redeemed, and made alive a people for himself in Christ, and that people now walks worthy of the calling by which it was called.
ephesians.christConnection: In Christ the Father gathers all things in heaven and on earth into one, and the church is his body and his bride, raised with him and seated with him to display the wisdom of God. Every command in the second half of the letter rests on what Christ has already done in the first.

sermons.title: Blessed With Every Blessing
sermons.idea: The Father has chosen, the Son has redeemed, and the Spirit has sealed a people for the praise of God's glory, so that every spiritual blessing the believer needs is already his in Christ.
sermons.verdict: Nothing was left for you to earn.

sermons.title: The Prayer for Open Eyes
sermons.idea: Paul prays not for new blessings but for sight, that the church would know the hope, the inheritance, and the power that raised Christ from the dead and seated him over all things as head of his body.
sermons.verdict: You already have what you cannot see.

sermons.title: Dead, Then Alive
sermons.idea: We were dead in our trespasses and by nature children of wrath, but God, rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ by grace through faith, that no one would boast and that we would walk in the works he prepared.
sermons.verdict: Grace from first breath to last.

sermons.title: The Wall Came Down
sermons.idea: The blood of Christ has brought near those who were far off and broken the dividing wall of hostility, making one new man out of the two and building both into a single dwelling for God by the Spirit.
sermons.verdict: Two peoples, one body, no wall.

sermons.title: The Mystery and the Power
sermons.idea: The mystery hidden for ages, that Gentiles are fellow heirs in one body, is now made known through the church to display God's wisdom, and Paul bows to ask that this people be strengthened to grasp a love beyond knowledge.
sermons.verdict: The church is God's wisdom on display.

sermons.title: Walk Worthy, Grow Up
sermons.idea: Called to one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, and one God, the church keeps its unity while the ascended Christ gives gifts to equip the saints, that the whole body grows up into him.
sermons.verdict: Unity is kept, not built.

sermons.title: Off With the Old, On With the New
sermons.idea: Because they were taught Christ, believers put off the old self with its corruption and put on the new self created after God, walking now in love and in light and being filled with the Spirit rather than the life they left.
sermons.verdict: You are not who you were.

sermons.title: Christ and the Church at Home
sermons.idea: The mystery of Christ and his church reshapes the home, as husbands love as Christ loved and gave himself, wives respond, children obey, fathers do not provoke, and masters and servants answer to the same Lord above.
sermons.verdict: The gospel reaches the kitchen table.

sermons.title: Standing in the Strength of the Lord
sermons.idea: The battle is not against flesh and blood but against spiritual powers, so the church puts on the whole armor of God, stands in his strength rather than its own, and prays at all times in the Spirit.
sermons.verdict: Stand. The strength is his.

esther.title: The God Who Is Not Named: Preaching Through Esther
esther.headline: A book that never says God, written so you cannot miss Him
esther.bigIdea: In a foreign court where God is never named and prayer is never recorded, the survival of His covenant people is secured by a chain of coincidences too precise to be coincidence, teaching the church to read the hidden providence of God in the rooms where He seems absent.
esther.christConnection: Esther rises to a throne not her own and risks her life to stand between her condemned people and a king's lethal decree, a queen who says, in effect, if I perish I perish. The deliverance she wins is partial, bloody, and bought at her own exposure. It points past itself to a greater Mediator who entered a court not His own, did perish for His people, and reversed not one decree but the sentence of death itself. The empty mention of God in Esther is filled at the cross, where the hidden God is named and shown.

sermons.title: The Empire That Could Not Command a Wife
sermons.idea: At the height of a 180-day display of his own glory, the most powerful man in the world cannot make his queen come when he calls, and the empire's response exposes a kingdom that is mighty over nations and helpless over a single human heart.
sermons.verdict: Power that rules everything but the heart.

sermons.title: A Jewish Girl in the King's Bed
sermons.idea: Esther is taken into a pagan harem, hides her people, and wins a crown, and the narrator records it without protest or applause, refusing to sanitize how God's purposes move through compromise, danger, and rooms His people would not have chosen.
sermons.verdict: He works where we would not look.

sermons.title: The Price of One Man's Pride
sermons.idea: Because Mordecai will not bow, Haman secures a decree to exterminate every Jew in the empire on a date chosen by the casting of lots, and the death of a whole people is purchased, sealed, and dropped into the imperial mail while the king sits down to drink.
sermons.verdict: Hatred always asks for everyone.

sermons.title: For Such a Time as This
sermons.idea: Mordecai tells Esther that deliverance for the Jews will come whether she acts or not, but that her position is not an accident and her silence will not save her, and Esther steps toward the king's throne, and possibly her death, with the words if I perish I perish.
sermons.verdict: Your place is not an accident.

sermons.title: The Night the King Could Not Sleep
sermons.idea: Esther's risk, Haman's gallows, and a king's sleepless night converge through a chain of small reversals no one engineered, until the man who built a stake for Mordecai is hanged on it himself, and the hidden hand behind every coincidence becomes impossible to deny.
sermons.verdict: The unnamed God runs the room.

sermons.title: The Decree That Could Not Be Revoked
sermons.idea: The first decree cannot be undone, so a second is written giving the condemned the right to defend their lives, and deliverance comes not by erasing the danger but by arming the threatened to stand, a costly and bloody rescue won inside the very law that doomed them.
sermons.verdict: Rescue inside the law that condemned.

sermons.title: A Feast for the People Who Should Be Dead
sermons.idea: The Jews establish Purim, a permanent feast named after the lots cast for their destruction, turning the day of their planned extinction into annual remembrance, so that a people who were marked for death keep a calendar built on a deliverance their God never signed His name to but never stopped working.
sermons.verdict: Remember the rescue you did not earn.

exodus.title: The God Who Comes Down
exodus.headline: How the LORD remembers a forgotten people, breaks the power that owns them, and binds them to himself
exodus.bigIdea: Exodus is the account of how the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob hears the cry of enslaved Israel, defeats the gods and king of Egypt by his own outstretched arm, and brings his people out so that he might dwell among them as their covenant LORD. Redemption is not the end of the story; the God who delivers a people is the God who comes to live with them.
exodus.christConnection: The exodus is the Old Testament's deepest pattern of salvation: a lamb whose blood turns away death, a people ransomed from bondage, a mediator who stands between God and sinners, and a holy presence that fills the tent. Christ is the true Passover Lamb, the greater Moses, and the God who tabernacles among us, accomplishing at the cross the deliverance Egypt only foreshadowed.

sermons.title: When the King Forgets and God Remembers
sermons.idea: While a new Pharaoh who does not know Joseph crushes a multiplying Israel and orders her sons drowned, God quietly preserves a deliverer and hears the groaning of his people.
sermons.verdict: The empire forgets. God remembers.

sermons.title: The Bush That Would Not Burn Up
sermons.idea: At the burning bush the LORD reveals his name and his resolve to deliver Israel, and overrides every excuse Moses raises until the reluctant shepherd goes back to Egypt.
sermons.verdict: He sends the man who runs.

sermons.title: It Gets Worse Before It Gets Out
sermons.idea: When Moses first demands release, Pharaoh hardens the labor and Israel turns on her deliverer, but God answers despair by repeating his covenant name and promising to act so that all will know he is the LORD.
sermons.verdict: Delay is not abandonment.

sermons.title: War Against the Gods of Egypt
sermons.idea: Through escalating plagues the LORD exposes Egypt's gods as powerless and hardens Pharaoh's heart, so that Israel and Egypt alike will know there is no one like the God of the Hebrews.
sermons.verdict: Every false god finally falls.

sermons.title: Death Passes Over the Blood
sermons.idea: On the night the firstborn of Egypt die, the blood of a spotless lamb shields Israel's houses, and the LORD commands them to keep this meal forever as the memory of how he redeemed them.
sermons.verdict: Blood stands between you and judgment.

sermons.title: The Sea That Opened and Closed
sermons.idea: Hemmed in between Pharaoh's army and the sea, Israel is told to stand still and watch the LORD fight, and he drowns Egypt's might in the waters his people walk through on dry ground.
sermons.verdict: Stand still and be saved.

sermons.title: Bread From Heaven, Water From the Rock
sermons.idea: In the wilderness a grumbling, thirsty, threatened Israel learns that the God who redeemed them will also provide their bread, their water, and their victory, testing whether they will trust him day by day.
sermons.verdict: The Redeemer is also the Provider.

sermons.title: The Mountain That Burned and Shook
sermons.idea: Having carried Israel to himself on eagles' wings, the LORD descends on Sinai in fire and speaks the Ten Words, claiming a redeemed people as his treasured possession and kingdom of priests.
sermons.verdict: Grace came first, then law.

sermons.title: The Book of the Covenant, Sealed in Blood
sermons.idea: The LORD gives Israel just laws for ordinary life and then ratifies the covenant with blood and a shared meal in his presence, binding the people to obey all he has spoken.
sermons.verdict: A covenant sealed with blood.

sermons.title: A Tent for the God Who Will Not Leave
sermons.idea: In meticulous detail the LORD designs a tabernacle, priesthood, and sabbath so that the holy God may dwell in the midst of an unholy people without consuming them.
sermons.verdict: He plans a place to dwell.

sermons.title: The Golden Calf and the Glory That Stayed
sermons.idea: While Moses is on the mountain Israel breaks the covenant with a golden calf, and the LORD, threatening to go no farther, relents at the mediator's pleading and reveals himself as merciful and just.
sermons.verdict: Mercy that does not excuse sin.

sermons.title: And the Glory Filled the Tent
sermons.idea: The people build the tabernacle exactly as commanded, and when the work is finished the cloud descends and the glory of the LORD fills it, so that God now travels in the midst of his redeemed people.
sermons.verdict: God came down to stay.

ezekiel.title: The Glory That Leaves and Returns
ezekiel.headline: Exile, Glory, and the God Who Will Not Stay Gone
ezekiel.bigIdea: Ezekiel watches the glory of God depart a doomed temple and then promises it will return to a city renamed for God's presence, so the whole book moves from judgment that is deserved to restoration that is sovereign and undeserved.
ezekiel.christConnection: The true Shepherd of Ezekiel 34 who comes to seek the scattered and feed them himself is fulfilled in Jesus, who calls himself the good shepherd, and the new heart and new spirit promised in Ezekiel 36 are given through his death and Spirit, so that the presence named at the end, 'The LORD is there,' becomes Immanuel, God with us.

sermons.title: The Glory by the River Chebar
sermons.idea: In exile, far from the temple, God appears to Ezekiel in overwhelming glory and commissions him as a prophet to a rebellious house, making him eat the scroll of lament before he speaks a word.
sermons.verdict: God finds you in exile.

sermons.title: The Watchman's Blood
sermons.idea: God appoints Ezekiel a watchman whose duty is to warn, holding him accountable for the silence that lets people die unwarned, while leaving each person responsible for their own response.
sermons.verdict: Warn them, or their blood answers.

sermons.title: The Siege Acted Out
sermons.idea: God commands Ezekiel to perform the coming siege of Jerusalem with brick, iron pan, and shaved hair, turning the prophet's own body into the sermon so a numb people might finally see what is coming.
sermons.verdict: The judgment is no longer abstract.

sermons.title: The Glory Departs
sermons.idea: Shown the hidden idolatry inside the temple itself, Ezekiel watches the glory of God lift from the cherubim, move to the threshold, and finally leave the city, exposing the worship that remained as an empty shell.
sermons.verdict: The worst judgment is God leaving.

sermons.title: The Soul That Sins
sermons.idea: Against the proverb blaming the fathers, God insists each person answers for their own life, the wicked who turn will live and the righteous who fall will die, because God takes no pleasure in the death of anyone.
sermons.verdict: Turn, and live.

sermons.title: The Shepherds Who Fed Themselves
sermons.idea: God indicts the shepherds of Israel who fattened themselves while the flock was scattered and devoured, and announces that he himself will come to seek, gather, and feed his sheep, setting one Shepherd over them.
sermons.verdict: The owner is coming for his sheep.

sermons.title: A New Heart and a New Spirit
sermons.idea: For the sake of his own holy name, not Israel's merit, God promises to cleanse his people, remove the heart of stone, give a heart of flesh, and put his Spirit within them so they finally walk in his ways.
sermons.verdict: He gives what he commands.

sermons.title: The Valley of Dry Bones
sermons.idea: In a valley of bones long dead, God commands Ezekiel to prophesy, and his word with his breath raises a slaughtered army to its feet, proving that even a people who say their hope is lost can be brought from the grave.
sermons.verdict: These bones can live again.

sermons.title: Gog and the End of the Threat
sermons.idea: God summons Gog against his restored and unsuspecting people only to defeat him utterly, demonstrating that no final enemy can undo the restoration God has secured for his name and his flock.
sermons.verdict: No enemy outlasts God's people.

sermons.title: The Glory Returns to the Temple
sermons.idea: In a vision of a measured new temple, Ezekiel sees the glory of God return by the same eastern way it left, filling the house, so that the presence that departed in judgment comes back to dwell.
sermons.verdict: The glory that left returns.

sermons.title: The River and the Name of the City
sermons.idea: From under the temple threshold flows a river that deepens and heals everything it touches, and the book ends naming the city 'The LORD is there,' resolving the whole vision in the restored presence of God.
sermons.verdict: The LORD is there.

ezra.title: The God Who Brings a Remnant Home
ezra.headline: An expository walk through Ezra: the hand of God moving kings, rebuilding worship, and reforming a people who keep forgetting why they returned
ezra.bigIdea: Ezra tells how God kept covenant with a scattered people by stirring pagan kings, restoring true worship at the temple, and confronting His remnant with the holiness their return demanded. Restoration is His work from start to finish, and it always aims at a people set apart for Him.
ezra.christConnection: The temple Ezra rebuilds is a shadow of the true dwelling of God with man. The remnant brought back from exile points to the greater return from a deeper captivity, accomplished not by a decree of Cyrus but by the Lord Himself coming in flesh. Where Ezra's reform could only separate the people from foreign wives, Christ cleanses His bride from within and presents her holy, the dwelling place of God by the Spirit.

sermons.title: The King's Heart in the Hand of God
sermons.idea: The Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus to fulfill His word through Jeremiah, releasing the exiles to rebuild His house, and the named remnant who answered were those whose spirit God had stirred to go.
sermons.verdict: He moves kings to keep His word.

sermons.title: The Altar Before the Foundation
sermons.idea: The returned remnant built the altar and restored sacrifice before a single stone of the temple was laid, fearing the peoples around them yet refusing to wait, because worship had to come first and the foundation was laid with weeping mixed into the shouting.
sermons.verdict: They built the altar first.

sermons.title: The Work Stops
sermons.idea: When the enemies of Judah were refused a share in the building, they turned to discouragement, hired counselors, and finally a royal decree, until the work on the house of God stopped and stood still by force.
sermons.verdict: Opposition can halt the work.

sermons.title: Prophets, a Letter, and a Finished House
sermons.idea: When Haggai and Zechariah prophesied, the leaders rose and resumed building, and under the eye of God their adversaries' letter to Darius only uncovered the original decree of Cyrus, so the house was finished, dedicated, and the Passover kept with joy.
sermons.verdict: God's eye watched over them.

sermons.title: A Scribe Set in His Heart
sermons.idea: Ezra, a scribe skilled in the Law who had set his heart to study, do, and teach it, went up from Babylon with the good hand of God upon him, and led a second return that trusted God for protection rather than asking the king for soldiers.
sermons.verdict: He set his heart to obey.

sermons.title: The Tears of a Holy Remnant
sermons.idea: When Ezra learned the people had not separated themselves and had taken foreign wives, he tore his garment, confessed the guilt as his own, and the assembly came to a trembling repentance that cost them dearly to make right.
sermons.verdict: Repentance that trembles and costs.

galatians.title: No Other Gospel: An Exposition of Galatians
galatians.headline: Paul wrote Galatians in anger, and the anger was love. A church he planted was trading the gospel of grace for a gospel of performance, and he would not watch it happen quietly. Six chapters, preached in order, that refuse to let righteousness become something we manufacture.
galatians.bigIdea: A person is set right with God through faith in Jesus Christ and not by works of the law, and the freedom that grace gives is not a license to indulge the flesh but the power to walk by the Spirit.
galatians.christConnection: We are justified before God not by anything we perform but by faith in Jesus Christ, who gave himself for our sins. Paul says he has been crucified with Christ, so the life he now lives he lives by the faithfulness of the Son of God who loved him and gave himself for him.

sermons.title: No Other Gospel
sermons.idea: There is only one gospel, given by revelation of Jesus Christ and not invented by men, and any message that adds requirements to grace is not a variation of it but a desertion of it that brings God's curse.
sermons.verdict: Add to grace and lose it.

sermons.title: Justified by Faith, Not Works of the Law
sermons.idea: When Peter withdrew from Gentile believers and forced the gospel to bend toward the law, Paul opposed him to his face, because a person is justified not by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, and to rebuild the law as the ground of acceptance is to nullify the grace of God.
sermons.verdict: If law could save, Christ died needlessly.

sermons.title: Abraham's Blessing and the Curse the Law Could Not Lift
sermons.idea: Abraham was counted righteous by faith before the law was ever given, so the blessing comes to all who believe and not to those who perform, and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us on the tree.
sermons.verdict: Faith receives what works could never earn.

sermons.title: Sons and Heirs, No Longer Slaves
sermons.idea: When the fullness of time had come God sent his Son to redeem those under the law so that we might receive adoption as sons, and the Spirit of the Son in our hearts cries Father, making us heirs of the promise rather than slaves returning to the weak and worthless elemental things.
sermons.verdict: A son does not earn his inheritance.

sermons.title: Free, and Walking by the Spirit
sermons.idea: Christ has set us free for freedom, so we must not submit again to a yoke of slavery, and that freedom is not an opening for the flesh but the room to walk by the Spirit, whose fruit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
sermons.verdict: Freedom serves through love, not self.

sermons.title: Bearing Burdens, Boasting Only in the Cross
sermons.idea: Those who live by the Spirit carry one another's burdens and sow to the Spirit rather than to the flesh, and at the end Paul refuses every ground of boasting except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to him and he to the world.
sermons.verdict: Boast in the cross or boast in nothing.

habakkuk.title: How Long, O Lord: Faith That Wrestles in the Dark
habakkuk.headline: An expository series through Habakkuk on the prophet who argued with God, waited for an answer he hated, and learned to live by faith when the harvest failed.
habakkuk.bigIdea: Habakkuk does not silence the believer's hardest question; it shows a prophet who brings his complaint to God, receives an answer harder than his question, and is taught that the righteous live by faith in the One who is working out a justice slower and deeper than they would have written.
habakkuk.christConnection: The single line at the center of this book, that the righteous shall live by his faith, is the sentence Paul carries into Romans and Galatians and the writer of Hebrews carries into his summons to endure, and in every case it points past Habakkuk to the One whose perfect faithfulness becomes ours. The God who tarries here is the God who would Himself come to drink the cup of judgment we earned, so that the just could live.

sermons.title: How Long, and Why Them
sermons.idea: When the prophet cries out at the violence he sees and God answers that He is raising up the ruthless Babylonians as His instrument, Habakkuk learns that the believer is permitted to bring his complaint to God, and that God's answer is often more troubling than the question, because His justice runs on a depth and a timeline we did not choose.
sermons.verdict: His answer outweighs your question.

sermons.title: The Righteous Shall Live by His Faith
sermons.idea: God tells the prophet to write the vision and wait, declaring that the proud soul is not upright but the righteous shall live by his faith, and then pronouncing five woes on the plunderer, the exploiter, the violent, the drunkard, and the idolater, so that the man who waits learns that God has already seen the end of every injustice and the whole earth will be filled with His glory.
sermons.verdict: The puffed-up fall; the faithful live.

sermons.title: Though the Fig Tree Should Not Blossom
sermons.idea: Habakkuk prays, remembering God's terrible acts of deliverance in the past and asking for mercy in wrath, and arrives at a settled resolve that even if every field is barren and every fold is empty he will rejoice in the Lord, because his joy now rests not on the harvest but on the God of his salvation who makes him walk on the heights.
sermons.verdict: Joy that the harvest cannot give.

haggai.title: Consider Your Ways: Haggai and the House That Waited
haggai.headline: Three sermons on misplaced priorities and the glory God promised to a half-built temple
haggai.bigIdea: Sixteen years after the return from exile, the people of God had finished their own houses and left his in rubble, and through Haggai the Lord called them to build, met their obedience with his presence, and pledged that the latter glory of this house would surpass the first.
haggai.christConnection: The desire of all nations and the glory greater than Solomon's were not exhausted by the second temple but answered in Christ, who walked its courts as the true and final dwelling of God with his people. The signet ring restored to Zerubbabel reverses the judgment on his line and keeps the messianic promise alive until the King is born.

sermons.title: Paneled Houses and a House in Ruins
sermons.idea: When the people excused their neglect of God's house by saying the time had not come, the Lord exposed the lie beneath their comfort: they had time, money, and craftsmanship for paneled houses while his house lay in ruins, and so he commanded them to consider their ways, for the empty harvest and the holes in their pockets were his doing, not the economy's.
sermons.verdict: Your comfort indicts your priorities.

sermons.title: They Obeyed, and I Am With You
sermons.idea: The whole remnant, governor and priest and people together, obeyed the voice of the Lord and feared before him, and into their first act of obedience God spoke the only words that matter, I am with you, and stirred up their spirits so that they came and worked on the house of the Lord their God.
sermons.verdict: Obedience is where his presence meets you.

sermons.title: The Latter Glory and the Signet Ring
sermons.idea: To builders discouraged that their work looked like nothing beside Solomon's temple, the Lord promised that he would shake the nations, fill this house with glory, and make its latter splendor greater than the former, and to Zerubbabel he pledged to make him like a signet ring, reversing the curse on his line and securing the promise that would not fail.
sermons.verdict: The glory you cannot see is coming.

hebrews.title: Better: A Walk Through Hebrews
hebrews.headline: God has spoken by his Son, and there is no going back
hebrews.bigIdea: Hebrews was written to people drifting back toward an old religion because the new one was costing them. The whole letter answers that drift with one word repeated in a hundred ways: better. A better revelation, a better priest, a better covenant, a better sacrifice, a better country. The Son is greater than angels, greater than Moses, greater than Aaron and his sons. The blood of bulls and goats could only point. The blood of Christ finishes. To leave him is not to return to something safe. It is to walk away from the only thing that holds.
hebrews.christConnection: Christ is the Son superior to angels, prophets, Moses, and the Levitical order, the great high priest after the order of Melchizedek who offered himself once for all and sat down. He is the mediator of a better covenant whose single sacrifice does what the blood of bulls and goats never could, and through him alone we draw near.

sermons.title: He Has Spoken by His Son
sermons.idea: God spoke in many fragments through the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken in a Son who is the radiance of his glory and the exact imprint of his nature, and that Son is higher than every angel because he is worshiped, not sent.
sermons.verdict: The Son is no messenger.

sermons.title: Why He Became Lower
sermons.idea: Because the Son was made lower than the angels for a little while to taste death for everyone, sharing flesh and blood to destroy the one who held the power of death, the salvation he brings is too great to drift past and neglect.
sermons.verdict: He was not ashamed of us.

sermons.title: Greater Than the House of Moses
sermons.idea: Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house, but Christ is faithful as a son over it, and the generation that hardened its heart in the wilderness did not fall short of the land for lack of miracles but for lack of belief that endured.
sermons.verdict: Unbelief left their bodies in the desert.

sermons.title: The Rest That Remains
sermons.idea: A Sabbath rest still stands open for the people of God, a rest entered not by works but by faith, and the word that promises it cuts deeper than any sword to expose whether we are resting in Christ or still laboring to save ourselves.
sermons.verdict: Strive, then, to stop striving.

sermons.title: A High Priest Who Was Tempted
sermons.idea: Because Jesus has passed through the heavens as a great high priest who was tested in every way we are yet without sin, learning obedience through what he suffered, we can hold fast our confession and come to the throne of grace with confidence.
sermons.verdict: Hold fast. He understands.

sermons.title: The Warning and the Anchor
sermons.idea: The same letter that warns it is impossible to restore those who fall away after tasting the heavenly gift grounds the believer's assurance not in the strength of his grip but in the oath of God, two unchangeable things, an anchor behind the curtain.
sermons.verdict: The anchor holds inside the veil.

sermons.title: A Priest Forever, After Melchizedek
sermons.idea: Because Christ is a priest after the order of Melchizedek and not of Levi, appointed by an oath and by the power of an indestructible life, he holds his priesthood permanently and is able to save completely those who draw near to God through him.
sermons.verdict: He always lives to intercede.

sermons.title: The Better Covenant
sermons.idea: The first covenant, with its earthly tent and its faults, was only a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, and in promising a new covenant that writes the law on the heart and remembers sin no more, God declared the first one obsolete.
sermons.verdict: He calls the first one old.

sermons.title: Once for All, Not Again and Again
sermons.idea: The blood of goats and bulls could cleanse the flesh but never the conscience, so Christ entered the greater tent not made with hands and offered his own blood once for all, securing an eternal redemption that the yearly ritual could only foreshadow.
sermons.verdict: The blood of bulls could not.

sermons.title: He Sat Down
sermons.idea: Where the priests of old stood daily offering sacrifices that could never take away sins, Christ offered one sacrifice for sins and then sat down, perfecting forever those being made holy, so we draw near with a true heart and do not shrink back.
sermons.verdict: The work is finished. He sat.

sermons.title: By Faith They Saw What Was Promised
sermons.idea: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for and the conviction of things not seen, and the long roll of witnesses from Abel to the prophets shows men and women who obeyed a promise they died without receiving, desiring a better country.
sermons.verdict: They died believing. So will we.

sermons.title: Run, Looking to Jesus
sermons.idea: Surrounded by that great cloud of witnesses, we lay aside every weight and run with endurance the race set before us, fixing our eyes on Jesus and receiving the discipline of a Father who treats us as sons, not as strangers.
sermons.verdict: The discipline proves you are his.

sermons.title: The Same, Yesterday and Forever
sermons.idea: The letter ends where it began, on the unchanging Son, calling us to love one another, to go to him outside the camp bearing his reproach, and to offer the sacrifice of praise, because Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
sermons.verdict: He does not change.

hosea.title: Hosea: The Marriage That Will Not Die
hosea.headline: A prophet ordered to marry a woman who would betray him, so that a nation could see what it had done to its God.
hosea.bigIdea: The covenant between God and his people is a marriage, and Israel has committed adultery against the One who loved her first; yet the offended Husband refuses to release his bride, pursuing her through judgment back into love.
hosea.christConnection: The Hosea who buys back his wandering wife with silver and barley is the shadow of a Bridegroom who would buy back his adulterous people with his own blood. What Hosea could only act out, Christ accomplished, redeeming the unfaithful at the cost of himself.

sermons.title: Go, Take a Wife of Whoredom
sermons.idea: God commands Hosea to marry an unfaithful woman and name their children for judgment, then to buy her back from her degradation, because Israel's idolatry is not a policy failure but adultery against a Husband, and that Husband will not let her go.
sermons.verdict: He bought back what betrayed him.

sermons.title: The LORD Has a Case Against the Land
sermons.idea: God files a lawsuit against Israel because there is no faithfulness, no steadfast love, and no knowledge of God in the land, and the priests who were given to teach have instead fed on the people's sin, so the whole nation languishes under a leadership that profits from its falling.
sermons.verdict: My people perish for ignorance.

sermons.title: Your Love Is Like a Morning Cloud
sermons.idea: Israel composes a quick prayer of return, confident that God will heal and revive, but God answers that their devotion is like the morning mist that burns off by noon, because he desires steadfast love and the knowledge of God, not the burnt offerings of a heart that repents only until the danger passes.
sermons.verdict: Your repentance evaporates by noon.

sermons.title: They Sow the Wind
sermons.idea: Having made kings God did not choose and idols of their own silver, Israel has set in motion a harvest it cannot stop, because the God who is mocked is not mocked for long, and a people who plant rebellion will reap a storm that consumes both the seed and the sower.
sermons.verdict: They sowed wind. The whirlwind comes.

sermons.title: When Israel Was a Child I Loved Him
sermons.idea: God remembers teaching Ephraim to walk and bending down to feed him, and though justice demands that he hand this child over to ruin, his heart recoils within him and his compassion grows warm, because he is God and not a man, and his holiness will not let his love give the rebel up.
sermons.verdict: His mercy overruled his wrath.

sermons.title: I Will Be Your Death, O Death
sermons.idea: Israel has grown fat and forgotten the God who fed her in the wilderness, so judgment falls like a lion and a bear robbed of her cubs, and yet in the middle of the sentence God speaks of ransoming his people from the grave itself, revealing that the same hand that strikes is the only hand that can raise the dead.
sermons.verdict: The hand that strikes can raise.

sermons.title: Return, O Israel
sermons.idea: God puts the words of repentance into his people's mouths and promises to heal their faithlessness and love them freely, no longer as an offended Husband demanding payment but as the dew that makes a withered nation blossom, ending the book not with a verdict but with an open door.
sermons.verdict: Return. He is the healing.

isaiah.title: Isaiah: The Holy One in the Midst of a People
isaiah.headline: A pastoral expository sweep through all sixty-six chapters of Isaiah, from the indictment of Judah to the new heavens and new earth.
isaiah.bigIdea: The Holy One of Israel judges a people who have abandoned him, and then saves them by his own arm, through a child born, a Servant pierced, and a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
isaiah.christConnection: The Immanuel of chapters seven through nine and the Servant of chapter fifty-three are not two figures but one: the Son who is given, who bears the iniquity God lays on him, and rises to make many righteous. Isaiah preaches Christ before his name was known.

sermons.title: A People Loaded With Iniquity
sermons.idea: God's covenant people have rebelled against the Father who raised them, turning worship into noise and justice into oppression, and yet he still pleads with them to reason together and be made clean.
sermons.verdict: Religion cannot cover blood-stained hands.

sermons.title: Woe Is Me, For I Am Undone
sermons.idea: To see the holiness of God is first to be destroyed by it, and only the coal from the altar, grace that touches the unclean mouth, sends the prophet out to a people who will not hear.
sermons.verdict: Holiness ruins before it sends.

sermons.title: The Child Born, the Son Given
sermons.idea: When a faithless king refuses to trust God, the sign given is not deliverance from his enemies but a child named Immanuel, the light that dawns on those walking in deep darkness, the government laid on infant shoulders.
sermons.verdict: God comes as a child.

sermons.title: A Shoot From the Stump of Jesse
sermons.idea: After the proud axe of Assyria is broken, life comes from a cut-down stump, a righteous King on whom the Spirit rests, ruling a kingdom where the wolf lies with the lamb and the earth is full of the knowledge of the LORD.
sermons.verdict: New life grows from the stump.

sermons.title: The God of All the Nations
sermons.idea: The oracles against Babylon, Moab, Egypt, Tyre and the rest declare that the Holy One of Israel is no tribal deity but the Sovereign who weighs every empire, and human pride that climbs to heaven is brought down to the pit.
sermons.verdict: Every empire answers to him.

sermons.title: The City of Chaos and the City of God
sermons.idea: The whole earth is judged and the proud city laid waste, yet on this mountain God prepares a feast, swallows up death forever, and wipes away tears, the strong city of salvation set against the city of confusion.
sermons.verdict: Death itself is swallowed up.

sermons.title: Woe to Those Who Go Down to Egypt
sermons.idea: Judah seeks security in alliances and horses and chariots rather than in the LORD, and the prophet warns that every refuge of lies will be swept away while God lays in Zion a tested cornerstone for those who trust.
sermons.verdict: Egypt's horses cannot save you.

sermons.title: The Desert Shall Blossom
sermons.idea: Against the day of vengeance that turns Edom to wilderness, God promises a highway of holiness where the blind see, the lame leap, and the ransomed return to Zion with everlasting joy.
sermons.verdict: God turns wilderness into highway.

sermons.title: When the Letter Comes
sermons.idea: Faced with Assyria's blasphemy, Hezekiah spreads the threat before the LORD and is delivered, yet the same king who trusts God in crisis later parades his treasures and sows the seeds of Babylon's exile.
sermons.verdict: Faith in crisis, pride in peace.

sermons.title: Comfort, Comfort My People
sermons.idea: To a people facing exile, God speaks tenderness and announces his own coming, the everlasting Creator who does not faint, who carries the lambs in his arms and renews the strength of those who wait on him.
sermons.verdict: Our God does not grow weary.

sermons.title: My Servant, My Chosen
sermons.idea: The LORD who alone declares the end from the beginning summons his Servant to bring justice to the nations without breaking a bruised reed, and shames the dead idols that cannot save the exiles he has carried from the womb.
sermons.verdict: Idols are nothing; God carries.

sermons.title: He Was Pierced for Our Transgressions
sermons.idea: The Servant called from the womb and given as a light to the nations is the one despised and rejected, who bears the iniquity the LORD lays on him, is cut off for the transgression of the people, and by his wounds heals the many.
sermons.verdict: By his wounds we are healed.

sermons.title: Come, Everyone Who Thirsts
sermons.idea: On the ground of the Servant's finished work, God invites the thirsty to come and buy without money, calls for a fast that loosens the chains of injustice, and grieves that only sin separates a people from the salvation his own arm has won.
sermons.verdict: Grace costs nothing but yourself.

sermons.title: New Heavens and a New Earth
sermons.idea: The Anointed One proclaims the year of the LORD's favor, light rises on a darkened world, and God creates new heavens and a new earth where the former troubles are forgotten and his people dwell forever in his presence.
sermons.verdict: He makes all things new.

james.title: James: Faith That Holds Its Weight
james.headline: An expository walk through the letter of James, where wisdom is not what a man says but what his life does under pressure.
james.bigIdea: James writes to scattered, suffering believers and refuses to let faith remain an idea. Real faith is tested in trial, proven in obedience, exposed by partiality, completed in works, governed in the tongue, marked by heavenly wisdom, broken of its worldliness, and sustained in prayer until the Lord comes. The whole letter measures belief by what it produces.
james.christConnection: James preaches the wisdom of God not as a concept but as a life, the same wisdom that came down from above and was lived out in full by the Lord of glory, in whom mercy triumphs over judgment and the prayer of faith finds its yes. To hold this faith is to hold to Him, and to hold to Him is to be doers of the word He gave.

sermons.title: Tested, and Not Left Alone
sermons.idea: The trials that come to scattered believers are not the absence of God's favor but the means of their maturity; the same God who lets faith be tested gives wisdom freely to the one who asks, and counts blessed not the hearer of the word but the one who does it.
sermons.verdict: Hearing is not having.

sermons.title: The Sin of the Welcome Mat
sermons.idea: To hold faith in the Lord of glory while honoring the rich man and shaming the poor is to make oneself a judge with evil thoughts, contradicting the God who chose the poor and the royal law that commands love of neighbor; partiality is not a small failure of manners but a breaking of the whole law.
sermons.verdict: Mercy triumphs over judgment.

sermons.title: The Faith That Does Nothing
sermons.idea: A faith that produces no works cannot save, because such faith is dead, as dead as a body without breath; Abraham and Rahab show that living faith is completed and proven in action, so the claim of belief without the evidence of obedience is empty.
sermons.verdict: Dead faith saves no one.

sermons.title: The Small Fire
sermons.idea: The tongue is a small member that sets the whole course of a life ablaze and that no man can tame; the same mouth that blesses God and curses those made in His image exposes a divided heart, for a spring cannot pour out both fresh water and salt.
sermons.verdict: Your mouth tells the truth.

sermons.title: Two Wisdoms
sermons.idea: There is a wisdom that is earthly, unspiritual, and demonic, known by its bitter jealousy and selfish ambition and the disorder it breeds; and there is a wisdom from above, pure and peaceable and full of mercy, known not by what a man claims but by the harvest of righteousness his life sows in peace.
sermons.verdict: Wisdom is known by fruit.

sermons.title: Friendship With the World
sermons.idea: The quarrels among believers come from desires at war within them, and their prayers go unanswered because they do not ask, or ask to spend it on their passions; friendship with the world is enmity with God, and the only way back is to humble oneself before the Lord who gives grace to the lowly.
sermons.verdict: Humble yourself. He lifts.

sermons.title: Until the Lord Comes
sermons.idea: Judgment is stored up for the rich who hoarded wealth and defrauded their workers, while the suffering believer is called to patience like the farmer waiting for rain, for the coming of the Lord is at hand; and in that waiting the church prays, over the sick, over sin, over one another, because the prayer of faith is powerful and effective.
sermons.verdict: Be patient. He is near.

jeremiah.title: The Weeping Prophet: Preaching Through Jeremiah
jeremiah.headline: A nation will not be saved by its rituals, and a man will not be spared for telling the truth, Jeremiah preaches collapse, and underneath it a covenant God will write on the heart.
jeremiah.bigIdea: Judah's worship had become a shield against the very God it claimed to serve, and Jeremiah was called to announce the judgment that ritual could not avert and to wait for the only thing that could heal it: a covenant God himself would keep.
jeremiah.christConnection: The new covenant Jeremiah promised in chapter 31, sins remembered no more, the law written on the heart, is the covenant Jesus inaugurated in his own blood at the table, and what Israel could not keep, Christ keeps for them and in them.

sermons.title: Before I Formed You
sermons.idea: God's call to Jeremiah rests not on the prophet's readiness but on God's prior knowing and appointing, which means the word he must speak, to pluck up and to plant, is God's word and not his own, and his fear is answered by presence rather than removed by ease.
sermons.verdict: You were known before you were ready.

sermons.title: Two Evils, Broken Cisterns
sermons.idea: Israel committed two evils at once: they abandoned the fountain of living water and they hewed for themselves cracked cisterns that hold no water, trading the God who gave them everything for substitutes that cannot even keep what little they pour in.
sermons.verdict: We dig for what we already had.

sermons.title: The Temple Will Not Save You
sermons.idea: Standing in the temple gate, Jeremiah forbids the people to trust the deceptive words "the temple of the LORD" as a charm, because God does not protect a house where they steal, murder, and oppress and then come to stand before him claiming safety, the sanctuary becomes Shiloh's ruins when justice is dead.
sermons.verdict: Sacred walls cannot cover injustice.

sermons.title: The Potter's House
sermons.idea: At the potter's wheel God claims the sovereign freedom to remake the marred vessel, but he binds that freedom to the people's response, relenting from disaster if they turn, withdrawing good if they do evil, and Judah answers that it is hopeless, that they will follow their own stubborn hearts.
sermons.verdict: The clay said no to the potter.

sermons.title: The Fire and the Curse
sermons.idea: Jeremiah's faithfulness costs him mockery, beating, and isolation, and his honest confession holds together two things at once: a word he cannot hold in because it burns in his bones, and a despair so deep he curses the day of his birth, the prophet does not edit his agony before God.
sermons.verdict: Faithfulness wounded him and held him.

sermons.title: The Yoke and the False Prophets
sermons.idea: God commands Jeremiah to wear a yoke as a sign that submission to Babylon is God's own discipline, and when Hananiah breaks the wooden yoke and promises peace in two years, the comforting lie is exposed as rebellion against God, replaced by an iron yoke and the prophet's death within the year.
sermons.verdict: The comforting lie kills its prophet.

sermons.title: Seek the Welfare of the City
sermons.idea: To exiles longing for a quick return, God commands the harder obedience of staying: build houses, plant gardens, marry, and seek the welfare of Babylon, because their peace is bound to the peace of the city that conquered them, and God's plans for a future and a hope unfold across seventy years, not seventy days.
sermons.verdict: Pray for the city that took you.

sermons.title: A Covenant on the Heart
sermons.idea: God promises a new covenant unlike the one Israel broke, not law carved on stone they will violate, but law written on the heart, a knowing of God from the least to the greatest, and the foundation under it all: I will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more.
sermons.verdict: He will remember sin no more.

sermons.title: Buying the Field
sermons.idea: With Babylon's army already at the walls and Jeremiah imprisoned, God commands him to buy a field in occupied territory and seal the deed, a deliberate act of money spent on a future no one could see, because houses and fields and vineyards shall again be bought in this land.
sermons.verdict: He paid for a promised future.

sermons.title: The City Falls
sermons.idea: After eighteen months of siege the wall is breached, Zedekiah watches his sons killed before his own eyes are put out, the temple and houses are burned, and the long-warned judgment finally lands, proving the prophet true and ending every illusion that ritual or politics could hold back the consequence of covenant betrayal.
sermons.verdict: The word warned came finally true.

sermons.title: The Ruin and the Lifted Head
sermons.idea: The closing record counts the dead, the burned, and the carried-away with sober precision, refusing to soften the cost of Judah's sin, and then, in the final verses, the imprisoned king Jehoiachin is released and given a seat above the other kings, a small lifted head that keeps the line and the hope alive in the dark.
sermons.verdict: Ruin recorded, yet a head lifted.

job.title: The Book of Job: When the Innocent Suffer
job.headline: A working pastor preaches the whole of Job, in order, refusing every cheap answer the text itself refuses.
job.bigIdea: Job is not a riddle to be solved but a man to be reckoned with: a righteous sufferer whose loss is real, whose questions are honest, whose friends are wrong, and whose God answers him not with explanation but with presence. The book holds innocent suffering open and will not let it close.
job.christConnection: Job longs for an arbiter who could lay a hand on both God and man, and for a Redeemer who stands at the last upon the earth, yet he has no one to fill that office. Jesus is the mediator Job could not find: the truly innocent sufferer who bore the silence Job feared and answers the cry Job could only voice.

sermons.title: The Wager Job Never Heard
sermons.idea: God permits the satan to strip a blameless man of children, wealth, and health to prove that worship can be free, and Job, who never sees the heavenly court, holds onto God without cursing him.
sermons.verdict: He worshiped without an answer.

sermons.title: The Day He Cursed
sermons.idea: The same man who blessed God now curses the day of his birth, and Scripture lets the lament stand as faithful speech, not failure, naming the unbearable weight of being kept alive to suffer.
sermons.verdict: Faith can sound like this.

sermons.title: Eliphaz and the First Wrong Comfort
sermons.idea: Eliphaz reasons from his vision that the innocent never perish and the guilty reap what they sow, so Job must have sinned, and Job answers that his friends have become a dry streambed when he was dying of thirst.
sermons.verdict: They explained away his pain.

sermons.title: Bildad and the God on Trial
sermons.idea: Bildad defends God's justice by insisting Job's children died for their sin, and Job, granting that no one can be righteous before God, longs for an umpire to lay a hand on them both.
sermons.verdict: He wanted someone between them.

sermons.title: Zophar and the Hope of a Tree
sermons.idea: Zophar claims Job deserves worse than he has received, and Job, holding to his integrity against all three, reaches past the grave to wonder whether a man, like a felled tree, might yet live again.
sermons.verdict: Even cut down, he hoped.

sermons.title: The Second Round and the Witness on High
sermons.idea: The friends harden into accusation as Eliphaz returns to the fate of the wicked, and Job, calling them miserable comforters, insists that even now his witness is in heaven and his advocate on high.
sermons.verdict: His defender was already above.

sermons.title: I Know That My Redeemer Lives
sermons.idea: Bildad consigns the wicked to terror and oblivion, and Job, abandoned by kin and friends, declares against every appearance that his Redeemer lives and that he will see God with his own eyes.
sermons.verdict: He hoped past his own flesh.

sermons.title: The Wicked Who Prosper Anyway
sermons.idea: Zophar recites the swift ruin of the wicked, and Job answers from what he has actually seen, that the wicked grow old, see their children settled, and go down to the grave in peace, exposing the lie in their tidy theology.
sermons.verdict: Their doctrine failed the evidence.

sermons.title: The Accusation Without Proof
sermons.idea: Eliphaz invents specific crimes to fit his theory, charging Job with stripping the naked and crushing the poor, and Job, finding God absent when he searches in every direction, still trusts that he will come forth as gold.
sermons.verdict: Accused, he sought the courtroom.

sermons.title: Where Wisdom Is Found
sermons.idea: Bildad's speech collapses into a few thin verses, the friends fall silent, and the great poem on wisdom declares that no creature can find it or buy it, for the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn from evil is understanding.
sermons.verdict: Wisdom is not ours to mine.

sermons.title: The Oath of a Clear Conscience
sermons.idea: Job remembers the days when he rescued the poor and was honored in the gate, mourns his present contempt, and seals his defense with an oath of innocence so complete that he stakes everything on God answering him.
sermons.verdict: He signed his own defense.

sermons.title: Elihu and the Anger of the Young
sermons.idea: Elihu, angry at both Job and the friends, claims to speak for God and argues that suffering is God's discipline and warning, that God afflicts to instruct rather than only to punish, adding a truer note the three never struck.
sermons.verdict: A new voice, still incomplete.

sermons.title: Elihu and the Coming Storm
sermons.idea: Elihu magnifies the greatness and justice of God and points to the gathering thunderstorm as evidence that the Almighty is beyond Job's reckoning, preparing the stage for the One who will speak from the very storm he describes.
sermons.verdict: He pointed toward the whirlwind.

sermons.title: God Answers from the Whirlwind
sermons.idea: God answers Job not with reasons but with questions, parading the foundations of the earth, the storehouses of snow, the wild donkey, and the war horse, until Job's small courtroom is dwarfed by a world he never made or governs.
sermons.verdict: God answered with the world.

sermons.title: Behemoth, Leviathan, and the Limits of Job
sermons.idea: God presses further with Behemoth and Leviathan, creatures Job can neither tame nor stand before, asking whether the man who cannot draw out Leviathan with a hook is fit to correct the One who rules the chaos he fears.
sermons.verdict: He cannot tame the dragon.

sermons.title: Now My Eye Sees You
sermons.idea: Job repents not of invented sins but of speaking beyond his knowledge, confessing that he had heard of God by the hearing of the ear but now his eye sees him, and the sight, not an explanation, is what finally quiets him.
sermons.verdict: Seeing God ended the argument.

sermons.title: The Friends Rebuked, the Sufferer Restored
sermons.idea: God vindicates Job and rebukes the friends for not speaking rightly of him, has the sufferer pray for his accusers, and restores his fortunes, yet the lost children are not the dead returned, leaving the wound named even in the blessing.
sermons.verdict: Restored, but not unmarked.

joel.title: The Day the Locusts Came: Preaching Through Joel
joel.headline: A ruined harvest, a torn heart, and a Spirit poured out on all flesh
joel.bigIdea: Joel reads a single catastrophe as a summons. The locust that strips the land is the near edge of the Day of the LORD, and the only adequate response is not management but return, a returning answered by a God who relents, restores the eaten years, pours out his Spirit on all flesh, and stands as refuge while he judges the nations.
joel.christConnection: The promise of Joel 2, that God would pour out his Spirit on all flesh, so that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved, is taken up by Peter at Pentecost and declared fulfilled in the crucified and risen Jesus. The Day of the LORD that Joel announces arrives in two movements: the cross where judgment falls on Christ, and the name now offered to skeptic and saint alike to call upon and live.

sermons.title: What the Locust Left
sermons.idea: A devastation total enough to silence the wine and stop the offerings is not a disruption to be absorbed but a word from God to be heard, and the first faithful act before such a loss is not explanation but lament.
sermons.verdict: Wake up and grieve before God.

sermons.title: Return to Me
sermons.idea: The Day of the LORD comes as an army no one survives by strength, and the only door left open is the one God himself names, return to me with all your heart, rending the heart and not the garments before a God known to be gracious and slow to anger.
sermons.verdict: Rend your heart, not your clothes.

sermons.title: The Years the Locust Ate
sermons.idea: When the people return, God answers with a jealousy for his own land and people that restores the very years the locust devoured and overflows into a Spirit poured out on all flesh, so that sons, daughters, servants, and strangers all prophesy and all who call on his name are saved.
sermons.verdict: He restores the eaten years.

sermons.title: The Valley of Decision and the Refuge
sermons.idea: The same Day that terrifies the guilty becomes shelter for those who called on his name, for God gathers the nations to account for what they did to his people and to the helpless, and in the same breath the LORD is a refuge and a stronghold who dwells with his own forever.
sermons.verdict: The Judge is also the refuge.

jonah.title: Jonah: The Prophet Who Resented Grace
jonah.headline: Four chapters about a God who pursues the people His prophet wants destroyed
jonah.bigIdea: Jonah is not finally a story about a fish or a city. It is a story about a man who would rather die than watch God forgive his enemies, and a God who keeps asking him to feel what mercy costs. The book ends on a question, and the question is for the reader.
jonah.christConnection: Jesus named this book as the sign of His own death and rising, three days in the grave as Jonah was three days in the deep. But where Jonah ran from his enemies and resented their rescue, Christ ran toward His, and prayed for them while they killed Him; He is the greater Jonah who actually loves the city.

sermons.title: The Runaway and the Storm
sermons.idea: Called to preach to the enemy, Jonah runs the opposite direction, and the storm God sends to chase him nearly drowns a boatful of pagans who fear the LORD more readily than His own prophet does.
sermons.verdict: You cannot outrun your call.

sermons.title: The Prayer from the Belly
sermons.idea: From inside the fish, at the bottom of his own rebellion, Jonah prays a psalm stitched from older psalms and arrives at the one true sentence of the book, salvation belongs to the LORD, though he has not yet let it change whom he wants saved.
sermons.verdict: Salvation belongs to the LORD.

sermons.title: Nineveh Repents
sermons.idea: A reluctant prophet preaches eight words of judgment, and the most violent city in the world repents from the king to the cattle, and God relents from the disaster He had spoken, grace falling on exactly the people Jonah wished it would skip.
sermons.verdict: God relents toward His enemies.

sermons.title: The Angry Prophet and the Worm
sermons.idea: Jonah is furious that God is gracious, would rather die than live in a world where Nineveh is spared, and God answers his rage with a withering plant and a question about mercy that the book refuses to answer for us.
sermons.verdict: Should I not pity them?

joshua.title: Joshua: The God Who Keeps His Word
joshua.headline: Preaching straight through the book of the land God swore to give
