joshua.bigIdea: The conquest of Canaan is the proof that not one word of all the good things the LORD promised has failed; the land is given, not earned, and the only fitting response is undivided allegiance.
joshua.christConnection: Joshua bears the name that means the LORD saves, the same name carried by the One who leads a greater people into a rest no enemy can break. The commander outside Jericho, sword drawn, belongs to no army but his own. The scarlet cord in Rahab's window and the blood that spares a household point past the walls of Canaan to the cross, where the outsider is grafted in and the inheritance is secured by another's faithfulness, not ours.

sermons.title: Be Strong and Courageous
sermons.idea: Moses is dead, but the promise is not; God commissions Joshua to take the land by clinging to the word in the Book and to the presence of the God who will not leave him.
sermons.verdict: The promise outlives the man.

sermons.title: The Scarlet Cord in the Window
sermons.idea: A Canaanite prostitute confesses what Israel keeps forgetting, that the LORD is God in heaven above and on earth below, and her faith brings her household inside the covenant.
sermons.verdict: Grace reaches the wrong house first.

sermons.title: Crossing the Jordan on Dry Ground
sermons.idea: When the priests carrying the ark step into the flood at harvest, the waters stand in a heap, and the stones piled on the far bank become a sermon to children not yet born.
sermons.verdict: The ark goes in first.

sermons.title: Circumcised and Fed Before the Fight
sermons.idea: Before a single battle, God renews the covenant sign, rolls away the reproach of Egypt, and the manna stops because the land itself now feeds them.
sermons.verdict: Consecration comes before conquest.

sermons.title: The Walls of Jericho Fall
sermons.idea: The commander of the LORD's army takes no side but his own, and the city is taken not by Israel's strength but by marching, trumpets, and a shout, devoted whole to God.
sermons.verdict: The victory was never ours.

sermons.title: Achan in the Camp
sermons.idea: One man's hidden theft of devoted things makes all Israel guilty, and only after sin is named and judged does God give Ai into their hand.
sermons.verdict: Hidden sin defeats the whole camp.

sermons.title: The Long Obedience of Conquest
sermons.idea: On Ebal and Gerizim the law is read aloud, the Gibeonites deceive Israel into a covenant Israel keeps, and from south to north the land is subdued because the LORD fought for Israel.
sermons.verdict: The LORD fought for Israel.

sermons.title: The Allotment of the Inheritance
sermons.idea: Land still unconquered is divided by lot tribe by tribe, because the inheritance rests on God's sworn gift and not on what Israel has already seized.
sermons.verdict: The gift precedes the taking.

sermons.title: Caleb at Eighty-Five
sermons.idea: Forty-five years after he brought back a faithful report, Caleb asks for the hill country of the giants, claiming the mountain God promised because he wholly followed the LORD.
sermons.verdict: Give me this mountain.

sermons.title: Cities of Refuge and the Levites' Towns
sermons.idea: God plants mercy into the map with cities where the manslayer may flee, and scatters the Levites among every tribe, and not one word of all His good promise fails.
sermons.verdict: Not one word has failed.

sermons.title: The Altar by the Jordan
sermons.idea: The eastern tribes build an altar that looks like rebellion and nearly starts a war, until they explain it is a witness that they too belong to the LORD.
sermons.verdict: Build witnesses, not divisions.

sermons.title: Joshua's Charge to the Leaders
sermons.idea: Old and ready to die, Joshua warns that the same God who kept every promise of blessing will keep every promise of judgment if they cling to the nations and their gods.
sermons.verdict: The faithful God also judges.

sermons.title: Choose This Day Whom You Will Serve
sermons.idea: At Shechem Joshua rehearses all God has done from Abraham forward and presses the people to put away their gods and choose, knowing the choice will cost them.
sermons.verdict: Choose the One who chose you.

jude.title: Contend: A Series Through Jude
jude.headline: A short letter written in alarm, ending in worship, Jude calls the church to fight for the faith it was given, to see what judgment has already done to the ungodly, and to be kept by the God who does not let His own fall.
jude.bigIdea: Jude meant to write about salvation and instead had to write about danger, because false teachers had crept into the church to turn grace into a license for sin and to deny the Lord; and the same letter that names the threat ends by entrusting believers to the only God who is able to keep them from stumbling and present them blameless.
jude.christConnection: Jude closes by addressing his praise to the only God our Savior through Jesus Christ, the One who is able to keep us from stumbling and to set us before the presence of His glory blameless and with great joy. The faith we are told to contend for is not finally held by our grip but by His.

sermons.title: The Letter He Did Not Want to Write
sermons.idea: Jude intended to write about the salvation believers share, but the intrusion of ungodly men who pervert God's grace into sensuality and deny the Lord forced him instead to urge the church to contend for the faith once for all delivered to the saints.
sermons.verdict: Defend the faith you received.

sermons.title: What Judgment Has Already Done
sermons.idea: Jude stacks examples from Israel, the angels, and Sodom to prove that God judges the ungodly, and then exposes the false teachers by their fruit, they defile the flesh, reject authority, grumble, flatter, and follow their own desires, showing that present sin sits already under a settled verdict.
sermons.verdict: God has judged the ungodly before.

sermons.title: Kept
sermons.idea: Against the scoffers the apostles foretold, Jude tells the church to build itself up in the faith, pray in the Spirit, keep itself in the love of God, and show mercy to the wavering, then turns from their effort to God's power, for He alone is able to keep them from stumbling and present them blameless before His glory.
sermons.verdict: He is able to keep you.

judges.title: When Everyone Did What Was Right: Preaching Through Judges
judges.headline: A nation circles the same drain for two hundred years, and God keeps reaching down into it
judges.bigIdea: Judges is the honest record of what happens when a covenant people stop remembering the Lord who saved them. Generation by generation the cycle tightens, sin, oppression, a cry, a deliverer, a brief rest, then sin again, and the deliverers themselves degrade until the last one is a manipulated strongman and the last chapters read like a coroner's report. The book diagnoses the human heart left to itself and exposes the desperate need for a King who will not corrode.
judges.christConnection: Every judge saves partly and then fails, and the book ends with no king and a refrain that names the disease: everyone did what was right in his own eyes. Judges is a long argument for a deliverer who does not need saving from himself. The flawed rescuers point past themselves to the one who would be raised up not for a generation but forever, Jesus, the righteous King who does what is right in the Father's eyes, and breaks the cycle from the inside by dying inside it.

sermons.title: The Compromise Nobody Called Sin
sermons.idea: Israel's incomplete obedience after Joshua, settling for coexistence with the nations they were charged to drive out, is the seed of every disaster that follows, and the angel at Bochim names it as covenant breach long before it bears fruit.
sermons.verdict: Partial obedience is disobedience that waits.

sermons.title: The Cycle Named in Advance
sermons.idea: The narrator pulls back to show the whole machine: a generation arises that does not know the Lord, Israel serves the Baals, God hands them over, they cry out, He raises a judge, then they turn back worse than before, and the pattern is the structure of the entire book.
sermons.verdict: We forget faster than He saves.

sermons.title: Three Deliverers and a Borrowed Strength
sermons.idea: Othniel, Ehud, and Shamgar each deliver Israel not by their own resources but by the Spirit and the cunning God provides, showing early that the rescue belongs to the Lord even when the rescuer is an underdog, a left-handed assassin, or a man with an ox goad.
sermons.verdict: The strength was never theirs.

sermons.title: The Glory Goes to a Woman
sermons.idea: When Barak will not go without Deborah, God deliberately routes the victory through unexpected hands, a prophetess who judges Israel and Jael who drives the tent peg, so that the honor of the day belongs to no man's courage but to the Lord who fights for His people.
sermons.verdict: God shares His glory with no man.

sermons.title: A Coward, a Fleece, and Three Hundred Men
sermons.idea: Gideon, hiding in a winepress and hedging with fleeces, is whittled down to three hundred so that Israel cannot boast its own hand saved it, and God patiently works with weak faith to make His own power unmistakable.
sermons.verdict: He saves so He gets the credit.

sermons.title: The Hero Who Could Not Stop Winning
sermons.idea: After the victory Gideon takes brutal revenge, gathers gold into an ephod that becomes a snare, and fathers seventy sons including one named Abimelech, showing how a man delivered by grace can turn his deliverance into the next generation's idol.
sermons.verdict: Unfinished men finish badly.

sermons.title: The Bramble King and the Fire He Started
sermons.idea: Abimelech murders his brothers to seize a crown nobody offered him, Jotham's parable exposes the rot of self-made kingship, and the whole arrangement collapses in mutual destruction, God repaying the violence of son and city alike.
sermons.verdict: Ambition without God consumes its own.

sermons.title: The Vow He Should Have Broken
sermons.idea: Jephthah, an outcast bargained back into leadership, wins by the Spirit but binds himself with a reckless vow he refuses to repent of, sacrificing his only daughter to his own word, a man who trusted God for victory but not for mercy.
sermons.verdict: A rash vow is not faith.

sermons.title: The Word That Got Men Killed
sermons.idea: Jephthah's quarrel with Ephraim ends in forty-two thousand Israelites slaughtered at the fords of the Jordan over the pronunciation of a single word, exposing a covenant people now turning their swords on each other.
sermons.verdict: Israel's worst enemy is Israel.

sermons.title: A Promise Made to People Who Stopped Asking
sermons.idea: Israel does not even cry out this time, yet God announces a deliverer to a barren woman and sets Samson apart from the womb as a Nazirite, grace arriving unrequested, with every sign of hope already shadowed by what this man will not keep.
sermons.verdict: God moves before we ask.

sermons.title: The Strong Man Ruled by His Appetites
sermons.idea: Samson's Spirit-given strength is real, but he is governed by his eyes and his anger, breaking his vows for a wife and a riddle while God still bends even his selfishness toward striking the Philistines.
sermons.verdict: Gifted and undisciplined still destroys.

sermons.title: Blind, Bound, and Finally Praying
sermons.idea: Samson loses his hair, his eyes, and his freedom because he treated holiness as a game, yet in the Philistine temple, broken and humbled, he prays for the first time and God answers, killing more in his death than in his life.
sermons.verdict: Grace meets us in the ruins.

sermons.title: A Religion Built to Order
sermons.idea: Micah manufactures his own gods, hires a wandering Levite as a private priest, and an entire tribe steals the whole operation, the first of the closing chapters showing Israel inventing convenient worship because there was no king and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
sermons.verdict: Homemade gods cannot save.

sermons.title: The Night Israel Became Sodom
sermons.idea: A Levite's concubine is handed over, abused through the night, and dismembered, and the narrator forces the reader to see that Israel has now become indistinguishable from the wickedness it was sent to drive out.
sermons.verdict: Without God, no one is safe.

sermons.title: Everyone Did What Was Right in His Own Eyes
sermons.idea: The civil war against Benjamin and the desperate, lawless scramble to provide them wives leaves the nation nearly self-destroyed, and the book's final line states the verdict over everything that came before: no king, and every man his own law.
sermons.verdict: We need a King who saves.

lamentations.title: How Lonely Sits the City: Preaching the Grief of Lamentations
lamentations.headline: Five poems from the ruins of Jerusalem, where God's people learn to grieve out loud and still call on his name
lamentations.bigIdea: Lamentations refuses to look away from the wreckage of judgment, and from the center of that wreckage it confesses that the LORD's mercies do not end, teaching the church to bring real loss into the presence of God without pretending the loss is smaller than it is.
lamentations.christConnection: The man of sorrows who weeps over Jerusalem and is himself forsaken outside its walls takes the cup of God's anger that Lamentations describes, and the mercies that are new every morning in chapter three are secured in his resurrection. The acrostic that runs A to Z over the ruin finds its answer in the One who is the beginning and the end and who turns mourning into the morning that does not fail.

sermons.title: How Lonely Sits the City
sermons.idea: Jerusalem, once full of people and now a weeping widow, has no comforter because her grief is bound up with her own sin, and yet she still turns her face toward the LORD and asks him to see.
sermons.verdict: Look on my affliction, LORD.

sermons.title: The LORD Has Become Like an Enemy
sermons.idea: The poem names the hardest truth in the book, that the ruin came from the hand of God in his anger against his own sanctuary and people, and the only honest response is to cry out to him through the night without explaining the pain away.
sermons.verdict: He himself bent the bow.

sermons.title: Great Is Your Faithfulness
sermons.idea: At the center of the deepest darkness the man under God's rod remembers that the LORD's steadfast love never ceases and his mercies are new every morning, and this hope does not cancel the grief but holds the sufferer while it lasts.
sermons.verdict: His mercies are new tomorrow.

sermons.title: The Siege and the Famine
sermons.idea: The poem counts the cost of judgment in starving children and a fallen leadership, refusing every comfortable abstraction, and insists that the punishment of God's people, though terrible, is not the final word over their enemies either.
sermons.verdict: Even gold loses its shine.

sermons.title: Restore Us to Yourself
sermons.idea: The broken acrostic gives way to a plain communal prayer that remembers the shame, confesses the sin of the fathers and the present generation, and casts the whole future on the eternal reign of God with no guarantee of the answer.
sermons.verdict: Restore us, unless you have rejected us.

leviticus.title: The Cost of a God Who Comes Near
leviticus.headline: Preaching straight through Leviticus, chapter by chapter, where a holy God makes a way to live with sinful people
leviticus.bigIdea: A holy God moves into the camp of an unclean people, and the whole book is the costly, blood-soaked answer to one question, how can they survive his nearness.
leviticus.christConnection: Every altar, every priest, every drop of blood, and every appointed feast points beyond itself to the one whose single offering makes the worshipers clean for good and brings the holy God all the way to dwell in human flesh.

sermons.title: The Fire That Will Not Take Just Anyone
sermons.idea: God prescribes five offerings so that a guilty worshiper can approach him only by a substitute consumed in his place, atonement made by blood and gift offered without defect.
sermons.verdict: Approach costs a life. Always.

sermons.title: Strange Fire at the Door
sermons.idea: God ordains and then consumes the priesthood he has chosen, killing Nadab and Abihu to teach that those who draw nearest must treat his holiness as holy or die.
sermons.verdict: Nearness is not a privilege to presume.

sermons.title: Clean Hands, Clean House, Clean Skin
sermons.idea: God orders the whole bodily life of his people, food, birth, disease, discharge, so that the line between clean and unclean trains them to see that holiness reaches into the ordinary flesh.
sermons.verdict: Holiness goes all the way down.

sermons.title: The One Day the Curtain Opens
sermons.idea: On the Day of Atonement the high priest enters the holiest place by blood and sends a second goat bearing all the people's sin into the wilderness, cleansing the sanctuary and the nation for one more year.
sermons.verdict: Sin is carried away, not excused.

sermons.title: The Life Is in the Blood
sermons.idea: God forbids eating blood and demands every sacrifice be brought to his altar, because the blood is the life and he alone may give it as the price of atonement.
sermons.verdict: Blood belongs to God, not us.

sermons.title: Be Holy, For I Am Holy
sermons.idea: God commands his people to refuse the sexual, social, and worship practices of the nations around them, because a people belonging to a holy God must look unmistakably unlike the world.
sermons.verdict: You are not the nations.

sermons.title: Those Who Carry the Holy
sermons.idea: God holds the priests and their offerings to a stricter standard of wholeness and purity, because those who handle holy things and bear his name must not profane them.
sermons.verdict: The closer the call, the higher the cost.

sermons.title: A Calendar Built for Worship
sermons.idea: God appoints the sabbath and the yearly feasts so that Israel's time itself is structured around remembering his deliverance and rehearsing his presence.
sermons.verdict: Time itself belongs to the LORD.

sermons.title: The Year Everything Goes Home
sermons.idea: God commands the sabbath year and the year of Jubilee so that land returns, debts release, and slaves go free, because the land and the people are his and not finally for sale.
sermons.verdict: Nothing here is ours to keep.

sermons.title: Blessing, Exile, and the God Who Remembers
sermons.idea: God sets blessing before obedience and devastating curse before rebellion, yet binds himself to remember his covenant even in exile, and seals the book with the vows his people freely make to him.
sermons.verdict: He will not forget his covenant.

luke.title: The Son of Man Came to Seek the Lost: An Expository Series Through Luke
luke.headline: Twelve sermons through the Gospel that bends toward the poor, the outsider, the woman at the margin, and the one who is lost.
luke.bigIdea: Luke writes an orderly account so that Theophilus, and everyone after him, might have certainty concerning the things he has been taught. The certainty is this: God's salvation has come in person, and it has come for the people the world wrote off. The Magnificat sets the key signature and the cross holds the note. From the first chapter to the road to Emmaus, Luke insists that the same God who scatters the proud and fills the hungry is the God who became flesh, ate with sinners, was crucified between criminals, and rose to open the Scriptures to slow hearts. This series preaches Luke in order, passage by passage, refusing to skip the cost.
luke.christConnection: Jesus is the Son of Man who came to seek and to save what was lost, the one who entered the room where people fall apart rather than ruling from a safe distance. He is born among the overlooked, anointed to preach good news to the poor, and lifted up on a cross between two thieves, where the lost are found at the last possible hour.

sermons.title: The Magnificat: God Takes Sides
sermons.idea: Mary's song announces that the salvation now stirring in her womb is not religious comfort layered over an unjust world but the overturning of it. God scatters the proud, brings down rulers, lifts the humble, fills the hungry, and sends the rich away empty, keeping the mercy he swore to Abraham. The whole Gospel of Luke is contained in this teenage girl's praise before a single sermon is preached.
sermons.verdict: God has chosen the lowly.

sermons.title: Good News to Shepherds: The Birth at the Bottom
sermons.idea: Luke dates the birth by Caesar's decree and Quirinius's census, then ignores the palace entirely. The Savior is laid in a feeding trough because there was no room, and the announcement of his birth goes first to shepherds working the night shift, the kind of men whose testimony did not count in court. The glory of the Lord shines on the people Rome counted only for taxation.
sermons.verdict: Glory came to the night shift.

sermons.title: The Year of the Lord's Favor: The Nazareth Manifesto
sermons.idea: Jesus opens Isaiah in his hometown synagogue, reads good news to the poor and liberty to the captives, and declares the text fulfilled in their hearing. Then he reminds them that Elijah was sent to a foreign widow and Elisha cleansed a Syrian, and the same people who marveled try to throw him off a cliff. The favor of the Lord is real, and it reaches past Nazareth to the outsider, which is exactly what the hometown cannot forgive.
sermons.verdict: Grace for outsiders enrages the insiders.

sermons.title: The Great Catch: Depart From Me, I Am a Sinful Man
sermons.idea: After fishing all night and catching nothing, Peter lets down the nets at Jesus's word and the catch nearly sinks two boats. His response is not delight but dread: he falls down and asks Jesus to leave, because nearness to holiness exposes him. Jesus does not leave. He calls the frightened sinner to catch men, and Peter leaves everything to follow.
sermons.verdict: He calls the ones who flinch.

sermons.title: The Sermon on the Plain: Blessings, Woes, and Enemies
sermons.idea: On level ground, eye to eye with the crowd, Jesus calls the poor, the hungry, the weeping, and the hated blessed, and pronounces woe on the rich, the full, the laughing, and the well-regarded. Then he raises the standard past anything reciprocity can reach: love your enemies, lend expecting nothing, be merciful as your Father is merciful. The kingdom inverts the scoreboard and then demands a love that only the merciful Father could supply.
sermons.verdict: Love the ones who hate you.

sermons.title: She Loved Much: The Sinful Woman at the Pharisee's Table
sermons.idea: A woman known in the town as a sinner crashes Simon's dinner, weeps on Jesus's feet, wipes them with her hair, and pours out perfume, while the host silently decides Jesus must be no prophet. Jesus tells a parable of two debtors and turns it on Simon: the one forgiven much loves much, the one who thinks he owes little loves little. Her tears are not the cause of her forgiveness but the evidence of it, and she goes in peace while the respectable host stays dry-eyed.
sermons.verdict: Forgiven much, she loved much.

sermons.title: The Cost of Following: Take Up the Cross Daily
sermons.idea: Jesus tells the crowd that to follow him is to deny self, take up a cross daily, and lose one's life in order to save it, and then he meets three would-be followers and refuses to soften the terms for any of them. There is no place to lay his head, no funeral that can come first, no last goodbye that takes priority over the kingdom. Luke will not let discipleship be a sentiment; it is a death with no plan B.
sermons.verdict: Follow him, or do not.

sermons.title: The Good Samaritan: Go and Do Likewise
sermons.idea: A lawyer wanting to justify himself asks who counts as his neighbor, and Jesus answers with a road, a beaten man, two religious professionals who pass by, and a despised Samaritan who stops, binds wounds, pays the bill, and promises to return. Jesus refuses to define the neighbor and instead asks which man became one. Mercy, not bloodline or theology, is the proof of love for God, and the hero is the heretic the lawyer despised.
sermons.verdict: The despised one was the neighbor.

sermons.title: Teach Us to Pray: The Shameless Friend at Midnight
sermons.idea: Jesus gives the disciples a short prayer that hallows the Father's name, asks for daily bread, forgiveness, and rescue, then tells of a man who pounds on a friend's door at midnight and receives because he will not stop asking. The argument runs from lesser to greater: if a sleepy neighbor and a flawed father will give, how much more will the Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask. Prayer is not flattery of a reluctant God but persistence before a Father who delights to give.
sermons.verdict: Ask the Father who delights to give.

sermons.title: The Lost Sons: A Father Who Runs
sermons.idea: Jesus answers the grumbling that he eats with sinners by telling of a son who takes his inheritance as if his father were dead, wastes it, and comes home rehearsing an apology he never gets to finish because the father runs, embraces him, and throws a feast. Then the camera turns to the elder son standing outside, furious that grace is free, and the father goes out to plead with him too. Both sons are lost, one in a far country and one in the field of his own resentment, and the father pursues them both.
sermons.verdict: The Father runs toward the lost.

sermons.title: Lazarus at the Gate: The Rich Man Who Stepped Over Him
sermons.idea: A rich man feasts in purple every day while a sick beggar named Lazarus lies at his gate longing for scraps, and when both die the positions are reversed beyond appeal. The rich man, who never learned Lazarus's name in life but knows it in torment, begs for warning to be sent to his brothers, and is told they have Moses and the Prophets. The sin was not cruelty but indifference at the gate, and no resurrection will move a heart that would not be moved by Scripture.
sermons.verdict: He stepped over a name.

sermons.title: Zacchaeus: Today Salvation Came to This House
sermons.idea: A chief tax collector, small and rich and hated, climbs a tree to see Jesus pass, and Jesus stops, calls him by name, and invites himself to dinner while the crowd grumbles that he has gone to a sinner's house. Zacchaeus stands and gives half his goods to the poor and restores fourfold what he extorted, and Jesus declares salvation has come to his house because he too is a son of Abraham. Then Luke gives the thesis of the whole Gospel: the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.
sermons.verdict: He came to seek the lost.

sermons.title: The Table and the Garden: This Is My Body, Not My Will
sermons.idea: At the table Jesus takes bread and cup and gives them as his body and blood poured out for the disciples, even as he names the betrayer at the same meal. Then in the garden he falls to the ground and prays that the cup pass, and surrenders his will to the Father's so completely that his sweat falls like blood. The covenant is sealed in a supper and then carried into an agony the sleeping disciples cannot share, where obedience costs everything before a single soldier arrives.
sermons.verdict: Not my will, but yours.

sermons.title: Father, Forgive Them: The Crucified King and the Last-Minute Thief
sermons.idea: Jesus is crucified between two criminals, prays forgiveness over the men driving the nails, and is mocked by rulers, soldiers, and one of the thieves to save himself if he is the Christ. The other criminal, with hours to live and nothing to offer, asks only to be remembered, and Jesus promises him paradise that very day. The King reigns from a cross, saving a guilty man at the last possible moment, and a Gentile centurion is the one who calls him righteous as he dies.
sermons.verdict: Today, paradise for the last thief.

sermons.title: The Road to Emmaus: He Opened the Scriptures
sermons.idea: Two disciples walk away from Jerusalem with their hope buried, and the risen Jesus joins them unrecognized and, beginning with Moses and the Prophets, shows how the whole of Scripture pointed to a suffering and glorified Messiah. Their hearts burn as he speaks, but they know him only in the breaking of bread, after which he vanishes and they run back to the city they had left. The resurrection is not a mood; it is the crucified Christ opening the text and the table to slow, grieving hearts.
sermons.verdict: Slow hearts, the Scriptures opened.

malachi.title: Malachi: The Quarrel of a Faithful God
malachi.headline: Six arguments between a covenant God and a people who have stopped believing He means it
malachi.bigIdea: Malachi is a series of disputes. God makes a claim, the people answer back with a question that is really a complaint, and God presses the case. The book is what happens when worship continues but conviction has died, when the altar still smokes but the heart has gone cold and the offerings have gone cheap. To a postexilic people who said God's love could not be seen and His justice could not be found, the LORD answers that He has not changed, that He keeps covenant when His people will not, and that He is coming Himself to refine, to judge, and to heal.
malachi.christConnection: The Lord whom the people seek comes suddenly to His temple as the messenger of the covenant, and He is Christ, who enters the temple to refine and purify so that an offering can again be brought in righteousness. He is the sun of righteousness who rises with healing in His wings, preceded by the Elijah-figure fulfilled in John the Baptist, turning hearts before the great and dreadful day.

sermons.title: I Have Loved You
sermons.idea: God's electing love for Jacob is the unearned ground of the whole covenant, and the people's question, how have you loved us, exposes a heart that measures love by present comfort rather than by God's settled, history-long choosing.
sermons.verdict: His love precedes your asking.

sermons.title: The Table You Despised
sermons.idea: The priests bring blind, lame, and sick animals to the altar and call the LORD's table contemptible, and God indicts a worship that gives Him what costs nothing, warning the priests who corrupt the covenant of Levi that He would rather the doors be shut than the fire be fed with leftovers.
sermons.verdict: Cheap worship is no worship.

sermons.title: Faithless to the Wife of Your Youth
sermons.idea: The God who made the covenant of marriage stands as witness against the man who breaks faith with the wife of his youth, and the broken vow at home is shown to be of one cloth with the broken vow at the altar, because the LORD hates the violence of a covenant betrayed.
sermons.verdict: He witnessed every broken vow.

sermons.title: The God of Justice Is Coming
sermons.idea: A people weary of waiting say evil prospers and ask where is the God of justice, and God answers that the Lord they seek will come suddenly to His temple as the messenger of the covenant, but they have not reckoned that His justice, when it comes, will refine and judge them first.
sermons.verdict: You asked for what you feared.

sermons.title: Will a Man Rob God
sermons.idea: Because the LORD does not change, His people are not consumed, and the call to return is made concrete in the withheld tithe, where a people robbing God in the storehouse are summoned to test Him and find a God who keeps His promises when they begin to keep theirs.
sermons.verdict: You withheld from the One who gives.

sermons.title: The Sun of Righteousness Will Rise
sermons.idea: God remembers those who feared Him and wrote a book of remembrance even as others called serving Him useless, and He promises a coming day that burns the arrogant like stubble but rises as the sun of righteousness with healing in its wings for those who fear His name, with Elijah sent to turn hearts before the day arrives.
sermons.verdict: The day decides everything.

mark.title: The Servant Who Reigns: An Expository Series Through Mark
mark.headline: From the wilderness baptism to the empty tomb, Mark drives one claim without pause: the Son of God came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
mark.bigIdea: Mark presents Jesus as the Son of God whose authority over sin, sickness, demons, nature, and death is never separated from his cross. The Servant who could command the storm chose to be silenced before his accusers, and the same hands that raised a dead girl were nailed to wood. To know who he is, Mark insists, is to follow him to Jerusalem.
mark.christConnection: Mark builds toward a single confession: Jesus is the Son of God who refuses the path of conquest and takes the path of the cross. He came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many, dying as the rejected stone that becomes the cornerstone and rising on the third day.

sermons.title: The Beginning of the Gospel
sermons.idea: Mark opens with no genealogy and no infancy; he opens with a verdict already rendered: this is the good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who arrives announcing that the kingdom of God has come near and whose authority over demons, disease, and a Sabbath morning is recognized by everyone but the crowds who want only the miracles.
sermons.verdict: The kingdom has come near.

sermons.title: The Authority They Could Not Forgive
sermons.idea: In five running conflicts Jesus claims what only God may claim: he forgives the paralytic's sins, eats with tax collectors, lets his disciples break the fast and the Sabbath, and heals on the Sabbath, until the keepers of the law conclude that authority this absolute must be destroyed, and they begin to plot his death by chapter three.
sermons.verdict: They plotted to destroy him.

sermons.title: Naming the True Family
sermons.idea: Jesus appoints the Twelve and then is charged by the scribes with casting out demons by Satan and by his own family with being out of his mind, and he answers that a kingdom divided cannot stand and that those who do the will of God, not those who share his blood, are his mother and brothers.
sermons.verdict: Doing God's will makes family.

sermons.title: The Word Sown and the Wind Stilled
sermons.idea: The parables explain why the same kingdom-word produces such different soil and why it grows hidden like seed and small like a mustard grain, and then the disciples watch that same authoritative word silence a storm with three syllables, leaving them to ask the question the parables were forcing: who then is this.
sermons.verdict: Even wind and sea obey.

sermons.title: Authority Over What We Cannot Touch
sermons.idea: Across one chapter Jesus frees a man no chains could hold, heals a woman twelve years unclean who only touched his garment, and raises a twelve-year-old girl already mourned as dead, showing that his power reaches the demon-possessed, the ceremonially defiled, and the grave itself without diminishing.
sermons.verdict: Do not fear, only believe.

sermons.title: Who Do You Say I Am
sermons.idea: Twice Jesus feeds thousands from almost nothing, and twice the disciples fail to grasp what the bread reveals, until at Caesarea Philippi Peter finally confesses that Jesus is the Christ, the hinge on which the whole book turns and the moment after which Jesus begins to teach that the Christ must suffer and die.
sermons.verdict: You are the Christ.

sermons.title: Glory on the Mountain, Greatness in the Service
sermons.idea: On the mountain the Father confirms what Peter confessed and commands the disciples to listen to his beloved Son, and then down in the valley Jesus corrects their argument about who is greatest by setting a child before them and declaring that whoever would be first must be last of all and servant of all.
sermons.verdict: First means last and servant.

sermons.title: A Ransom for Many
sermons.idea: The rich man walks away because he will not let go of his wealth, James and John ask for the seats of glory, and Jesus turns both failures into the heart of the chapter and the book: the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.
sermons.verdict: He came to give his life.

sermons.title: The King Enters and the Tenants Are Judged
sermons.idea: Jesus enters Jerusalem as the awaited king, curses the fruitless fig tree, drives out the temple traders, and in the parable of the tenants names himself the rejected stone that becomes the cornerstone, confronting the leaders who hold the temple while missing the One greater than the temple standing before them.
sermons.verdict: The rejected stone becomes cornerstone.

sermons.title: Watch
sermons.idea: Looking at the temple the disciples admire, Jesus foretells its fall and warns that wars, deceivers, and persecution will mark the days before the Son of Man comes on the clouds, and he presses the whole discourse into a single sustained command repeated to the end: stay awake, for no one knows the hour.
sermons.verdict: Stay awake. Keep watch.

sermons.title: The Cross of the Servant King
sermons.idea: Betrayed by one friend and denied by another, Jesus is condemned by the council, mocked, crucified, and at the moment of his death the temple curtain tears and a Roman centurion confesses what Mark announced in his first verse, that this man was the Son of God, dying as the ransom he came to give.
sermons.verdict: Truly this was God's Son.

sermons.title: He Has Risen; He Is Not Here
sermons.idea: The women come to anoint a corpse and find the stone rolled away and a young man announcing that the crucified Jesus has risen and goes before them to Galilee, and Mark ends abruptly on their fear and silence, leaving the reader to do what the women must: believe the word and go.
sermons.verdict: He is going before you.

matthew.title: The King and His Kingdom: An Expository Series Through Matthew
matthew.headline: Matthew wrote to prove that the carpenter from Nazareth is the King Israel waited for, the new Moses on a new mountain, and God with us to the end of the age.
matthew.bigIdea: Jesus is the promised Messianic King who fulfills the Law and the Prophets, gathers a new people through his teaching and his cross, and reigns with all authority over heaven and earth.
matthew.christConnection: Matthew presents Jesus as the long-awaited Son of David and Son of Abraham, the new Moses who ascends the mountain to give the law of the kingdom, and Immanuel, God with us. He is the King whose throne is a cross and whose reign begins at an empty tomb.

sermons.title: The Son of David, the Son of Abraham
sermons.idea: Through a genealogy of sinners and a virgin birth, God keeps every promise made to Abraham and David, and names the child Immanuel, God himself come to be with his people and to save them from their sins.
sermons.verdict: God kept the promise himself.

sermons.title: The Beloved Son Tested in the Wilderness
sermons.idea: John prepares the way and the Father declares Jesus his beloved Son, and the Son who is identified at the Jordan is then driven into the wilderness, where he succeeds with Scripture and obedience exactly where Israel failed.
sermons.verdict: Where Israel fell, the Son stood.

sermons.title: The Kingdom and Its Righteousness
sermons.idea: Jesus announces the kingdom, calls disciples to follow, and on the mountain teaches that the blessed life and a righteousness that exceeds the Pharisees come not from external compliance but from a heart remade by the King.
sermons.verdict: The kingdom begins in the heart.

sermons.title: Two Roads, Two Builders, One Authority
sermons.idea: Jesus closes the Sermon on the Mount by forcing a decision between two gates, two trees, two confessions, and two foundations, teaching that hearing his words without doing them is a house built to fall.
sermons.verdict: Hearing is not yet obeying.

sermons.title: Authority Over Everything That Breaks Us
sermons.idea: In a sweep of miracles Jesus shows authority over disease, demons, storm, sin, and death, and reveals that he came not for the healthy and righteous but as the physician of sinners who scatters the crowds because the harvest has no shepherds.
sermons.verdict: He came for the sick.

sermons.title: Sent as Sheep Among Wolves
sermons.idea: Jesus commissions the twelve to extend his own ministry to Israel, warning that proclaiming the kingdom will cost them family, comfort, and safety, because a servant is not above his master and the one who loses his life for Christ finds it.
sermons.verdict: Following him will cost you.

sermons.title: The Rejected King and the Unforgivable Hardness
sermons.idea: As John doubts, cities refuse to repent, and the Pharisees attribute Jesus' works to Satan, Jesus reveals that the kingdom is hidden from the wise and given to the weary who come to him, and that final hardness against the Spirit cannot be forgiven.
sermons.verdict: Come, all who are weary.

sermons.title: The Secrets of the Kingdom in Parables
sermons.idea: Through the parables of the soils, the wheat and weeds, the mustard seed, the leaven, the treasure, and the net, Jesus teaches that the kingdom comes now in hidden and contested form, grows beyond appearance, and will be sorted only at the end of the age.
sermons.verdict: The kingdom grows hidden, then revealed.

sermons.title: You Are the Christ, and the Cross
sermons.idea: When Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, Jesus blesses the confession and immediately redefines it, teaching that this Messiah must suffer and die, and that to follow him is to take up a cross and lose your life to save it.
sermons.verdict: The Christ is a crucified Christ.

sermons.title: Greatness, Lost Sheep, and the Limit of Forgiveness
sermons.idea: Jesus orders the life of his church around childlike lowliness, relentless pursuit of the straying, honest confrontation of sin, and a forgiveness that has no ceiling, because the servant forgiven an unpayable debt cannot withhold mercy from his brother.
sermons.verdict: Forgive as you were forgiven.

sermons.title: The Cost of the Kingdom and the Last Made First
sermons.idea: On the road to Jerusalem Jesus overturns the world's accounting, marriage, children, wealth, reward, and rank, teaching that the rich young man's grip on possessions cannot enter the kingdom, that grace pays the latecomer the same, and that greatness is to serve and give your life as a ransom.
sermons.verdict: The first will be last.

sermons.title: The King Enters and Indicts His House
sermons.idea: Jesus enters Jerusalem as the humble King, cleanses the temple, and in a series of confrontations and woes exposes the religious leaders as a fruitless fig tree and faithless tenants, pronouncing judgment on a religion of show that has refused the very Son the Father sent.
sermons.verdict: The King judges his own house.

sermons.title: Watch, for the Master Is Coming
sermons.idea: On the Mount of Olives Jesus foretells the fall of the temple and his own return, and through the wise and foolish virgins, the talents, and the sheep and the goats, he commands his servants to stay awake, to invest what they are given, and to be found ready when the King comes to judge.
sermons.verdict: Stay awake. He is coming.

sermons.title: The Crucified and Risen King of All Authority
sermons.idea: Betrayed, abandoned, condemned, and crucified, the King dies as a ransom and the temple curtain tears, and on the third day the risen Christ meets his disciples and claims all authority in heaven and on earth, sending them to make disciples of all nations with the promise that he is with them to the end of the age.
sermons.verdict: He is with us, always.

micah.title: Micah: The God Who Comes Down to Judge and to Pardon
micah.headline: Seven chapters from a country prophet who watched two capitals lie about God and learned what the LORD actually requires.
micah.bigIdea: Micah indicts the covenant people for trading justice for profit and worship for show, announces a judgment that levels both Samaria and Jerusalem, and then promises a ruler from Bethlehem and a God who pardons iniquity rather than retaining His anger forever.
micah.christConnection: The ruler Micah names in chapter 5 comes from Bethlehem, small among the clans of Judah, yet His origins are from of old, from ancient days, and He shepherds in the strength of the LORD. Matthew reads this over the manger, and the church reads it over the cross: the God who comes down to judge is the same God who comes down, in Bethlehem, to be our peace.

sermons.title: The LORD Comes Down
sermons.idea: The LORD steps out of His holy temple and treads the high places of the earth as a witness against His own people, because Samaria's idolatry and Jerusalem's sin are not private failures but the wound that has reached the gate.
sermons.verdict: He treads down our high places.

sermons.title: The Land-Grabbers and the Prophets for Hire
sermons.idea: Those who lie awake devising how to seize fields and houses, and the rulers and prophets who sell verdicts and sermons for a price, have made Zion a slaughterhouse, so the God they presume on will plow Zion as a field.
sermons.verdict: They built Zion with blood.

sermons.title: The Mountain of the LORD
sermons.idea: In the latter days the mountain of the LORD's house will be lifted above the hills and the nations will stream to it, learning His ways until they beat their swords into plowshares, the peace that judgment was always clearing ground for.
sermons.verdict: His mountain will outlast empires.

sermons.title: Out of Bethlehem
sermons.idea: From Bethlehem, too little to be counted among Judah's clans, the LORD will bring out a ruler whose origins are from of old, who will shepherd His flock in the strength of the LORD and Himself be their peace.
sermons.verdict: The small town carries everything.

sermons.title: What the LORD Requires
sermons.idea: When the people ask what offering will buy God off, He answers that He has already shown them what is good: to do justice, to love kindness, and to walk humbly with their God, which no quantity of rams or firstborn can replace.
sermons.verdict: He told you what is good.

sermons.title: Who Is a God Like You
sermons.idea: From the rubble of a society where no one is trustworthy, Micah turns to wait for the God of his salvation, and ends astonished that this God pardons iniquity, does not retain His anger forever, and casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
sermons.verdict: He buries our sin in the sea.

nahum.title: Nahum: The Patience and the Reckoning of God
nahum.headline: Three sermons through Nahum on the comfort of a God who is slow to anger and will not leave the guilty unpunished.
nahum.bigIdea: The same patience that holds back God's wrath is the patience that guarantees its arrival; Nineveh's fall is not cruelty but the refuge of every people the empire has crushed, because the God who is slow to anger does not, in the end, clear the guilty.
nahum.christConnection: Nahum announces a judgment on Nineveh that comfort cannot finally rest in, because Assyria's fall did not end oppression and Babylon rose in its place. The avenging God who is jealous for his people and who breaks the yoke of the empire is the God who, at the cross, takes the reckoning Nineveh deserved into himself for all who trust him. The stronghold for those who take refuge in him is not a city wall but the crucified and risen Lord, the only feet on the mountains that bring lasting peace.

sermons.title: Slow to Anger, and Not Clearing the Guilty
sermons.idea: The God of Nahum is jealous and avenging and slow to anger, and his patience is not the same thing as indifference; the very kindness that has held back his wrath against Assyria for a hundred years is the kindness that will not, at the last, leave the guilty unpunished, so that the storm of his coming is terror to Nineveh and a stronghold to those who take refuge in him.
sermons.verdict: His patience is not your acquittal.

sermons.title: The Fall of Nineveh Announced
sermons.idea: The LORD himself stands behind the armies marching on Nineveh, declaring that he is against the lion's den that filled itself by tearing other nations apart, so that the empire which seemed permanent is undone in a single announced night, and the comfort of the oppressed is precisely that no power built on plunder outlasts the God who says he is against it.
sermons.verdict: The empire was never permanent.

sermons.title: Woe to the Bloody City
sermons.idea: The woe over the bloody city of endless lies and plunder is not a private grudge but the verdict of God on a power that made its wealth by devouring the weak, and every nation that hears of Nineveh's wound claps its hands, because the fall of the oppressor is the relief of the world it had wounded without ceasing.
sermons.verdict: The oppressor's wound heals no one but the oppressed.

nehemiah.title: Rebuilt: Preaching Through Nehemiah
nehemiah.headline: A wall, a book, and a people remade
nehemiah.bigIdea: God restores a covenant people not by spectacle but by burdened prayer, ordinary labor, costly justice, and the public reading of His word, and every restoration exposes how quickly the restored forget.
nehemiah.christConnection: Nehemiah leaves a comfortable post to rebuild a ruined city and gather a scattered people, then watches them break the covenant he sealed. He is the servant who repairs the breach and still cannot finish the human heart. The wall holds; the people do not. The book ends with a man asking God to remember him, because the rebuilding the people needed was deeper than stone. That work waited for the one who would leave a far greater throne, rebuild the temple of His own body, write the law not on a scroll but on the heart, and remember His people not according to their breaking but His own blood.

sermons.title: The Burden Before the Building
sermons.idea: News of Jerusalem's ruin breaks Nehemiah, and his first act is not strategy but weeks of fasting, weeping, and prayer that confesses his own people's sin as his own.
sermons.verdict: Grief that prays before it plans.

sermons.title: The King's Favor and the Midnight Survey
sermons.idea: God moves the heart of a pagan king, and Nehemiah secures provision, then rides the broken walls by night and counts the rubble before he ever calls anyone to build.
sermons.verdict: He measured the ruin first.

sermons.title: A Wall Built by Names You Skip
sermons.idea: The repair is accomplished by priests, perfumers, goldsmiths, daughters, and whole families working each beside his own house, named one by one because God records ordinary labor done in its place.
sermons.verdict: God writes down the obscure.

sermons.title: Mockery, Threat, and a Sword in the Other Hand
sermons.idea: When ridicule hardens into conspiracy, Nehemiah answers by praying and posting a guard, arming the builders so that each worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other.
sermons.verdict: Pray, and set a watch.

sermons.title: The Enemy Inside the Gate
sermons.idea: While the wall rises, the poor are crushed by their own brothers through debt and mortgaged children, and Nehemiah confronts the nobles, demands restitution, and refuses the governor's allowance himself.
sermons.verdict: Injustice undoes what walls protect.

sermons.title: The Wall Finished, the Worker Targeted
sermons.idea: With the breach nearly closed, the opposition shifts from the work to the man through false summons, slander, and a hired prophet urging fear, yet Nehemiah refuses to flee or hide, and the wall is completed in fifty-two days.
sermons.verdict: Finish what fear would abandon.

sermons.title: The Register of a Restored People
sermons.idea: God lays it on Nehemiah to enroll the returned exiles by family, and the long census declares that restoration is not an idea but a named, counted, located people belonging to a place.
sermons.verdict: A people, not a project.

sermons.title: When the Book Is Opened
sermons.idea: The whole assembly gathers and asks for the Law, Ezra reads from dawn to midday while Levites give the sense, and the people first weep under the word, then are sent to feast because the joy of the LORD is their strength.
sermons.verdict: The word read, the people remade.

sermons.title: The Great Confession
sermons.idea: With the word fresh, the people retell their whole history as one long account of God's faithfulness against their fathers' rebellion, naming the sin honestly and standing now as servants in a land whose harvest goes to kings because of it.
sermons.verdict: He kept faith; we broke it.

sermons.title: Names on a Binding Oath
sermons.idea: Confession turns to covenant as leaders, Levites, and people sign and swear specific obligations, mixed marriage, the Sabbath, the tithe, the temple, because repentance that names nothing concrete changes nothing.
sermons.verdict: Repentance signs its own name.

sermons.title: The Cost of Filling the City
sermons.idea: A rebuilt wall encircles an empty city, so lots are cast and a tenth of the people leave their lands to dwell in Jerusalem, with those who volunteer freely blessed, because restoration requires somebody to bear the cost of staying.
sermons.verdict: Someone must inhabit the ruin.

sermons.title: The Dedication of the Wall
sermons.idea: The completed wall is dedicated with two great choirs marching in opposite directions atop it until they meet at the house of God, and the joy of Jerusalem is heard far off because the work was always meant to end in worship.
sermons.verdict: The labor ends in praise.

sermons.title: What the Reforms Could Not Hold
sermons.idea: Returning after an absence, Nehemiah finds the covenant already broken, the temple defiled, the Levites unpaid, the Sabbath sold, foreign marriages resumed, and he cleanses, confronts, and contends, ending with a plea for God to remember him.
sermons.verdict: The heart needs deeper rebuilding.

numbers.title: In the Wilderness: Preaching Through Numbers
numbers.headline: A counted, ordered people who refuse the land that was already theirs
numbers.bigIdea: Numbers is the account of a redeemed people stalled in the desert between the mountain and the land, whose unbelief forfeits a generation and whose God keeps His promise anyway, raising up a second people to inherit what the first refused.
numbers.christConnection: The God who tents among an unclean camp, who provides bread and water and a lifted bronze serpent for the dying, who turns a hired curse into blessing, and who carries a faithless people to a land they did not deserve, is the God who comes finally in Jesus Christ, lifted up so that everyone who looks lives, the true Israel who passed through the wilderness without grumbling and inherited the rest His people forfeited.

sermons.title: A People Counted and Arranged
sermons.idea: God numbers His redeemed for war and arranges every tribe around the tent of His presence, so that order in the camp is worship before it is logistics.
sermons.verdict: He builds His house around Himself.

sermons.title: The Cost of Carrying Holy Things
sermons.idea: The Levites are taken in place of Israel's firstborn and assigned the weight of the tabernacle, because nearness to God is a gift purchased and a burden guarded.
sermons.verdict: Holiness is handled with fear.

sermons.title: A Clean Camp and a Kept People
sermons.idea: Confession, jealousy, the Nazirite vow, and the priestly blessing all serve one end: a holy God dwelling among His people keeps them clean and speaks His name over them.
sermons.verdict: The Lord makes His face shine.

sermons.title: Gifts Brought, Lamps Lit, Levites Given
sermons.idea: The tribes give identical offerings for one dwelling and the lampstand burns before the Lord, because the worship of the redeemed is both costly and deliberately shared.
sermons.verdict: Everything given to the one altar.

sermons.title: Following the Cloud
sermons.idea: Israel keeps Passover and then marches only when the cloud lifts and stops when it settles, because a delivered people lives by the visible leading of God, not its own schedule.
sermons.verdict: They moved when He moved.

sermons.title: The Camp That Craved
sermons.idea: A people fed by heaven weeps for Egypt's meat, and their craving exposes that complaint against the manna is contempt for the God who gives it.
sermons.verdict: Their appetite despised His provision.

sermons.title: When Leaders Resent the Called
sermons.idea: Miriam and Aaron grasp at Moses' authority and learn that God Himself defends His servant, so envy among leaders is rebellion against the One who appointed them.
sermons.verdict: God speaks for whom He chooses.

sermons.title: The Land They Would Not Take
sermons.idea: Israel believes the report of giants over the promise of God and so refuses the good land, and the whole generation is sentenced to die in the desert for unbelief.
sermons.verdict: They forfeited the land by fear.

sermons.title: Grace for the Generation That Failed
sermons.idea: Even under sentence God gives laws for life in the land they will one day enter, distinguishing the sin of weakness from defiant rebellion and binding His people to remember.
sermons.verdict: His promise outlasts their failure.

sermons.title: Korah and the Limits of Ambition
sermons.idea: Korah's company claims a holiness God never gave them and the earth swallows the rebellion, proving that the priesthood is God's appointment and not the congregation's to seize.
sermons.verdict: He alone assigns the priesthood.

sermons.title: Who May Draw Near and Stay Clean
sermons.idea: The priesthood bears the guilt of the sanctuary and the water of cleansing answers the defilement of death, because a people surrounded by dying still needs a way to approach the living God.
sermons.verdict: Atonement guards the road to Him.

sermons.title: The Rock, the Anger, and the Forbidden Land
sermons.idea: Moses strikes the rock in anger and fails to treat God as holy before the people, and even the deliverer is barred from the land, because no leader stands above the holiness he serves.
sermons.verdict: Even Moses does not enter.

sermons.title: Look and Live
sermons.idea: When the serpents bite the grumbling camp, God commands a bronze serpent lifted on a pole so that all who look are healed, making the means of judgment the means of mercy.
sermons.verdict: The dying live by looking up.

sermons.title: The Curse That God Turned to Blessing
sermons.idea: Balak hires Balaam to curse Israel, but God overrules the prophet's mouth so that only blessing comes out, because no hired word can undo what God has spoken over His people.
sermons.verdict: No curse stands against His promise.

sermons.title: The Seduction Balaam Could Not Buy
sermons.idea: Israel, unconquerable by curse, falls to Moab's women and idols, and Phinehas' zeal stays the plague, showing that the enemy outside fails where the appetite inside succeeds.
sermons.verdict: Compromise did what cursing could not.

sermons.title: A Second Census, A Second People
sermons.idea: A new generation is counted for the land their fathers refused, and of the first census only Caleb and Joshua remain, proving that God's purpose survives the burial of the faithless.
sermons.verdict: He raises up another generation.

sermons.title: Inheritance, Succession, and Ordered Worship
sermons.idea: The daughters of Zelophehad secure their inheritance, Joshua is appointed to lead, and the offerings are fixed, because the God who keeps His promise also keeps order in His people.
sermons.verdict: He provides for after Moses.

sermons.title: Appointed Times and Binding Words
sermons.idea: The yearly feasts and the law of vows together teach that the people who belong to God order their calendar and keep their word, for life with Him is governed down to the day and the syllable.
sermons.verdict: What is vowed must be kept.

sermons.title: Judgment on Midian and the Spoils of War
sermons.idea: Israel executes the Lord's vengeance on the Midian that seduced them and dedicates the spoil to God, because the holy war of the camp ends not in plunder but in tribute to the One who gave the victory.
sermons.verdict: The victory is rendered back to God.

sermons.title: The Tribes Who Settled Short of the River
sermons.idea: Reuben and Gad ask for land east of the Jordan and are granted it only on the vow to fight for their brothers, because no tribe inherits rest while the others still go to war.
sermons.verdict: No one rests until all rest.

sermons.title: Every Place They Camped
sermons.idea: The record of forty years of campsites becomes a charge to drive out the nations and take the land, so that the long memory of the wilderness ends in a command to possess the promise.
sermons.verdict: Remember the road, take the land.

sermons.title: Borders, Cities, and the Blood That Defiles the Land
sermons.idea: God draws the boundaries of the inheritance, gives the Levites cities and refuge for the manslayer, and warns that bloodshed pollutes the land where He dwells, because the place of His presence must be kept clean.
sermons.verdict: He will not dwell where blood cries.

sermons.title: Keeping the Inheritance Whole
sermons.idea: The law of the heiresses is settled so that no tribe loses its allotment, ending the book with a promise so secured that even its edges are guarded against loss.
sermons.verdict: What He gives, He keeps secure.

obadiah.title: The Pride of the Heart: Preaching Obadiah Against Edom
obadiah.headline: One chapter, twenty-one verses, where the LORD answers a brother's cruelty and announces a kingdom that will not be Edom's but his own
obadiah.bigIdea: Obadiah declares that the pride which made Edom feel secure on its high rock will bring it down, that the day it stood aloof while its brother Jacob bled is the day God remembered, and that the day of the LORD is coming on all nations until deliverance stands on Mount Zion and the kingdom belongs to the LORD.
obadiah.christConnection: The saviors who go up on Mount Zion to rule the mountain of Esau point beyond themselves to the one Savior whose kingdom cannot be brought down from any height, and the closing word that the kingdom shall be the LORD's is fulfilled in the King who took the place of the abandoned brother and reigns from the true Zion. Where Edom stood aloof from a brother in his calamity, Christ came near to the calamity that was ours.

sermons.title: Though You Soar Like the Eagle
sermons.idea: Edom trusts the height of its rock and the wisdom of its wise men and says in its heart who will bring me down, but the LORD answers that the pride of the heart has deceived it, and from that height he will bring it down lower than thieves who take only what they need.
sermons.verdict: Pride builds the nest God empties.

sermons.title: You Stood Aloof
sermons.idea: The charge against Edom is the violence done to its brother Jacob, not only in the looting and the cut-off survivors but in the standing aloof on the day of distress, for to watch a brother's calamity and do nothing is itself the sin God names and will not forget.
sermons.verdict: To stand aside is to strike.

sermons.title: The Kingdom Shall Be the LORD's
sermons.idea: The day of the LORD is near upon all nations and what Edom did will be done to it, but on Mount Zion there shall be deliverance and the house of Jacob shall possess its inheritance, until saviors go up to rule and the kingdom belongs not to Edom or any nation but to the LORD.
sermons.verdict: The high rock falls; Zion stands.

philemon.title: No Longer a Slave: Paul's Letter to Philemon
philemon.headline: What the gospel costs the man who owns the debt.
philemon.bigIdea: When Christ stands between two people who have every right to hold something against each other, the gospel does not erase the debt. It moves the debt onto someone willing to pay it, and it changes the names by which the offender is known.
philemon.christConnection: When Paul writes 'charge it to my account,' he steps into the gap between an offender and the man he wronged, taking on a debt he never incurred so the guilty one can be received as if he owed nothing. This is the shape of the cross. Christ does not excuse the debt we owe. He assumes it, and he tells the Father to put it on his account.

sermons.title: The Love That Refreshes the Saints
sermons.idea: Before Paul asks Philemon for anything, he names what is already true of him: a love and faith that have given rest to the hearts of God's people, so that the appeal to come will land on a man already formed by grace.
sermons.verdict: Grace prepares the ground first.

sermons.title: No Longer a Slave
sermons.idea: Paul has the authority to command but chooses to appeal, because the gospel turns a runaway slave into a beloved brother, and it asks Philemon to receive Onesimus not by the old category of property but by the new category of family.
sermons.verdict: Receive him as a brother.

sermons.title: Charge It to My Account
sermons.idea: Paul puts himself between the wronged man and the wrongdoer, promising to repay whatever Onesimus owes, and on that ground he is confident Philemon will do even more than asked, because reconciliation is paid for by someone willing to stand in the debtor's place.
sermons.verdict: Put the debt on me.

proverbs.title: The Fear of the LORD: A Series Through Proverbs
proverbs.headline: Wisdom for the Weight of a Tuesday Afternoon
proverbs.bigIdea: Proverbs is not a collection of clever sayings but a sustained argument that the skill of living well begins with the fear of the LORD and is worked out in the body, the tongue, the money, the bed, and the home.
proverbs.christConnection: The Wisdom personified in Proverbs 8, present before creation, delighting in the LORD, calling out in the streets, finds her fulfillment in Christ, who became to us wisdom from God. The fear of the LORD that Proverbs names as the beginning is the same fear that bows before the Son.

sermons.title: The Beginning You Cannot Skip
sermons.idea: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, and every other claim to wisdom that bypasses it is folly dressed in competence.
sermons.verdict: Wisdom starts on its knees.

sermons.title: Two Women Calling From the Street
sermons.idea: Wisdom and Folly both set their tables and call out to the same passersby, and the whole of life is the daily choice of which voice you answer.
sermons.verdict: Two tables. One life. Choose.

sermons.title: The Power of an Inch of Flesh
sermons.idea: The tongue holds the power of death and life, so that careless words wound like a sword and the wise restraint of speech is itself an act of love.
sermons.verdict: Your words are never neutral.

sermons.title: The Gospel According to the Sluggard
sermons.idea: The sluggard is not merely lazy but self-deceived, and Proverbs sends him to the ant to learn that diligence is not optional to a life of wisdom.
sermons.verdict: Poverty arrives like an armed man.

sermons.title: What Your Money Knows About Your Heart
sermons.idea: Money is a revealer, not just a resource, exposing whether you trust the LORD who gives or the wealth that perishes, and generosity is the proof.
sermons.verdict: Honor God with your first.

sermons.title: The Bed and the Whole of You
sermons.idea: Sexual fidelity in Proverbs is not a private rule but the protection of your life, your honor, and your home against a folly that promises pleasure and delivers death.
sermons.verdict: Drink from your own well.

sermons.title: The Friend Who Wounds
sermons.idea: True friendship in Proverbs is not flattery but faithful presence and the willingness to wound, because iron sharpens iron only by contact.
sermons.verdict: Faithful wounds. Deceitful kisses.

sermons.title: The City of the Heart and Its Walls
sermons.idea: Anger reveals what guards or fails to guard the heart, and the one who rules his spirit is stronger than the one who takes a city.
sermons.verdict: The fool vents. The wise rules.

sermons.title: A Woman of Valor
sermons.idea: The Proverbs 31 woman is not an impossible standard but a portrait of wisdom embodied in ordinary labor, ending where the book began, in the fear of the LORD.
sermons.verdict: Charm is deceptive. Fear endures.

psalms.title: The Songs God Gave Us: Preaching the Psalter
psalms.headline: Thirteen sermons through the prayer book of the church, from the two ways to the final hallelujah
psalms.bigIdea: The Psalter is not a random anthology but a shaped book in five movements, teaching the people of God to pray the whole of their lives, obedience and failure, lament and praise, fear and trust, until the songs that begin with one blessed man end with everything that breathes giving praise.
psalms.christConnection: The Psalms were the prayer book of Jesus, who sang them in the upper room and prayed Psalm 22 from the cross. He is the blessed man of Psalm 1 who walked the way of the righteous to the end, the anointed King of Psalm 2 and the Priest-King of Psalm 110, the suffering one of the laments and the risen one whose praise fills the final hallelujahs. To preach the Psalter is to preach Christ praying, suffering, reigning, and leading the redeemed in song.

sermons.title: The Two Ways
sermons.idea: The Psalter opens by setting every reader before two roads, the way of the one who delights in the Lord's instruction and is rooted like a planted tree, and the way of the wicked who are driftless as chaff, and insists there is no third path.
sermons.verdict: Choose the road that ends standing.

sermons.title: The King the Nations Rage Against
sermons.idea: The kings of the earth conspire to throw off the rule of the Lord and his Anointed, but the One enthroned in heaven laughs, installs his King on Zion, and offers the raging nations refuge instead of ruin if they will kiss the Son.
sermons.verdict: Rage ends at the King's feet.

sermons.title: How Long, O Lord
sermons.idea: Lament is permitted prayer; the psalmist hurls his fourfold 'how long' at God's apparent absence, moves from complaint to petition, and then chooses to trust in steadfast love before the circumstances have changed at all.
sermons.verdict: Sing trust before the answer comes.

sermons.title: Forsaken, Then Heard
sermons.idea: The deepest lament in the Psalter cries out of God-forsakenness and the mockery of enemies, yet turns at its center to remembered faithfulness and ends with a congregation that stretches to the ends of the earth, the cry Jesus made his own on the cross.
sermons.verdict: The forsaken cry was finally answered.

sermons.title: The Shepherd in the Valley
sermons.idea: The Lord himself is the shepherd who provides, restores, and walks with his sheep through the valley of deep darkness, so that the presence of God, not the absence of trouble, is the ground of the believer's confidence.
sermons.verdict: Goodness follows you all the way.

sermons.title: Create in Me a Clean Heart
sermons.idea: David's confession after his sin lays the whole guilt bare before God alone, refuses to bargain or excuse, and asks not for relief but for re-creation, a clean heart and a steadfast spirit only God can give.
sermons.verdict: Broken before God is mended.

sermons.title: A Refuge When the Earth Gives Way
sermons.idea: Though the mountains fall into the sea and the nations rage, the city of God is unshaken because God is in her midst, and the command to be still is not a call to calm but a summons to stop striving and know who is exalted.
sermons.verdict: Be still; he is exalted.

sermons.title: Until I Entered the Sanctuary
sermons.idea: The wisdom psalm names the scandal of the prosperous wicked and the bitter envy it breeds, until worship reorders the whole vision, the end of the wicked is seen, and the psalmist finds that having God is the only good he needs.
sermons.verdict: Nearness to God is the good.

sermons.title: Teach Us to Number Our Days
sermons.idea: Moses sets the eternity of God against the brevity and frailty of human life lived under wrath, and prays not to escape mortality but to be given wisdom in it and the steadfast love that establishes the work of fleeting hands.
sermons.verdict: Number your days toward wisdom.

sermons.title: The Priest-King at God's Right Hand
sermons.idea: The Lord seats David's Lord at his right hand to rule amid his enemies and swears him an everlasting priesthood after the order of Melchizedek, joining throne and altar in one figure the New Testament reads as Christ.
sermons.verdict: One man holds throne and altar.

sermons.title: The Word That Holds a Life
sermons.idea: The longest psalm circles a single love, the word of God in its many names, confessing that the law is not a burden but the lamp, the freedom, and the life of the one who is pressed on every side and clings to what God has spoken.
sermons.verdict: His word keeps the pressed soul alive.

sermons.title: Songs for the Road Up
sermons.idea: The Songs of Ascents carry the pilgrim from distress in a far country up to the house of the Lord, teaching a people on the move to lift their eyes for help, to wait for the Lord more than watchmen for morning, and to find unity and rest in Zion.
sermons.verdict: Keep climbing toward the house.

sermons.title: Searched and Known
sermons.idea: God's exhaustive knowledge and inescapable presence are at first overwhelming and then become comfort, the One who knit the psalmist together and hems him in is invited to search his heart and lead him in the everlasting way.
sermons.verdict: You are fully known and held.

sermons.title: Let Everything That Has Breath
sermons.idea: The Psalter closes not with petition but with five unbroken hallelujahs, widening from the individual soul to the whole congregation to all creation, so that the book that began with one blessed man ends with every breathing thing praising the Lord.
sermons.verdict: Every breath ends in praise.

revelation.title: The Unveiling: An Expository Series Through Revelation
revelation.headline: The last word does not belong to the empire. It belongs to the Lamb.
revelation.bigIdea: Revelation is not a code to be cracked but a revelation of Jesus Christ given to a suffering church, unveiling the Lamb who was slain and now reigns, so that the saints might endure. Read in order, the book moves from the risen Lord standing among His lampstands, through the worship of heaven and the judgments that fall on a world in rebellion, to the day when the dwelling of God is with man and every tear is wiped away. Its purpose is not speculation but endurance. It is written so the church can keep its faith when keeping it costs everything.
revelation.christConnection: At the center of every vision stands the Lamb who was slain and is alive forevermore, the only one found worthy to open the scroll because He purchased people for God by His blood. He holds the keys of death, He rides out in righteousness, and He is coming to make all things new.

sermons.title: The Voice Behind You
sermons.idea: Revelation is the unveiling of the glorified Christ, who walks among His churches, holds the keys of death, and addresses His suffering people not from a distance but from their midst.
sermons.verdict: He holds death's keys.

sermons.title: What the Lord Knows About His Church
sermons.idea: The risen Christ examines Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, and Thyatira with eyes like fire, commending faithfulness and confronting compromise, and what He demands is not success but repentance and endurance to the end.
sermons.verdict: He knows your works.

sermons.title: The Door He Stands Behind
sermons.idea: To Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea the Lord exposes the church that is dead while thinking itself alive and the church that is lukewarm while thinking itself rich, and He stands outside knocking, offering everything to those who open.
sermons.verdict: He stands outside, knocking.

sermons.title: The Only One Worthy
sermons.idea: Behind the chaos of history is a throne already occupied, and the sealed scroll of God's purposes is opened by none but the Lamb who was slain, whose worthiness draws every creature into worship.
sermons.verdict: The Lamb alone is worthy.

sermons.title: Who Can Stand
sermons.idea: As the Lamb opens the seals and judgment rides across the earth, the terrified ask who can stand, and the answer is the sealed and uncountable multitude washed white in the blood of the Lamb.
sermons.verdict: The Lamb's people will stand.

sermons.title: The Prayers That Move Heaven
sermons.idea: The trumpets sound warnings of judgment that still leave room for repentance, the church bears witness as God's two faithful witnesses, and the seventh trumpet declares that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord.
sermons.verdict: The kingdom belongs to Him.

sermons.title: The Dragon and the Slain Lamb's People
sermons.idea: The ancient conflict is unveiled as a dragon who failed to devour the child wages war on his people through beastly powers, but the saints conquer not by force but by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony, loving not their lives unto death.
sermons.verdict: They overcame by His blood.

sermons.title: The Song No One Else Can Learn
sermons.idea: Against the mark of the beast stand the redeemed on Mount Zion who bear the Lamb's name and sing a new song, while the harvest of the earth declares that God will gather His own and judge the unrepentant.
sermons.verdict: The Lamb gathers His own.

sermons.title: The Fall of the City That Could Not Last
sermons.idea: The bowls pour out the finished wrath of God, and Babylon, the seductive empire built on blood and luxury and self-worship, falls in a single hour, exposed as the city that always promised permanence and never had it.
sermons.verdict: Babylon falls in an hour.

sermons.title: The Rider on the White Horse
sermons.idea: Heaven erupts in worship at the marriage supper of the Lamb, and the Faithful and True rides out with justice, ending the long reign of deception not with negotiation but with the sword of His word.
sermons.verdict: Faithful and True rides out.

sermons.title: The Books and the Throne
sermons.idea: The dragon's defeat is sealed and the dead, great and small, stand before the great white throne where the books are opened, and the only deliverance is to be found written in the Lamb's book of life.
sermons.verdict: Be written in His book.

sermons.title: All Things New
sermons.idea: The end of the story is not escape from earth but God coming down to dwell with His people in a new heaven and new earth, where the river of life flows, the curse is gone, every tear is wiped away, and the Lamb who promises to come soon says, Behold, I make all things new.
sermons.verdict: Behold, He makes everything new.

romans.title: The Righteousness of God: An Expository Series Through Romans
romans.headline: Paul's gospel, argued from sin to glory, for the church that needs to know what it stands on
romans.bigIdea: In the gospel the righteousness of God is revealed and given to the unrighteous, so that everyone who believes, Jew or Gentile, is justified by faith, freed from sin and death, secured by the Spirit, and remade for a life of obedient love.
romans.christConnection: The righteousness Romans declares is not a quality we manufacture but a gift credited to those joined to Christ by faith, who died our death and was raised for our justification. To be in Christ is to be counted righteous, freed from condemnation, indwelt by his Spirit, and held by a love nothing can sever.

sermons.title: Not Ashamed of the Gospel
