sermons.idea: Paul is set apart for a gospel promised long before it arrived, a gospel that is itself the power of God for the salvation of everyone who believes, because in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith.
sermons.verdict: The gospel itself is the power.

sermons.title: The Wrath Already Revealed
sermons.idea: God's wrath is being revealed against those who suppress the truth they plainly know, exchanging the glory of God for images and being handed over to the desires they chose, so that the Gentile stands without excuse.
sermons.verdict: We knew, and we suppressed it.

sermons.title: Every Mouth Stopped
sermons.idea: The one who judges others condemns himself, for God shows no partiality and the law's possession saves no one; both Jew and Gentile stand under sin, and by works of the law no flesh will be justified.
sermons.verdict: No one is righteous, not one.

sermons.title: But Now a Righteousness From God
sermons.idea: Apart from the law a righteousness of God has now been revealed and given through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe, justifying sinners freely by his blood as a propitiation, so that God is both just and the justifier.
sermons.verdict: Just, and the one who justifies.

sermons.title: Abraham Believed God
sermons.idea: Abraham was justified not by works but by faith credited to him as righteousness before he was circumcised, making him the father of all who believe, who like him trust the God who raises the dead and calls into being what is not.
sermons.verdict: Counted righteous before he worked.

sermons.title: Peace With God in the Second Adam
sermons.idea: Having been justified by faith we have peace with God and stand in grace, for while we were still sinners Christ died for us, and as one man's trespass brought condemnation to all, the one man's obedience brings justification and life.
sermons.verdict: Where sin increased, grace abounded more.

sermons.title: Dead to Sin, Alive to God
sermons.idea: Those baptized into Christ have died with him to sin and been raised to walk in newness of life, so grace is no license; having been set free from sin and made slaves of God, they must present themselves to righteousness.
sermons.verdict: You died. Now live like it.

sermons.title: The War the Law Could Not Win
sermons.idea: The law is holy, but it cannot give life; it exposes sin and stirs it, and the believer feels the war of wanting the good he cannot do and doing the evil he hates, crying for a deliverance the law was never able to provide.
sermons.verdict: Who will deliver me from this body.

sermons.title: No Condemnation, No Separation
sermons.idea: For those in Christ Jesus there is now no condemnation, because the Spirit who raised him gives life and adoption and intercession, working all things for good toward a glory so certain that nothing in all creation can separate us from God's love.
sermons.verdict: Nothing can separate us from him.

sermons.title: Has the Word of God Failed
sermons.idea: Israel's unbelief has not nullified God's promise, for God's purpose stands by his sovereign mercy and not by works; he hardens and shows mercy as he wills, grafting in the Gentiles and keeping a remnant, until all Israel is saved and mercy covers all.
sermons.verdict: Mercy belongs to God alone.

sermons.title: Living Sacrifice, Renewed Mind
sermons.idea: Because of God's mercies the only fitting response is to offer the body as a living sacrifice and be transformed by the renewing of the mind, living out love that is genuine, submitting to governing authorities, and owing nothing except to love.
sermons.verdict: Mercy received becomes a body offered.

sermons.title: Welcome One Another
sermons.idea: The strong and the weak must stop despising and judging one another over disputable things, for each will answer to God; love restrains liberty, the strong bear with the failings of the weak, and Christ who welcomed us is the pattern for welcoming each other.
sermons.verdict: Welcome each other as Christ welcomed you.

ruth.title: Ruth: The Hidden Hand
ruth.headline: Preaching straight through the book of Ruth, where God works in the years that look like nothing.
ruth.bigIdea: Through the loyalty of an ordinary woman and the integrity of an ordinary man, God quietly turns an empty family toward the throne of David, working His covenant kindness when no miracle interrupts the field.
ruth.christConnection: Boaz is the kinsman-redeemer who has both the right and the willingness to buy back what was lost and to take Ruth as his own, restoring a name to the dead and a future to the destitute. He stands at the head of the line that runs to David and to Jesus, the Redeemer who pays the full price for those who had no claim and no hope, gathering the foreigner and the widow into His family.

sermons.title: Emptiness and the Long Road Home
sermons.idea: In the days of the judges a famine drives Elimelech's family out of Bethlehem to Moab, where three funerals leave Naomi with no husband, no sons, and no future, until Ruth binds herself to Naomi's God and the two empty women return to Bethlehem at the start of the barley harvest.
sermons.verdict: Bitter, but not abandoned.

sermons.title: Providence in a Stranger's Field
sermons.idea: Ruth goes out to glean to keep two widows alive and happens upon the field of Boaz, a worthy kinsman who has heard of her loyalty, protects her, feeds her, and blesses her under the wings of the LORD, so that the chance of the field is in fact the kindness of God.
sermons.verdict: No such thing as chance.

sermons.title: The Risk at the Threshing Floor
sermons.idea: On Naomi's plan Ruth comes to Boaz at night on the threshing floor and asks him to spread his garment over her as redeemer, and Boaz, calling her request a greater kindness than the first, honors her, guards her purity, and pledges to settle the matter of redemption at once though a nearer kinsman stands ahead of him.
sermons.verdict: Redemption sought with empty hands.

sermons.title: The Price Paid at the Gate
sermons.idea: At the city gate before the elders Boaz offers the field to the nearer kinsman, who refuses once he learns redemption includes marrying Ruth and raising up the dead man's name, so Boaz publicly takes the field and the widow, paying in full to restore a name that would otherwise vanish from Israel.
sermons.verdict: Love that pays the cost.

sermons.title: From Empty Hands to the House of David
sermons.idea: The LORD gives Ruth a son, the women bless Naomi whose emptiness is now filled by a redeemer and a daughter-in-law worth more than seven sons, and the genealogy reveals that this hidden Moabite widow becomes the great-grandmother of David, the line that carries God's covenant promise.
sermons.verdict: God was writing a king.

song-of-songs.title: The Weight of Belonging: An Exposition of the Song of Songs
song-of-songs.headline: A poem the church has been afraid to read, and the love it refuses to make small
song-of-songs.bigIdea: Covenant love between a man and a woman is sung here without apology, and in its mutual delight, exclusive belonging, and unbreakable strength it bears the shape of the love between God and his people, Christ and his church.
song-of-songs.christConnection: The Song refuses to be embarrassed by desire, and in that refusal it teaches us how God loves. The bridegroom who seeks, the beloved who is sought, the garden enclosed, the seal upon the heart, the love that many waters cannot quench: the New Testament names the church the bride and Christ the bridegroom who gave himself for her. The Song is human love sung at full volume, and it echoes a love that went to a cross and could not be drowned.

sermons.title: The Longing and the Beloved
sermons.idea: Love opens not with achievement but with desire, a woman who knows she is dark and lovely speaking her longing aloud, and the poem honors that desire as good without yet satisfying it.
sermons.verdict: Desire is not the enemy.

sermons.title: The Voice of My Beloved, the King Who Comes
sermons.idea: The beloved comes leaping over mountains, calls her out of winter into spring, and the searching of the night gives way to a wedding procession, where longing becomes the certainty that the one who seeks will not lose what he seeks.
sermons.verdict: He came over the mountains.

sermons.title: Mutual Delight and the Garden Enclosed
sermons.idea: On the wedding night the bridegroom praises his bride head to foot and calls her a garden locked, a spring sealed, and she opens that garden to him alone, so that exclusive covenant belonging is what makes delight whole and not diminished.
sermons.verdict: A garden for one.

sermons.title: When Love Is Lost and Sought Again
sermons.idea: After union comes a night of absence, a door not opened in time, a city that wounds the one who searches, and yet she will not stop seeking, because covenant love is proven not in the ease of having but in the cost of seeking again.
sermons.verdict: She rose and sought him.

sermons.title: I Am My Beloved's and My Beloved Is Mine
sermons.idea: The lovers arrive at the settled language of belonging, a mutual possession spoken without fear, where to be wholly given to another and wholly given over is not loss of self but the place the self was made for.
sermons.verdict: Wholly his, and wholly mine.

sermons.title: Love Strong as Death
sermons.idea: The Song lands on its verdict, that love is strong as death and jealousy fierce as the grave, a fire many waters cannot quench, a seal set upon the heart, and so it tells us what the whole poem has been about, a love that holds when everything else gives way.
sermons.verdict: Many waters cannot quench it.

titus.title: Titus: A People for His Own Possession
titus.headline: Sound doctrine, ordered churches, and grace that does not leave us as it found us
titus.bigIdea: The truth that accords with godliness produces a people whose ordered lives and ready good works make the grace of God visible to a watching world.
titus.christConnection: The grace of God appeared in Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for himself a people of his own possession. He saved us not because of works done by us, but according to his own mercy, by the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit.

sermons.title: Order in the House, Silence to the Liars
sermons.idea: Paul leaves Titus on Crete to appoint qualified elders whose character matches their calling and to silence the deceivers whose empty talk is ruining whole households, because a church without proven leaders is a church without defense against error.
sermons.verdict: Character qualifies. Empty talk must stop.

sermons.title: The Doctrine That Adorns
sermons.idea: Sound doctrine teaches every kind of person, old and young, slave and free, to live in a way that adorns the gospel, because the same grace that saves also trains us to renounce ungodliness and wait for the appearing of our great God and Savior.
sermons.verdict: Grace teaches us to say no.

sermons.title: Saved by Mercy, Ready for Good
sermons.idea: Because he saved us not by our righteousness but by the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, the people he rescued are now to be ready for every good work, gentle toward all, and done with foolish quarrels that profit no one.
sermons.verdict: He saved us. Now be ready.

zechariah.title: Return to Me: An Expository Series Through Zechariah
zechariah.headline: A prophet to a half-built temple and a half-believing people, calling a discouraged remnant back to the God who has not forgotten them
zechariah.bigIdea: God summons a returned but discouraged people back to himself, assures them through visions and signs that he has chosen Jerusalem again, and points beyond the rubble to a coming King who will be struck, pierced, and crowned, and who will reign over all the earth.
zechariah.christConnection: Zechariah's humble King riding on a donkey, the shepherd sold for thirty pieces of silver, and the pierced one over whom the city mourns are fulfilled in Jesus, who entered Jerusalem to die. The fountain opened for sin and uncleanness is his blood, by which the LORD becomes king over all the earth.

sermons.title: Return to Me
sermons.idea: Before any vision or comfort, God's first word to the returned exiles is a call to come back to him, with the warning that their fathers are gone but God's words outlived them all.
sermons.verdict: Your fathers died. His word did not.

sermons.title: The Night Visions
sermons.idea: In a single night God gives Zechariah eight visions that answer the despair of a small remnant: he is jealous for Jerusalem, he will measure it for growth without walls, he restrains the nations, and he is already at work while the world sits quiet.
sermons.verdict: God is not asleep over Jerusalem.

sermons.title: Joshua the High Priest Reclothed
sermons.idea: The high priest stands accused in filthy garments with Satan at his right hand, and God himself silences the accuser and clothes him in clean robes, declaring that priestly standing is given by grace, not earned by the priest.
sermons.verdict: The accuser speaks. God removes him.

sermons.title: Not by Might, Nor by Power
sermons.idea: Facing a temple too large for a remnant too small, Zerubbabel is told the work will be finished not by human strength or resource but by the Spirit of God, who delights to use small beginnings and weak hands.
sermons.verdict: Not by might. By his Spirit.

sermons.title: The Crowning and the Branch
sermons.idea: A crown is set on Joshua the priest and God names the coming Branch who will build the temple and sit as both priest and king on one throne, joining two offices that Israel had always kept apart.
sermons.verdict: One man, both crown and altar.

sermons.title: The Fast That God Wants
sermons.idea: When the people ask whether to keep mourning, God exposes that their fasts were for themselves and calls instead for true justice, mercy, and faithfulness, promising that the days of mourning will become feasts of joy.
sermons.verdict: He wanted justice, not your hunger.

sermons.title: Behold Your King Comes
sermons.idea: Against the war-horses of the nations, God promises a King who comes to Jerusalem righteous and bringing salvation, yet humble and riding on a donkey, who will cut off the weapons of war and speak peace to the nations.
sermons.verdict: The King comes low, on a donkey.

sermons.title: Thirty Pieces of Silver
sermons.idea: Commissioned to shepherd a flock marked for slaughter, the prophet is rejected and paid off with thirty pieces of silver, the price of a slave, thrown to the potter in the house of the LORD, exposing a people who priced their shepherd as worthless.
sermons.verdict: They weighed the Shepherd at slave price.

sermons.title: Whom They Have Pierced
sermons.idea: God pours out a spirit of grace and pleading, and the people look on the one they have pierced and mourn for him as for an only son, and in that day a fountain is opened to cleanse the very sin that pierced him.
sermons.verdict: They look on the one they pierced.

sermons.title: The Fountain for Sin
sermons.idea: An open fountain washes away sin and uncleanness, the idols and false prophets are cut off, the Shepherd is struck and the sheep scattered, and a refined remnant is brought through the fire to call on God's name as his people.
sermons.verdict: Struck Shepherd, scattered sheep, cleansed remnant.

sermons.title: The LORD Will Be King
sermons.idea: On the day the nations gather against Jerusalem, the LORD himself goes out to fight, his feet stand on the Mount of Olives, living waters flow from the city, and he is declared king over all the earth, one LORD with one name, until even the cooking pots are holy.
sermons.verdict: The LORD will be king over all.

zephaniah.title: The Day of the LORD: A Series Through Zephaniah
zephaniah.headline: Three sermons on judgment, the call to seek God, and the love that sings over a rescued people
zephaniah.bigIdea: The day of the LORD comes against every complacency that imagines God is silent, and the only refuge from that day is to seek the LORD in humility, yet beyond the fire stands the God who gathers the remnant, stills their fear, and rejoices over them with singing.
zephaniah.christConnection: The God who promises to come into the midst of his people to save them and to exult over them with singing is the God who took on flesh and dwelt among us, bearing the day of the LORD in his own body on the cross so that the remnant who shelter in him are no longer judged but sung over. In Christ the warrior who saves and the bridegroom who rejoices are one and the same.

sermons.title: The God Who Will Not Be Called Idle
sermons.idea: The day of the LORD falls hardest on those who have settled into their comfort and concluded, in their hearts, that God neither acts for good nor for ill, and that quiet practical atheism, not open rebellion, is what Zephaniah names as the sin God comes to search out with lamps.
sermons.verdict: Complacency is its own indictment.

sermons.title: Seek the LORD Before the Day
sermons.idea: Against the coming day there is one shelter and it is not innocence but humility: to seek the LORD, to seek righteousness, to seek lowliness, gathering before the decree takes effect, the only refuge offered to a guilty people is to turn and seek the God who judges.
sermons.verdict: Seek him while there is time.

sermons.title: He Will Rejoice Over You With Singing
sermons.idea: The same God whose judgment burns through the whole book turns at the end to gather a humble remnant, to take away their punishment and stand in their midst as a warrior who saves, and the astonishing word is that this God is not merely satisfied with them but glad over them, quieting them with his love and rejoicing over them with singing.
sermons.verdict: The Judge becomes the singing God.
